title: What is derived state in a persisted Fabric object?
detail:
The dirty guard's cause (vg-026) is one field of a general question, and patching styles alone leaves the next per-character cache to arrive and be found by the user. SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES is an allowlist that already intends to do this job and is not applied on the way out. The spec should answer which Fabric properties are derived from telemetry or from rendering, how a serialisation excludes all of them, and whether the allowlist should be enforced at the boundary. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-asset-ownership.md. AND NOW THERE IS A SHARP INSTANCE OF IT, MEASURED, which is vg-026. The dirty guard compares a document key against one captured when the editor was built, and with no input at all 13 of the Starter 52 objects change between 0.4 and 1.9 seconds after load — every one a Textbox, repainted by the live preview pass. The document differs from itself with nothing touched, so every New asks the author to save work nobody did. That is what the allowlist was meant to stop and does not reach: the changed objects are bound text, and what the live pass writes is the same property the author edits. This row is therefore not an abstract design question any more — it is one concrete false prompt an author meets on the first Ctrl+N, and the fix belongs here rather than in the dirty guard. AND A SECOND SHARP INSTANCE, MEASURED, is vg-188: entering a group writes `subTargetCheck`/`interactive` on the group, both of which ARE serialized, so `isDirty()` flips with nothing authored and a save taken inside a group would persist editor-only reachability flags into the theme package. That row carries the diff and the Fabric evidence.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user, taken once on this question as it is filed on both vg-041 and vg-188: A SPEC NAMES THE DERIVED SET AND ITS ONE OWNER. Which Fabric properties are derived or editor-only, and how serialisation excludes all of them, is written down as a spec rather than patched instance by instance, so the Textbox repaint measured on this row and the group's subTargetCheck and interactive flags measured on vg-188 are two members of one class with one owner that strips them. Both rows move to that spec. COLLAPSED 2026-10-16 (§8.3). This row and `vg-188` ask one question — which Fabric properties are derived, and how a serialisation excludes them — and one ruling covers the pair. `vg-188` is the *measured instance* of the general question this row poses rather than a second finding: it names `subTargetCheck` and `interactive` reaching the serialized scene through `grouping-manager`'s reachability flags. One ruling, two rows marked; neither closes without the other.

title: Where the defect queue lives: the open-ended pass, the Superpowers lifecycle, and beads
detail: The working-out of whether every defect should become a spec and a plan (overkill), and where an open-ended queue sits beside a change lifecycle that has a finish line. Beads is proven installable natively on Windows (v1.3.0, no WSL) with the full lifecycle exercised; bd init edits AGENTS.md and installs hooks by default and --skip-agents declines that. Marked undecided by the user pending thought — specifically, not wanting two agent frameworks fighting each other. The registry is the incumbent until this is decided. RULED 2026-10-14: KEEP THE REGISTER. It stays the single queue, and the beads evaluation stays recorded as evaluated and declined rather than adopted — the reason is the one this row was marked undecided for, that two agent frameworks would be fighting each other, and `bd init` editing AGENTS.md and installing hooks by default is that fight starting. Nothing is installed and nothing else changes; the row closes with the evaluation on it.

title: Sixteen of the envelope's shapes have no published counterpart, so a key added there is invisible to the schema
detail:
FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-095. The decision note settles that the code owns the key list and the published schema is a hand-written contract held to it by a test - and that arrangement only covers what the schema publishes. Of the 23 shapes KNOWN_KEYS decides, only 7 appear in the schema at all. The other 16, including transform, node, textContent and the four chart settings shapes, live inside Fabric JSON that the schema validates as an opaque jsonValue, and fabric-envelope-schema-sync.test.ts forbids publishing the node tree. So a key added to one of those sixteen is invisible to anything validating against the published schema, which is the whole reason the two registries could disagree in the first place. The sync test catches disagreement where both sides speak; it is silent where only one does. Worth deciding whether that ceiling is accepted - a partially-describing published contract is a reasonable thing to publish, provided nobody reads it as total - or whether the sixteen need some other check. Also noted alongside: serialize.ts KEY_ORDER is a THIRD hand-written list of the same key names. It decides write order rather than membership, so it is not a second owner, but it moves with every key and nothing would notice if it stopped agreeing. AND THE GATE DID NOT CATCH IT WHEN IT HAPPENED, which is worth a line of its own. This row was briefly filed as "vg-vg-1101" — an id built by string-concatenating a formatted id — and backlog-check reported 21 items, all valid, without complaint. So the id check accepts a string that is not an id. That is a small hole in the gate every row depends on, since an id is what closes, what an artefact points at and what a commit trailer names, and it is filed by hand from a script often enough that the mistake is easy to make again.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence: THE PUBLISHED CONTRACT IS A CEILING, AND IT SAYS SO -- no check is added for the other 16. The contract states what it guarantees and names what it does not, which is the shape this drain has already ruled twice (vg-184 for the ownership sweep, vg-380 for the sweeps reverse direction): a claim that reads as verification while being none is the defect, and sixteen speculative checks are not the fix. COST IF WRONG: one of the 16 drifts uncaught, which is a finding about a member rather than about the contract.

title: Two of upstream registry titles disagree with the pairing document they point at, and one seeds the family the other names
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING THE FONT CATALOGUE DEDUPE, and both instances are upstream bugs, not ours - we ship a workaround for the class and this row is the durable record of it. At Fonttrio commit 8af7098ada0b90f076fbfe260244d11b05dd2403 the registry index contradicts its own pairing documents on two pairings out of 379, and in both cases the document is right. FIRST, the index is not one-to-one with its documents: it carries 380 entries for 379 distinct pairing names, because playfair-display-roboto is listed twice. Entry one is titled "Playfair Display Inter - Playfair Display + Inter + Inconsolata", entry two is titled "Playfair Display Roboto - Playfair Display + Roboto + Inconsolata", both carry the same url, and both resolve to one pairing document whose own title and cssVars name Roboto for the body role with an h1 weight of 800. So the index ships a title promising a family the record does not carry. SECOND, and independent of the duplicate: cormorant-garamond-proza-libre is titled "Cormorant Garamond Proza Libre" while its pairing document seeds Proza Libre for the heading, Cormorant Garamond for the body and JetBrains Mono for the mono - two family names run together with no separator and the mono family is absent from the title entirely. Its faces are correct, so the title is the whole defect there, where the first case is a duplicated record rather than a bad name. What made both findable is that nothing throws and the shape is valid: the catalogue is 379 unique ids of three faces each with correct weights and licences, so a count-based check passes. The test now asserts that a trio title ends with the three families it seeds, and it holds for 378 of 379 with this second case as the only exception - named in the test rather than waved through, so a third is red and a fix upstream is red too. Our workaround in docs/decisions/0024 is to treat the pairing document as the authority, keep the registry entry whose title matches it, require exactly one match and throw on none or two - so the duplicate resolves correctly today and a future contradiction stops the run instead of being guessed at. What is left for upstream is to drop the stale Inter entry or retitle it to the Roboto one the document serves, and to give cormorant-garamond-proza-libre a title that names its three families. Both are the same fix request and the same owner, which is why this is one row rather than two. RULED 2026-10-14: KEEP THE WORKAROUND. Decision 0024's rule — the pairing document is the authority, the registry entry whose title matches it is kept, exactly one match is required and none or two throws — stays the permanent answer, and upstream is not asked. The row closes recording that the request was never filed, so a later reader does not read the workaround as a stopgap waiting on a filing.
owner: upstream kapishdima/fonttrio registry.json at commit 8af7098ada0b90f076fbfe260244d11b05dd2403; workaround in src/web/scripts/generate-font-trios.mjs resolvePairings

title: The spec requires visible notch and safe areas, and no task or row owns them
detail: FOUND IN REDESIGN PLAN 2 TASK 2 REVIEW. The redesign spec at section 2 requires "Device frame, notch and safe areas are visible and accounted for, because the display has them." No task in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-04-the-device-lens.md covers the notch or safe areas, the implementing agent declined them correctly as out of its brief, and the gap appears in NO backlog row and carries no "Discovered, not fixed:" trailer on the commit. Under AGENTS.md the trailer is the one path that survives compaction, so as shipped the requirement is simply lost. This is a controller error: the requirement was written into the spec without being given a task or a row. The device frame itself is an outline only and does not mask, which the reviewer confirmed is the honest direction - an author may pan artboard outside the screen and sees more than a device would rather than less. What is missing is the safe-area inset: a theme whose content sits under a notch or a rounded corner looks right in the editor and is cut on the device. That is exactly the preview-disagrees-with-the-phone failure this plan exists to remove, so it belongs with the device lens rather than as an orphan. RULED 2026-10-13: the row LEAVES PHASE 8 and is not built in this drain. It was seated there as a "row with a named single owner and no open ruling" and has neither, which this row's own text says -- the spec requirement was written "without being given a task or a row". THE MEASUREMENT: `DisplayLens` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/display-lens.ts:45-58`) carries exactly three fields -- `id`, `aspect`, `shape` -- and the interface's own comment refuses the fourth thing this would add ("**A shape, never a size.** No resolution... Fixing one here would be the redesign's own failure -- silently settling a second thing nobody asked about"). Building the safe area means settling what a lens's inset is per device and whether it masks or only overlays (the frame is outline-only and does not mask, which the row records a reviewer judged the honest direction). The requirement's EXISTENCE is settled by the spec; its SHAPE is not, and the shape is what the work is -- inventing one is the move this plan has had to undo before. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: this row is the first candidate for the device-lens work that follows the drain, where a spec can settle what a lens's inset is before anything renders it. SEVERITY: the row's own -- a spec requirement stays unbuilt one plan longer, against shipping device geometry nobody chose.

title: A text side handle does not snap at the portrait lens, so an author resizing text gets no guide at all
detail: FOUND BY THE SABOTAGE RUN AGAINST vg-137, and it is NOT a test reading the camera wrong - this one is the product. Set DEFAULT_DISPLAY_LENS to 9:19.5, rebuild, and tests/e2e/snapping.spec.ts "resizing geometry snaps a side handle onto a guide" lands 100.0 scene units from the line it was aimed 3 client px short of. 100 units is a quarter of the 600-tall artboard: that is not a missed snap, it is no snap at all, and at the default lens the same gesture passes. Measured on the same run where every other snapping test passes at both lenses, so the fixture, the gesture and the camera plumbing are all fine. CONFIRMED IT IS NOT THE TOLERANCE: vg-137s derived bound at this lens is 2.92 scene units and the landing is 100, so no tolerance question can be behind it. The gesture arrives as object:resizing on a canonical width rather than as a scale - Fabric gives a text box changeWidth side controls - and that path is the one that does not reach a snap line under this camera. Whether the side-handle resize path consults the camera at all is the thing to check, and it is a one-symbol question in the resizing side of snap-manager, not a test change. VERIFIED PRESENT ONLY AT 9:19.5; NOT VERIFIED ON ANY OTHER LENS, portrait is the one measured, and landscape is the default so the mainline gate is green and does not see it. This is the shape vg-137 fixed the test side of: a lens or a resize that moves the camera changes what the snapping path is asked to do, and this is where it shows. BROWSER PASS TAKEN 2026-10-12 (base 9e5d261e): with DEFAULT_DISPLAY_LENS planted to `9:19.5` and rebuilt, and the PLANT PROVEN LIVE by reading the camera off the preview (zoom 0.2468 x 1672 = 412.6px, a portrait 9:19.5 rect inscribed in the 894px-tall stage), `npx playwright test snapping.spec.ts --grep "resizing geometry snaps a side handle onto a guide" --workers=1` PASSES - 1 expected / 0 unexpected in the run own JSON report - so the 100-unit miss does not reproduce at HEAD and the lens is not the explanation for it. The row stays open: one measurement of a defect against one non-reproduction is not a refutation.
owner: packages/editor/src/snap-manager (the resizing side of the gesture path)

title: A video frame in the host media spec is an intermittent that fails at the baseline too
detail: FOUND WHILE CLOSING DEVICE-LENS PLAN 2 TASK 5, in the full host suite rather than by driving the product. tests/e2e/host-media.spec.ts has a video-frame test that fails intermittently: 3 of 5 samples with the Task 5 commit f49f632b, 1 of 3 at its parent, and it fails at the clean baseline too, so it is NOT a regression from that task and NOT this plan's. MEASURED on both sides rather than assumed, per the repo rule that a single sample is not a measurement. A flaky spec in a suite that gates merges is a real defect whatever its cause, and the cause is not established: video decode timing under a loaded, shared box is the obvious candidate and has not been confirmed. Needs an owner and a determinism fix; the surface to look at is the video-frame readiness wait, not the assertion. SAMPLES TAKEN 2026-10-12 (base 9e5d261e, --workers=1, one suite at a time): `npx playwright test host-media.spec.ts --grep "a playing video background reaches the glass panel over it"` is green in FIVE consecutive runs, 1 expected / 0 unexpected each in its own JSON report. Five samples of one case on one box is not a measurement of an intermittent and does not close it; the row still needs an owner for the readiness wait it names.

title: The artboard panel crop figure lags during a drag, though it catches up on release
detail:
FOUND WHILE CLOSING DEVICE-LENS PLAN 2 TASK 5, then AMENDED by its own task review, which found the controller had filed it too narrowly. ORIGINALLY FILED AS: the panel recomputes its outside-object count only on render(), so the number lags while an object is dragged past the edge - a transient cosmetic lag identified by reading, not by driving. THE REVIEW SHOWS THAT IS NOT THE WHOLE OF IT. The bleed control (selection-inspector/bleed.ts:94) fires object:modified, and its own comment claims the artboard panel is thereby told the scene moved - but the panel has NO canvas subscription at all. sizeNote.textContent is assigned from exactly one place, render() at artboard-panel.ts:336, and render() is called from only three sites in the editor: mount, #setArtboard, and #deletePalette. So ticking the mark leaves the figure reading "1 of 1 objects are now outside" until the author changes the artboard or deletes a palette token. THAT IS NOT A LAG: an explicit author action whose whole purpose is to change the number produces no visible change at all and never catches up, which is the feature being invisible on the surface it is judged on. The two tests that appear to cover the refresh do not - one asserts only that fire was called with object:modified, and its name claims the outcome; the other covers the panel arithmetic by calling panel.render() BY HAND, which is the call the product does not make.  PARTIALLY FIXED BY TASK 5, and the remainder is exactly this row. Task 5 added the subscription that closes the mark case - panel now listens to object:modified and refreshes the note through a single refreshNote writer - and that fires on drag RELEASE, so the figure catches up on mouse-up. THE REMAINDER IS THE DURING-DRAG CASE: Fabric fires object:moving per frame while a drag is in progress and object:modified only on release, and the panel does not subscribe to object:moving. So the figure is stale for the duration of a drag and correct afterwards. NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY: subscribing to object:moving would be a per-frame recompute of a figure that already converges on release, and that is a product call about whether a live figure during a drag is worth a per-frame recompute, not an oversight. This row exists to hold the question open rather than to assert the lag is a defect. FIXTURE if it is taken on: add object:moving to the panel existing subscription array and confirm the figure tracks the drag without a full render - refreshNote was built to be cheap enough for exactly this, which is why the mark case did not have to be.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence: SUBSCRIBE TO object:moving, SO THE FIGURE TRACKS DURING THE DRAG. A figure that only catches up on release is the same defect vg-254 rules on for sliders -- the author cannot see what they are choosing -- and the standard remedy for a high-frequency event is coalescing to the animation frame rather than dropping the event, so the recompute rides the frames the canvas already paints. COST IF WRONG: a per-frame recompute is real work; if it measurably costs the drag its frame budget the answer is a cheaper recompute, not a return to release-only tracking.

title: The host player units spec times out on the real host, and does so in isolation too
detail: FOUND AT THE DEVICE-LENS PLAN 2 BOUNDARY, in the full e2e gate run against a verified-current bundle. tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts, "hosted player over the real host :: shows a temperature in the units this PC chose, converting nothing else" times out at 30s. IT REPRODUCES IN ISOLATION - it was among the six of a prior 16-failure run that still failed when re-run alone - so this is a real defect and not machine load. NOT THIS PLAN'S: device-lens plan 2 touched the artboard clip, the display switch, the new-theme chooser, arc and wedge shapes, and the deliberate-bleed flag, and none of them touches unit formatting or the host player's reading pipeline. MEASURED CONTEXT: the same boundary run was 260 passed / 1 failed / 160 skipped against a pre-plan baseline of 236 / 17, so the suite is otherwise in good shape and this is the last red. The failure is a 30s TIMEOUT rather than a wrong value, which points at a readiness wait on the host stream rather than at the conversion itself - the same shape as vg-141, the host-media video-frame intermittent, and the two may share a cause on this box. Cause not established. Needs an owner: establish whether the host never delivers the reading or the player never repaints on it. BROWSER PASS TAKEN 2026-10-12 (base 9e5d261e): `npx playwright test host-player.spec.ts --grep "shows a temperature in the units this PC chose, converting nothing else"` ran on the real host and PASSED in 5.8s (1 expected / 0 unexpected; the second copy in the report is skipped). The 30s timeout does not reproduce at HEAD. One green sample against a defect that reproduced in isolation is a sample, not a refutation, so the row stays open.

title: The reuse gate is satisfied forever by any older note claiming the same directory
detail:
FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 3, TASK 1. scripts/reuse-gate.mjs answers "has any note in docs/decisions/ ever claimed this path", not "is this change argued for". 0005-chart-glow-is-skipped-pending-an-artboard-unit.md claims src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/charts/ and 0022/0023 claim src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/theme/, so a first write to either returns EXIT=0 before any note about that change exists - measured with printf '{"tool_input":{"file_path":"src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/charts/settings-fields.ts"}}' | node scripts/reuse-gate.mjs. The README calls the check deliberately blunt and presence-only, so that a weak note must be caught in review; this is a different property: the gate is a one-shot latch per directory, so it guards the first change to a boundary and nothing after it. Whether a per-change claim, a staleness rule, or nothing at all is wanted is a design decision, not a fix.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: A NOTE MUST CLAIM THE FILE, NOT THE DIRECTORY. A path claim matches the file being written rather than a directory prefix, so 0005's claim on charts/ stops licensing every later change in it and the gate answers the question it appears to answer. The blunt, presence-only reading stays; what changes is the unit a claim is made in.

title: The rebuild journey's memory-rings test takes 45 to 52 seconds against Playwright's 30 second default, and three of its siblings sit at 27 to 28
detail:
FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 3 TASK 9, running the rebuild spec as its browser gate. MEASURED, and pre-existing: at the previous commit (e37f0b51) the test reaches its vg-145 assertion in 52.1s, and with this task's fix it passes in 45.3s, so the work is real and the budget is simply smaller than it is. THREE SIBLINGS ARE NEAR THE EDGE AT THE SAME TIME, which is what makes this a row rather than one test's business: the wordmark test 27.0s, the GPU card 27.0s and the storage bar 27.9s, against a 30s default that playwright.rebuild.config.ts does not override. A loaded box then turns any of them red for a reason that has nothing to do with the document. FIXED IN PART AND ONLY IN SCOPE: the memory-rings test carries test.slow() (this task had to make it green), and the other three were left as they were, because raising a suite-wide timeout is a decision about this spec's own budget rather than a task-9 edit. WHAT THE ROW IS ASKING FOR: either a project-level timeout in playwright.rebuild.config.ts, or test.slow() on each journey test, chosen deliberately rather than by whichever one goes red next.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: A PROJECT-LEVEL TIMEOUT IN playwright.rebuild.config.ts. One budget covers the whole journey, so the three siblings measured at 27.0-27.9 seconds against a 30-second default stop reddening because the box is loaded; test.slow() on individual tests is not the mechanism, and the memory-rings test's existing call becomes redundant rather than load-bearing once the project budget lands.

title: The json reporter writes to one shared test-results/summary.json unless the run also passes --reporter=json, and a plan that names only the env var never notices
detail:
FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 4 TASK 3, trying to keep this session's report out of the shared test-results/summary.json. THE ROW'S FIRST VERSION OVERSTATED IT AND IS CORRECTED HERE, because the controller reproduced both sides rather than accepting one. Measured, first run (the agent's): PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_NAME=<temp>/probe.json npx playwright test composition-panel --workers=1, with NO --reporter flag - the probe file was never created and test-results/summary.json carried that run. Measured, second run (the controller's, same spec, same machine): the same env var with --reporter=json on the command line - the probe file WAS created, and test-results/summary.json was not written at all. CAUSE, named to the line: src/web/playwright.config.ts:60-65 configures the json reporter as ["json", { outputFile: "test-results/summary.json" }]. A CLI --reporter replaces that list, so the CLI json reporter runs with no outputFile and the environment variable applies; without the flag the config's reporter runs, its own outputFile wins, and the variable has nothing to apply to. So the variable is not inert - it is inert WITHOUT THE FLAG, which is the condition every instruction this repo writes omits. WHAT IT COSTS: test-results/summary.json is one unqualified path, plans 3 and 4 both tell agents to route the JSON through the environment variable and neither says to pass --reporter=json, and on a machine where two sessions run the same suite an agent that obeys without the flag reads a file it did not write and reports another run's numbers as its own. STILL OPEN because the hazard is real once the flag is dropped, and the two candidate fixes are a decision: name --reporter=json in the instruction - cheap, keeps the collision for anyone who forgets - or drop outputFile from the config, which makes the variable apply unconditionally but moves where every session's report lands. The controller has corrected the instruction in plan 4's briefs and in its own session memory; the config is untouched.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: DROP outputFile FROM THE CONFIG. The environment variable then applies unconditionally, so an instruction naming only the variable cannot be obeyed wrongly, and the shared one-path collision ends rather than being documented in every instruction. Every session's report lands where the variable says.

title: Every imported JPEG was placed on the canvas, but only some of them appeared in the layer panel
detail: Reported by the user on 2026-10-07 from hands-on testing, and restated by them the same day after an agent mis-filed it: they imported JPEG images only, not a mix of file types, and every one appeared on the canvas, but only some produced a row in the layer panel. The ones that did not were missing from the panel while present on the canvas. The user does not know whether it has been fixed since. THE CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED, which is why this is a row rather than a fix on the fly. What reading ruled out, each a real mechanism rather than a guess: not isPlaceable (asset-manager/panel.ts:232-236), because every JPEG is kind image and so is placeable; not the storage path, because placeImage (asset-manager/index.ts:60-91) declares and places together and importImage (image-manager/index.ts:105-115) calls canvas.add(image) at the root unconditionally, since placeImage does not set withoutAdding; not the listing filter, because isListed (layer-tree.ts:112) excludes only excludeFromExport objects, namely the artboard plate, the clip and the crop frame, and no import sets that flag; not a row cap or virtualisation, because layer-panel.tsx renders every row and contextRows (:231-240) builds a dimming set rather than a filter; and not a missing trigger, because bridge.ts:124-130 subscribes object:added and object:removed to notify(), which re-projects. Every mechanism readable says the row should appear, which is exactly why a reproduction is needed rather than more reading. What the reproduction has to vary: how many files were imported in one session, whether a group was entered or selected when each import happened, whether files went in one at a time or several quickly, and whether the document already held many objects. Worth noting for whoever takes it: no browser spec covers this path at all, because no case in tests/e2e asserts that a placed image produces a layer row, so nothing would have caught it and nothing will catch a regression. BROWSER PASS TAKEN 2026-10-12 (base 9e5d261e, editor preview on 4174, --workers=1), driving the Add pane file section and comparing the document own image ids against the layer rows ids at every step. THREE VARIATIONS, ALL CLEAN: five JPEGs one at a time on a document already holding 60 objects (5 images, 5 rows, none missing); five picks with NO pause between them (5 images, 5 rows); and three imports with `group-cpu-card` ENTERED (3 images, 20 rows, none missing). A several-files-at-once pick cannot be made at all - the input carries no `multiple` attribute - so that route does not exist. The defect does not reproduce in any variation tried, and no browser spec still covers the path.

title: Three verification bullets plan 4 wrote are not delivered as tests
detail:
FOUND BY THE WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW of the composition-panel plan (`2026-10-06-the-composition-panel.md`), over commits f8197102..af2d3e49, which ran after the plan closed because its workspace held no review diffs while plan 2s held eleven. Three bullets the plan states as verification have no test behind them at af2d3e49. (1) Task 7s browser bullet, "open Document, put the panel at an offset, swap to Assets and back - the offset survives", is not delivered: the new editor-pane-bar.spec.ts case asserts only visibility, and an offset-survival case exists only for the layer list. (2) Task 4s bullet "entering twice names the group once" has no test at all; bridge.dom.test.ts has no twice/once case, while the other four Task 4 bullets are present. (3) Task 8s unit bullet "with a selection ... assert on a group selection" is not unit-tested, because the panel no longer accepts a selection by construction, and is covered only by the composition-panel-document browser case. NOT FIXED ON THE FLY because the three need three different decisions rather than one correction: (1) is a missing proof of a behaviour that may work, (2) may be a bullet the bridges contract no longer carries, and (3) is arguably already discharged by the browser case - so whether the test or the plans wording should change is not the same answer each time. Nothing here contradicts a delivered behaviour: the gaps are in proof, not in product.

RULED 2026-10-12: THREE ANSWERS, because the row is right that these are not one question. (1) The offset-survival case is ADDED for the surfaces the bullet claimed: the behaviour is specified (DESIGN.md §7.7 — preserve per-pane offsets and disclosure state across routine updates), so a proof that exists for the layer list alone is a proof of one surface's luck rather than of the rule. (2) The once/twice case is PROVED as the bridge stands: `bridge.dom.test.ts` carries no such case at all, and an unproved verification bullet is the defect whether or not the behaviour is fine — if reading the bridge's contract shows it no longer carries entering-twice, the plan's bullet is annotated as superseded rather than a test invented for a contract that is gone. (3) The selection bullet is DISCHARGED by the browser case that already covers it, and the plan's bullet is annotated to name where its proof lives, because a unit test is not owed where the panel cannot accept a selection by construction. What settles all three: a bullet is a CLAIM, and a claim is discharged by pointing at its proof or by correcting the claim — never by leaving it standing.

title: An unlanded plan removes the menubars Insert and View menus, and nothing queues it
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5S PLAN AUTHOR and left for the controller by that plans Out of scope section rather than fixed inside it. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-03-editor-left-column-and-header.md is 19.8 KB of unlanded plan whose Task 4 removes the Insert and View menus from the menubar. That removal is one half of the superseded frontend redesign, which ruled those menus leave the header (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-frontend-redesign-design.md:383). AGENTS.md requires that exactly one plan is active and every other incomplete plan is queued, and STATUS.md names no queue entry for this one. It matters now rather than later because plan 5 gives insertGroups() a fourth rendering (the + popover beside the Add pane, the Insert menu and the canvas context menu), and this plan is the one that would take the second of those away. Merging it into plan 5 would be two plans at once, which AGENTS.md forbids, so it is neither executed nor merged here. ITS OWN STATUS IS UNESTABLISHED: whether any of its tasks landed under another plan is not measured, and neither is whether its remaining tasks are still the shape its file describes. The neighbouring bookkeeping defect is vg-152, the same archive-versus-queue rule applied to plans 1 and 2, which are closed but still live in the plans directory. MEASURED IN PART BY PLAN 5S WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW, which is the measurement this row said was missing: the unlanded plans Task 3 is now actively false rather than merely unqueued. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-03-editor-left-column-and-header.md:229 says to create editor-shell/insert-popover.tsx, which plan 5 created at 577c44e5 with a different contract, taking an anchor ref that the older plans Produces does not mention. Worse, that plans verification says to delete insertMenuGroups, insertMenuEntry and the test inserts the same objects from the Insert menu as the Add pane offers (shell-layout.dom.test.tsx:209-216, :286, :843), and plan 5 deliberately keeps and extends all three. So restoring that plan as written would now delete tests that a closed plan made load-bearing. Everything else about that plans state remains unmeasured, and the row stays open. MEASURED BY TASK 9.3 (2026-10-13, base f6e3a705), and the row stays open because the measurement answers only half of it. The Insert half is now false: the Insert menu is gone — redesign plan 2 (`2026-10-08-the-shell-and-the-rail`, archived by this task) trimmed the header, and `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx:1169` now asserts 'has no Insert menu', while the `insertMenuGroups`/`insertMenuEntry` helpers and their tests this row named as load-bearing are themselves gone. The View half stands: `editor-shell/shell-menu-bar.tsx` still renders File, Edit and View, the three View settings inside the View menu, so this plan's Task 4 — moving those beside the canvas and leaving two menus — is unlanded and unqueued. Task 1 (pane bar) and Task 3 (insert popover) landed then were reversed: `pane-bar.tsx` created e0171079, deleted c6ee8d32; `insert-popover.tsx` created 577c44e5, deleted 2eeb4516. Task 2 (scale tokens) landed. Whether the View menu leaves the menubar is a product decision the redesign owns and not this task's to take; the plan file is left in `docs/superpowers/plans/` and `plans/README.md` now names it as the one entry held out of the queue.

title: The spec's primitive list names video, and no object kind can carry one
detail:
FOUND WHILE CLOSING PLAN 5, and left for the controller by that plan's Out of scope section rather than fixed inside it. The spec's §5 primitives bullet sells the Add pane as offering text, shape, chart, image and video "exactly as today" (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-dashboard-authoring-design.md:362-370), but the fifth of those cannot become an object at all: isPlaceable at asset-manager/panel.ts:232-236 is the two-element allowlist image or svg, so an MP4 is declared in the asset manager and never placed, and no Fabric object kind exists for one. A reader who took §5 literally would look for a video button in the Add pane and find none. THE SUBJECT HERE IS THE SPEC SENTENCE, NOT THE ASSET PANEL: the same allowlist is already recorded from the import side by vg-155 (importing a file silently does one of two things, and only the file type decides which) and inside vg-154's extension (a video or a font can never become an object), and neither of those says the spec promises a primitive the product does not deliver. It shares vg-154's fix site; the user's own 2026-10-07 report is vg-156, which is about JPEGs and is unrelated. Plan 5 added no asset button to any surface, because doing so would take vg-154's decision on an agent's hand. The open question is which side is wrong: §5's list corrected to the primitives that exist, or video gaining an object kind, which is vg-154's question.

RULED 2026-10-12: THE DEFECT IS DISCHARGED AND THE PREMISE IS RETIRED. The row was written against the bible, `docs/design/design-language.md`, whose §5 primitive list named video; that file was replaced by `DESIGN.md` on 2026-10-10, and `grep -i video DESIGN.md` returns NOTHING — the current §5 names no video primitive, so there is neither a list to drop from nor a kind to add. The question underneath was already decided by ADR-0008, *Video is background media, not a scene object* (accepted), which is why the replacement never carried the primitive: the product renders video as artboard background media, and a background is not a member of a primitive list. **The row is not closed here**, because closing needs a `check` that names the row's own problem and an ancestor sha, and neither exists for a premise that expired with a file; it closes at the next closure pass, with a check reading this same grep. Until then it stands as a row whose defect does not reproduce — which this repo records as a finding about the ROW, never as a licence to delete it.

title: The settings page's disk dropdown is missing when the suite runs it under load
detail: FOUND AT PLAN 5'S CLOSE-OUT BROAD GATE, in the full browser suite rather than by driving the product. tests/e2e/host-settings.spec.ts:249, 'asks a theme's disk question once, and remembers the answer', failed with locator('select[data-group="system-disk"]') element(s) not found after a 5000 ms timeout, the spec itself taking 23.9 s. IT PASSES ALONE: re-run in isolation on the same rebuilt bundle with --project=desktop-host --workers=1, it is 1 expected / 0 unexpected in 21.4 s. Two samples, opposite outcomes, so the failure is environment- or ordering-sensitive and is NOT a defect this plan caused — plan 5 touched the editor shell, the card library, the layer projection and two docstrings in scene-fabric, and none of those is the settings page or its device enumeration. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED, and the two readings are a real cross-test interference (the desktop-host project shares one host app dir across host-media, host-player and host-settings, and the disk list is read live from the machine) or plain load (the select did not populate inside its 5 s window while the whole suite ran serially). The surface to look at first is what populates [data-group="system-disk"], and whether an earlier spec in the same project mutates the host fixture's directory. BROWSER PASS TAKEN 2026-10-12 (base 9e5d261e): `npx playwright test host-settings --project=desktop-host --workers=1 --grep "asks a theme disk question once, and remembers the answer"` PASSED in 9.5s (1 expected / 0 unexpected). That is the third sample saying the case passes in isolation, which is the green half of the pair the row already records; it is not a measurement of the under-load failure, so the row stays open.

title: A stamp on a nested group is unchecked, because the walk skips every group
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5S WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW, over 5230778c..194f9e5a. Plan 5s Review Focus 1 says a stamp that leaked onto a child is pinned in Task 5 and Task 6. The Task 5 half pins only the non-group children: card-library.test.ts:186 is `if (object["type"] === "Group") continue;`, which skips every group at every depth, so a nested group carrying a stamp is asserted nowhere in the tree. The Task 6 half cannot cover it either: layer-tree.test.ts:836-837 filters `row.kind === "group" && row.depth > 0` and expects length 0, but the starter has no nested group at all, so that assertion is structurally empty and could only fail if a card legitimately gained one. WHAT IS REALLY PINNED, and was proved by the reviews own break: a stamp on a non-group part, the panel and every part inside a card, does fail when removed. The gap is the nested-group half of RF1 and nothing else. NOT FIXED IN PLAN 5 because the honest fix is not another assertion of the same shape: with no nested group in the starter, any such assertion is unfalsifiable, so closing this means deciding to walk the projection against a constructed document that does have one, which is a test-design decision rather than a correction.

RULED 2026-10-12: YES — walk the projection against a CONSTRUCTED document that contains a nested group, and keep the starter out of it. The assertion this row names is structurally empty: `layer-tree.test.ts:836-837` filters `row.kind === "group" && row.depth > 0` and expects length 0, which can only fail if the starter gains a nested group by accident, so it asserts nothing about the stamp rule it sits beside. AGENTS.md's own verification rule decides it — a regression test must fail when its fix is disabled before it is trusted — and an unfalsifiable assertion cannot. Constructed rather than authored into the starter, because the starter is product content and its shape is not a test's to choose. The two halves the review's break proved stay exactly as they are.

title: The pin that the builders words agree with the library is a tautology
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5S WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW. Plan 5s Task 5 Constraints say the task adds a pin that the unit word in the builders and the unit word in CARD_LIBRARY agree, naming the failure mode a unit label re-spelled in the builder instead of read from uiCopy.cardLibrary. The test cannot detect that: CARD_LIBRARY is built from uiCopy.cardLibrary (card-library.ts:105-138, `label: uiCopy.cardLibrary.time` and so on) and the builders pass the same uiCopy.cardLibrary references (new-fabric-theme-cards.ts:99-101, :386, :401). Both sides resolve one object, so the comparison holds for any value that object ever takes and a re-spelled literal in a builder would have to be introduced on the library side too to go unnoticed, which is not the failure mode. What the test does pin is real and was proved by a break: the stamp present at all, and its widgetId. The precedent the plan cited is no stronger: new-object-defaults.test.ts:626 reads uiCopy.shapeKinds on both sides as well. The cross-path agreement that IS sound is the one Task 6 added, layer-tree.test.ts:820-834, which compares a revived document against CARD_LIBRARY. NOT FIXED HERE because closing it means asserting on the builders source rather than on a value, which is a shape assertion and a decision about how much source-reading this suite wants, not a correction to a wrong test.

RULED 2026-10-12: REMOVE the tautology and do NOT replace it with a source-shape assertion. `uiCopy.cardLibrary` compared against `new-fabric-theme-cards.ts:99-101` resolves one object on both sides, so the comparison holds for every value that object could ever take: it cannot fail for the reason it claims to check, which makes it evidence of nothing — the same defect as vg-167. Source-reading is rejected as the replacement: this suite's business is behaviour, and an assertion over a builder's spelling pins the text of a file rather than what the product does. Keep the two assertions the break proved real — the stamp is present at all, and its widgetId — and leave `layer-tree.test.ts:820-834`, the cross-path comparison Task 6 added, as the one that covers agreement.

title: lanAddress() returns the first non-internal IPv4 with no preference for a physical adapter, so the header can name an address no phone can reach
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 6'S TASK 1.3, which was told to file it and instead left a Discovered, not fixed trailer, because its dispatch forbade writing the register. src/web/packages/host/src/cli/net.ts:90-100 iterates os.networkInterfaces() and returns the first non-internal IPv4. A laptop that also carries a Hyper-V virtual switch, a WSL adapter, a Docker bridge or a VPN routinely enumerates one of those first, so GET /api/hosting hands the editor header an address no phone on the Wi-Fi can reach, and the QR encodes it. Nothing on this machine shows the mistake -- the header renders a plausible dotted quad and the failure appears only on the phone that cannot connect. That address is the header's entire payload, so this is a correctness defect and not a cosmetic one. Not fixed there: the fix needs a decision that task did not own -- which interface wins, how to rank them, and what to do when three are plausible -- and it belongs to lanAddress()'s owner rather than to the route that reads it. Reproduction: run the host on a machine with any virtual adapter present and compare the address printed after Phones on this Wi-Fi with the physical adapter's own.

RULED 2026-10-12: THE DEFAULT-ROUTE INTERFACE WINS, and the ranking is data beside `lanAddress()`'s owner (`host/src/cli/net.ts:90-100`, which today returns the first non-internal IPv4 and therefore whatever the OS enumerates first). The rule, in order: drop loopback, link-local and internal candidates; drop interfaces whose name matches a virtual-adapter pattern (Hyper-V and `vEthernet`, WSL, Docker and `br-`, VirtualBox, VMware, and the tunnel adapters a VPN installs), because those are exactly the ones a phone cannot reach; among what remains prefer the interface carrying the default IPv4 route, since that is the address the phone's own traffic leaves by. When two candidates survive and neither carries the route, the host keeps its choice DETERMINISTIC (lowest interface index) and logs the alternatives rather than silently guessing — the failure this row describes is invisible on the machine that makes it, so the alternatives being on the record is what makes a wrong pick findable without a phone. The pattern list is data, owned beside the function, so a new virtual adapter is a one-line addition rather than a new heuristic.

title: A GET that arrives while a LAN move is in flight waits for a move that is waiting for it, and the host never listens again
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 6'S TASK 3.4, which reasoned it, could not reproduce it, and left it unfiled because its cause was not established; filed here because the consequence is a permanently dead host rather than a slow answer. The mechanism, read from the code rather than observed: server.ts:770 has the GET await binding?.idle(); cli/hosting.ts:86 has the move await server.close(), which does not complete until every existing connection ends. A GET whose handler is parked on idle() is one of those connections and will not end until it answers, so the move never finishes, bind(next) never runs, and the server never listens again -- every editor and every display on that host is dead until the process is restarted. It is NOT a slow editor re-read, which is how it was first described. That is the whole reason it is worth a row. Reachability is narrow and the narrowness is the honest part: `finish` -> setLan -> server.close() runs in one synchronous run with no await between them, so no connection can be ACCEPTED in that window, and closeIdleConnections() has already taken the idle keep-alive sockets. What remains is a request already sitting on an accepted connection when close() is called -- a second editor tab, a display reconnecting, anything issued concurrently with the PUT rather than after it. Ordinary single-client use cannot reach it, which is why no reproduction was found. The fix is a design decision between two hazards, and they are not symmetric: the move could destroy connections instead of waiting on them -- closeAllConnections() is now safe precisely BECAUSE the answer is already flushed, which is what Task 3.4's Step 5 accidentally proved when putting it back did not break anything -- at the cost of an empty reply to whichever request was unlucky, which the editor's bounded re-read already tolerates; or the GET could bound its wait and answer from state(), at the cost of answering before the move settles. The first is the smaller change and the failure it trades for is bounded; somebody should still choose rather than inherit.

RULED 2026-10-12: THE MOVE MUST NOT WAIT ON A REQUEST: destroy the remaining connections rather than letting `server.close` wait for them. As written, `move()` calls `closeIdleConnections()` and then `server.close(cb)` (`host/src/cli/hosting.ts:85-86`), and close waits for ACTIVE connections — so a GET arriving during the move blocks the callback, the move blocks the GET, and the host never listens again. That is a deadlock reachable by any second client, not a race, and a deadlock is not a hazard to be weighed against an empty reply. The trade is the one `vg-173` already measured and the editor already tolerates: whichever request was unlucky gets an empty reply, and its bounded re-read recovers. The other branch is rejected on the repo own rule rather than on taste — answering from `state()` before the move settles would have the host assert something it knows to be stale, which is the fabrication this product forbids everywhere else.

title: Neither THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md nor docs/engineering/dependencies.md states whether its rows are direct dependencies only or the installed closure, and the licence obligation this row filed was discharged by ADR-0038 removing the dependency
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 7'S AUTHORING PASS at the reuse gate's rung 2, and verified here against the package metadata rather than taken from the agent's report. `src/web/packages/editor/package.json:16` declares `"@radix-ui/react-popover": "^1.1.23"`, and `grep -ci radix THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` is 0 and the same reading holds for docs/engineering/dependencies.md -- neither file has ever carried a Radix row, although the popover has been a direct dependency since the colour picker landed (vg-031, which recorded the cost of a second headless library in view when the user ruled for it). AGENTS.md makes the duty explicit -- 'Before adding a shipped dependency, verify its licence from package metadata and update THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and docs/engineering/dependencies.md' -- so this is a missed obligation rather than an unstated one. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED ON THE FLY: the fix needs a scope decision, not a licence lookup. Nineteen Radix packages are installed for the popover's closure, and whether these two files list DIRECT dependencies only or the installed closure is a policy neither file currently states; writing 19 rows where the convention is 1 would be inventing a rule. That question is about to become load-bearing rather than academic, because section 8 rules Radix the single primitive library and plan 7 adds `@radix-ui/react-dialog` on top -- plan 7's Task 3.1 carries the licence row for the new dependency, and it will set the convention the popover row then follows. NOTHING FAILS AT RUNTIME and no test can redden on this: it is a compliance and provenance gap, which is why it has survived four plans.

RULED 2026-10-12: THE OBLIGATION THIS ROW FILED IS DISCHARGED, and by removal rather than by a row: `grep -rn radix` over every `package.json` in the workspace returns nothing, because ADR-0038 took the popover and its eighteen siblings out of the manifest on the user's ruling. So the repo no longer ships the unrecorded licence obligation this row measured — and the row is NOT closed on that, because what survives is the real question under it: **neither provenance file states whether its rows are direct dependencies only or the installed closure**, which is a policy question a false premise was hiding. The title is corrected to that question, and the body's premise is left as it was written so the correction is legible. What would close it: the convention declared in the file that owns it, applied to whichever dependency ships next — the risk has not gone with the dependency, because the next shipped package arrives with the same unstated rule.

title: the ownership sweep cannot see an exported id vocabulary spelled as a type union or a dot-separated id, though ownership.md claims it finds every one
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 2.2 OF PLAN 7 while adjudicating a hit the plan told it to expect and the sweep never produced. Verified here at the source, not taken from the report. THE CONTRACT IT BREAKS: `docs/architecture/ownership.md:22-23` says the sweep "finds every module exporting an id vocabulary and reports any other module re-spelling two or more of those ids" -- unqualified. `shortcut-manager/index.ts:2-21` exports exactly that: `ProductShortcutId`, a nineteen-member id vocabulary, with `PRODUCT_SHORTCUTS` the table that binds it. Task 2.2 put eight of those ids into `object-actions.ts`, and `npm run ownership:sweep` exits 0 naming neither module. BOTH HALVES OF THE MECHANISM MISS IT, and they miss for different reasons. `discriminatorsIn` (`scripts/ownership-sweep.mjs:84`) matches `"([a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+)"` -- the `(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+` group requires **at least one hyphen**, so `"edit.duplicate"` is never a candidate at all. `exportedVocabularies` (`:91-101`) parses two shapes only: `const NAME = [ ... ]` with three or more quoted ids, and `Readonly<Record<string, ...>>` records. `ProductShortcutId` is a `type` union, so it is never seen as anyone vocabulary. A vocabulary that is a union *and* dotted is invisible twice over. THE SWEEP IS NOT BROKEN, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS PRECISE: the same run finds two genuine collisions -- `packages/host/src/settings/devices.ts` against `main.ts` and against `server.ts`, sharing `system-disk` and `data-disk`. So the mechanism works; it is blind to one shape, not failing generally. WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY COVERED: `ownership.md:122-123` records a blindness, and it is a *different* one -- the seven object-creation sites "each inline a string literal" and so export no vocabulary at all. That is a module with no vocabulary. This is a module with a vocabulary the sweep cannot read, and the doc gives no sign of knowing that shape exists. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: it is a verification gate, so widening it is a decision about precision against recall, not a bug fix. Dropping the hyphen requirement would make every dotted string in the tree a candidate discriminator and flood the report -- and `ownership.md:48` already carries the hard-won lesson that a gate flagging most of the tree gets ignored, which is why the count floor exists. Accepting type unions means writing a third parser for a syntax the sweep currently reads as data. Neither has an obvious regression test. Consequence for the plan that found it: Task 2.2s constraint told the executor the sweep would report this change and required it to adjudicate the hit as a consumer. There was no hit. The plan asserted a gate watched something the gate cannot see, which is worse than the gate being absent -- it reads as verification and is not.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: DO NOT WIDEN -- CORRECT THE CLAIM. The defect is the claim rather than the coverage: ownership.md says the sweep finds every exported id vocabulary when it cannot see a type union or a dotted id, and that reads as verification while being none. The doc states the boundary instead, because a gate widened to flag most of the tree is ignored, which ownership.md:48 already records as the hard-won lesson.

title: Entering a group marks the document unsaved, because the grouping manager's reachability flags reach the serialized scene
detail:
FOUND BY THE ROOT WHILE PLACING TASK 4.1 OF PLAN 7's second capture, from an `Unsaved changes` mark in the footer that the task's first capture does not have. Pre-existing and not plan 7's: `grouping-manager` predates the plan and plan 7 does not touch it. THE MEASUREMENT, TAKEN IN THE BROWSER AND PROBED STEP BY STEP: reading `.editor-shell-save-state[data-dirty]` after each act gives after-load `false`, after-enterLayer `true`, and `true` for every act after it (selecting a part, pressing `?`, `Delete`, `Control+z`, `Escape`). So the keypresses behind the sheet change nothing -- the deferral being proved -- and entering the group is what flips the marker. THE CAUSE IS MEASURED, not inferred: diffing `canvas.toJSON()` across `enterLayer` gives 8 changed paths, `objects[3].subTargetCheck`, `objects[3].interactive`, and `objects[4|5|6|8|9].objects`. Both of the first two are set by `makeSelectableThrough` (`grouping-manager/index.ts:92-97`) and **both are serialized by Fabric**. THE COMMENT THAT SAYS OTHERWISE IS NARROWER THAN THE CODE: `grouping-manager/index.ts:75-78` claims '`selectable`/`evented` are not in Fabric's `stateProperties`, so this never reaches a save', and at `:111-119` 'neither key is in Fabric's `stateProperties`, so it stays view state (SS67)'. The `stateProperties` claim is TRUE -- verified against `node_modules/fabric/dist/index.mjs`, whose `stateProperties` list is top/left/scaleX/scaleY/flipX/flipY/originX/originY/angle/opacity/globalCompositeOperation/shadow/visible/skewX/skewY, with neither key in it. But the comment reasons only about `applyReachability`, which sets `selectable`/`evented`; **`makeSelectableThrough` sets two different keys, `subTargetCheck` and `interactive`, and the comment never covers them.** So the guard the comment believes it has does not exist for those two. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE MARKER: if the author saves while inside a group, the reachability flags this manager set are written into the theme package, which is the same class as `vg-129`/`vg-130` -- editor-only state reaching a shareable artifact -- and SS67 says view state is never authored history and never a Fabric write. The six changed `objects` arrays are measured but NOT explained: the cause of those is not established, and they may be a consequence of the same flag write or something else in the path. THE FIX NEEDS A DECISION AND IS NOT TAKEN HERE: it is the general question `vg-041` owns -- which Fabric properties are derived or editor-only, and how serialisation excludes them -- and `vg-026` is that row's other measured instance, a text object repainted by the live pass. Filed as its own row rather than folded into `vg-041` because that is the pattern this register already uses for `vg-026`: the instance is independently fixable and independently verifiable, and the general row points at it.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user, taken once on this question as it is filed on both vg-041 and vg-188: A SPEC NAMES THE DERIVED SET AND ITS ONE OWNER. Which Fabric properties are derived or editor-only, and how serialisation excludes all of them, is written down as a spec rather than patched instance by instance, so the Textbox repaint measured on this row and the group's subTargetCheck and interactive flags measured on vg-188 are two members of one class with one owner that strips them. Both rows move to that spec.

RE-MEASURED 2026-10-15, WHILE PROVING `vg-023`'s ROUND TRIP. **One half of this row is stale and the other half stands, and they are two different key pairs.** The half this row measured — `subTargetCheck`/`interactive`, armed by `makeSelectableThrough` — is **no longer a leak**: `scene-fabric`'s `persist.ts` now strips both after serialization through `removeGroupEntryFlags`, and its own docblock says so, naming exactly this case. The half that survives is the pair `applyReachability` writes, `selectable`/`evented`, because `SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES` lists both by name (`persist.ts`, the constant read directly rather than inferred) alongside `locked`. So an author who saves while inside a group still writes editor-only reachability into the package, which is this row's subject and `vg-041`'s class. **THE COMMENT THAT MISLEADS IS STILL STANDING, and this is the part worth acting on: `grouping-manager/index.ts`'s `applyReachability` docblock justifies the write with "neither key is in Fabric's `stateProperties`, so it stays view state". That sentence is true and reasons about the wrong list.** `stateProperties` governs Fabric's default `toObject`; this project serialises through `canvas.toObject([...SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES])`, which adds both keys back explicitly — so the guard the comment believes it has does not exist. Task 12.4f edited that same docblock (it added the dim's paragraph) and left the false sentence in place, correctly declining to fix it: the ruling below makes the derived set a spec's business, so correcting one instance here would pre-empt the owner. The next reader of this row should read the comment as the instance of the defect rather than as its refutation. COLLAPSED 2026-10-16 (§8.3). This row is the measured instance of the question `vg-041` poses — which Fabric properties are derived from rendering, and whether the allowlist is enforced at the serialisation boundary — so one ruling covers the pair and it is recorded on `vg-041`. Marked rather than re-asked; neither row closes without the other.

title: No e2e fixture raises a data gap and a composition gap together, so the pair section 97 describes is measured as two transport-side strips instead
detail:
FOUND BY THE ROOT ON 2026-10-08, correcting plan 8 Task 2.3 before dispatching it, while checking whether the theme its ceiling test uses could actually raise the two strips the test's own comment named. THE MEASUREMENT, read from the seeded packages rather than assumed: `.e2e-host-app/themes/e2e-missing-sensor/theme.json` has artboard `{width:640,height:360,contentFit:contain}` and ONE object, a `Textbox` at `40,140` sized `420x60` -- entirely inside the artboard. `.e2e-host-app/themes/e2e-hosted/theme.json` has the same 640x360 artboard and four objects, the lowest a `Textbox` at `40,300` sized `420x60`, whose bottom edge is exactly 360. Neither bleeds, so neither raises `#vigilia-crop`, and `showCropNotice` (`packages/player/src/chrome.ts:121`) is the only writer of that strip. THE PAIR THAT DOES NOT EXIST: a theme that both bleeds and binds a key no provider reports. The bleed fixtures (`HOST_BLEED_THEME_ID`, `HOST_BLEED_ALL_THEME_ID`, `e2e-bleed-*`) bind real keys, so they raise a composition gap and no data gap; the missing-sensor fixture binds an unreportable key and raises a data gap and no composition gap. SECTION 97's rationale -- that an unreadable sensor and a cropped object must be legible as different things, which is why two strips may be on screen at once -- is therefore not exercised as a pair by any browser test. WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT IN THE PLAN RATHER THAN HERE: Task 2.3's second test keeps its two-strip assertion, because the chrome ceiling is about total chrome height and not about which notices make it up, and its comment now says the pair is a data gap beside a TRANSPORT gap (`#vigilia-connection`, drawn because the test aborts `**/ws`) instead of claiming a composition gap. Filed rather than fixed because closing it means adding a fixture to `tests/e2e/host-theme.ts` that is both bleeding and missing-sensored, which is a decision about fixture inventory rather than a change to the code under test.

RULED 2026-10-12: ADD the fixture — one document that both bleeds and binds a key the host cannot report. §97's rationale is that an unreadable sensor and a cropped object must be legible as DIFFERENT things, which is why two strips may be on screen at once, and no browser test exercises that pair today: Task 2.3's two-strip assertion passes with a transport gap standing in for the composition gap, which is a different pair. Fixture inventory is the test suite's own decision and this is the entry it is missing, against a requirement that already exists rather than a new one. It is a change to the evidence and not to the code under test, which is why the row was filed rather than fixed.

title: No tsconfig includes tests/e2e, so a type error in any browser spec is checked by nothing
detail:
FOUND BY THE ROOT ON 2026-10-08 while running plan 8 Task 2.3's gates on a new spec file (`src/web/tests/e2e/host-chrome.spec.ts`, commit 1e52b8da), and it is repo-wide rather than this task's. THE MEASUREMENT, read from the configuration rather than assumed: `cd src/web && npm run typecheck` runs `npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present`, and `package.json`'s workspaces are `packages/renderer-core`, `packages/theme-package`, `packages/scene-fabric`, `packages/player`, `packages/editor`, `packages/fake-source` and `packages/host` -- `tests/` is not among them, so no workspace tsc program can see it. There is no `src/web/tsconfig.json` and no `tests/tsconfig.json` (`ls tsconfig*.json tests/tsconfig*.json` finds only `tsconfig.base.json`). Of the seven package tsconfigs, `renderer-core` includes `src/**/*.ts` and `theme-package` includes `src/**/*.ts`; the other five carry no `include` at all and fall back to TypeScript's default, which is `**/*` relative to the config's own directory -- so every one of them is scoped inside its own package. The one config that mentions tests, `packages/editor/tsconfig.json`, mentions them in a comment about `src/core`'s architecture tests and includes only `src/**/*.ts` and `src/**/*.tsx`. WHAT STILL RUNS: `./node_modules/.bin/biome lint tests/...` checks syntax and style but is not a type checker, and Playwright transpiles specs with esbuild, which strips types without checking them -- so a spec that reads a property which does not exist on a fixture, or passes the wrong shape to a helper, fails only at runtime and only in the branch that reads it. NOT A REGRESSION AND NOT BLOCKING: this is the state every existing browser spec has always been in, and it cost nothing in this task because the new file's helpers are copies of a spec that runs. It is filed because the absence is invisible -- a green `npm run typecheck` reads as coverage of the whole workspace, and it is not -- and because the fix is a decision rather than a one-liner: adding `tests/` to a program pulls `@playwright/test` and both DOM and Node libs into one project, which is the conflict the editor's tsconfig already documents for `@types/node`. NOW LOAD-BEARING (2026-10-09, plan 3's close): plan 3 rewrote three tests/e2e/ specs (author-journey-rebuild, inspector-sections and editor-canvas) and added four parity captures, and none of that is typechecked by any tsconfig - which the close's own reviews kept re-learning, since the standing trap 'tests/e2e/ belongs to no tsconfig' had to be stated in briefs to stop a mis-typed locator passing review. The risk is no longer theoretical.

RULED 2026-10-12: YES — `tests/e2e/` joins a tsconfig program, as its OWN project rather than by folding into the editor's. The absence is invisible and now load-bearing: plan 3 rewrote three specs and added four parity captures with no typechecker anywhere, and briefs had to carry a standing warning so a mis-typed locator would not pass review — an error class that only review catches is the state `npm run typecheck` exists to prevent. Its own `tsconfig.e2e.json` rather than a shared program, because the DOM/Node lib conflict is exactly what TypeScript solves by separating projects: the e2e project needs Playwright's types and the DOM, and pulling those into the editor's program would trade one missing check for a weaker one. Wire it into the typecheck script in the same commit, or the project exists and nothing runs it.

title: A theme install that loses the staging rename to EPERM fails a spec outright, and the cascade reads as unrelated defects
detail: FOUND AT PLAN 9 PHASE 1'S BOUNDARY, where it was the single largest reason a full browser-suite run was unreadable. THE MECHANISM: the e2e host installs a fixture by writing into `.e2e-host-app/themes/.staging-<random>.<fixture>` and renaming it onto the fixture's own directory. Under parallel load that rename intermittently loses with `EPERM: operation not permitted` on Windows, and the spec fails at the install: `the host accepted the fixture: EPERM: operation not permitted, rename '...\.staging-muzerquni8dhlraixl.e2e-clip-parity' -> '...\.e2e-host-app	hemes\e2e-clip-parity'`. WHAT MAKES IT WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A SHRUG IS THE BLAST RADIUS, not the race. In one full-suite run that failure accounted for 17 of 21 unexpected results without appearing 17 times: every spec whose fixture did not install then fails somewhere else - five on a missing object (`no object with id authoring`, `no object with id mover`, `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'groupContext')`), three on `#status` never reaching the text the spec waits for - so ONE filesystem race presented as five unrelated defect classes across glass, clip, snapping and appearance specs. That is precisely the shape that gets misattributed to whatever diff happens to be in the tree, and it very nearly was here. THE SAMPLE THAT CLASSIFIES IT: re-running the same spec set with the box quiet left 4 unexpected, and `clip-parity` run entirely alone is 2 expected / 0 unexpected. So it is load- or handle-dependent and NOT a standing red; the remaining 4 were `vg-151` (known open) and `vg-196` (filed separately). The staging directory is left clean - no `.staging-*` survived either run - so nothing is wedged between runs. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the handle belongs to the host's own file watcher on the themes directory, to an indexer or scanner on this box, or to a previous run's host process that had not fully exited is not measured, and no other session's Chromium is implicated because none was on the box for the classifying run. THE FIX IS PROBABLY SMALL AND IS NOT TAKEN HERE: a bounded retry around the rename is the obvious repair, since the staging directory is the host's own and a lost race currently fails the spec outright with no attempt to recover. Worth pairing with whatever owns `themes/store.ts`'s install path, because `vg-174`'s LAN move work is in the same neighbourhood. RUN TAKEN 2026-10-12 (base 9e5d261e, --workers=1): `npx playwright test clip-parity --workers=1` is 2 expected / 0 unexpected / 2 skipped, no EPERM and no `.staging-*` left behind - the same quiet-box reading the row already records, so it adds nothing to it. The bounded retry the row names as the repair was NOT implemented: the row own cause is unestablished (the handle holder is not measured), so a retry would be a guessed fix under the closing rule rather than a repair with a named owner. The row stays open.

title: The docs map sent architecture decisions to `adr/` while the live decision register is `decisions/`: the map is fixed, and whether `docs/adr/` is merged into `decisions/`, kept as a second class of record, or removed is still open
detail:
FOUND BY THE ROOT while adding a row to docs/README.md for the new design language, so this is a doc-map defect spotted in passing rather than the task being done. MEASURED: docs/README.md's table has the row 'Why major architecture choices were made | adr/'. Two directories exist and they are not the same register: docs/adr/ holds 0002-0010 plus its own README, and docs/decisions/ holds 0019-0039 plus its own README. AGENTS.md's *Reuse before build* section names the live one plainly - 'Land a note at docs/decisions/NNNN-<slug>.md' - and scripts/reuse-gate.mjs enforces writes against that directory, so the gate and the map disagree about where a decision note goes. The numbering is contiguous when the two are read together (0002-0010, then 0019-0039) and there is a gap at 0011-0018, which is consistent with decisions/ having replaced adr/ at 0019 rather than with two registers running in parallel. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether adr/ is deliberately kept for a different class of decision - nothing in either README says it is, and both READMEs describe the same thing, one file per decision where the way something is built was not obvious. That is the same text in both places, which is what a superseded directory looks like when it was copied and then diverged. The cost is that the canonical map - the file AGENTS.md points a fresh session at for durable project truth - sends a reader to a register that stopped receiving rows at 0010. The fix is a judgement rather than a lookup, which is why this is a row and not a drive-by edit: either the map points at decisions/, or adr/ is the live one and decisions/ is the mistake, or the two are merged and the gap at 0011-0018 is explained. Nothing here changes either directory. AMENDED 2026-10-12 by the dead-code sweep's Task 6 (`f7900f5c`) and retitled by Task 7 to what survives. THE MAP HALF IS DONE: `docs/README.md`'s row now reads "`decisions/` - the live register, and the one `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs` enforces; the earlier set stopped at 0010 in `adr/`", so the disagreement this row's old title stated - the map sending readers to a register that stopped receiving rows at 0010 - no longer holds, and the map is no longer one of the three candidates. WHAT SURVIVES is the half the row raised and Task 6 explicitly did not settle: whether `docs/adr/` (0002-0010, last commit `36f141b1`, 2026-09-25) should be merged into `decisions/`, kept as a deliberate second class of record, or removed. The two directories' numbers still collide (both hold a `0004`), the gap at 0011-0018 is still unexplained, and nothing rules between the three. Retitled rather than closed for that reason, exactly as `vg-266` was.

RULED 2026-10-12: KEEP `docs/adr/` as a CLOSED series and make its citations explicit — do not merge, do not remove, do not renumber. Merging is not available at a price anyone should pay: the two series collide across 0001-0010 (both hold 0001-0005, and both hold a 0004 on a different decision), so a merge renumbers one of them and breaks every citation to the other, and this repo's citation discipline is what makes that cost real rather than theoretical. Removing is rejected because 0002-0010 still bind the architecture — `0002-fabric-is-the-single-renderer` is the decision the whole product is built on, and `0010` is the dispatch-record rule `AGENTS.md` cites by number — and deleting a decision that still governs is not housekeeping. What the row needs is legibility, which is cheap: a header in `docs/adr/README.md` saying the series closed at 0010 on 2026-09-25 and its numbers are its own, a citation convention that always writes the directory (`adr/0004` against `decisions/0004`), and one line in `docs/decisions/README.md` accounting for the 0011-0018 gap so the next reader does not go looking for it.

title: `--shell-warm` stayed a pastel in ember, moss and plum while those palettes' paper is light, so every `--warn` text reads at 1.4-2.0:1
detail:
FOUND BY THE DESIGN-LANGUAGE PARITY GATE (this plan, task 4) on the gate's first green run. MEASURED in the same browser pass as vg-200: a rejected numeric draft renders its reason in `text-warn` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/control-number.tsx:158`), and the composite over each palette's own panel is ember `#ff7e6e` on `rgb(247,226,210)` = 1.98:1, moss `#e8c56a` on `rgb(228,239,217)` = 1.40:1, plum `#ffb2a1` on `rgb(236,227,247)` = 1.39:1, against 5.18-9.36:1 in editorial, graphite and light. THE CONTROL SET IS NOT THE OWNER: the three declarations the pastels come from (`--shell-warm`'s three declarations, in the ember, moss and plum blocks) are the same `--shell-warm` that `.editor-shell-diagnostic` (`:1607`) and `.editor-shell-save-state` (`:1618`) paint, so on those three palettes the footer's warnings and the unsaved marker are unreadable too - the first `text-warn` in the product is not the defect, it is the first place the defect was measured. THE FILE ALREADY RECORDS THE SHAPE OF THE FIX: the comment above `[data-shell-palette="ember"]` says the three palettes' accents were 'deepened from the pastel that named them' because 'a light accent on a light surface carries nothing' and a pastel hover 'was a hover the author could not see'. `--shell-warm` was left as the pastel it was named for, and the same deepening is what it needs - at least 4.5:1 against each palette's own `--shell-surface` and against the glass overlay. NOT FIXED HERE because it is a colour decision with currency beyond text: `--vigilia-accent` aliases `--shell-warm` (`:112`) on the canvas side, so the value that makes warnings readable also moves the canvas accent, and only the design owner can rule on the hue. PINNED, NOT WAIVED, in `design-language.spec.ts` as `PINNED_FLOOR.invalid` (ember 1.9, moss 1.35, plum 1.35), deleted and replaced by the 4.5:1 minimum when this row is ruled on. SEVERITY: medium-high - required information (why a value was rejected) is illegible in three of the six shipped palettes.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: DEEPEN --shell-warm TO AT LEAST 4.5:1 AGAINST EACH PALETTE'S OWN --shell-surface AND AGAINST THE GLASS OVERLAY, AND LET THE CANVAS ACCENT MOVE WITH IT. One owner for the hue: --vigilia-accent aliases --shell-warm on the canvas side, so the readable value moves the canvas accent rather than the alias being broken. The pinned floor in design-language.spec.ts (PINNED_FLOOR.invalid -- ember 1.9, moss 1.35, plum 1.35) is deleted and replaced by the 4.5:1 minimum.

title: A well's horizontal padding is 6px, where bible section 3's table assigns 4px to inside-a-control and the mockup draws 8px
detail:
FOUND BY THE MOCKUP COMPARISON this plan's task 4 owes (the difference list beside `docs/design/mockups/inspector-controls.html`). MEASURED: `src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/control-well.tsx:54` pads every well `px-[var(--space-6)]` = 6px, and the same 6px carries through the select trigger, the swatch well and the number wells. Bible section 3's spacing table is an assignment as well as a set: `4` is 'Inside a control (well padding, icon button)' and `6` is 'Between the rows of one section', so 6px here is a step that belongs to a different place. The checked target disagrees with itself: `docs/design/mockups/inspector-controls.html` draws the select and range wells at `padding:5px 8px` and the slider's value well at `4px 6px`, so it offers 8, 6 and an off-scale 5 for the same job. Three sources, three answers, which is why this is a row rather than an edit - the value is contested, not merely unspecified. WHY THE GATE DOES NOT CATCH IT: `design-language.spec.ts` asserts that every authored spacing value is a step from section 3, which 6px is; it cannot see that the table assigns that step elsewhere, and no closed assertion can without the table becoming code. NOT FIXED HERE because the repair is a design ruling between three authorities and it moves the width of every control, including the 36px value well and the 246px pane's own gutters. SEVERITY: low - the chrome reads correctly today and only the step assignment is wrong.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: 6px. The product ships 6 and the drawing's own value well draws 4px 6px for the same element, so the mockup agrees with the product where it draws a well; section 3's 4px is the step inside a control rather than this row's horizontal padding, and the mockup's 5px 8px wells are the half that is corrected.

title: The palette picker's popup lands at the window's top-left instead of beside its swatch, and the spec that measures it is red at base
