detail: FOUND WHILE RUNNING plan 2 Task 1's full desktop-chromium gate, not by that task. keyboard.spec.ts ("the palette picker lands beside its trigger, and its tracks answer the arrow keys") fails at its `Math.abs(popup.y - (swatch.y + swatch.height + 6))` assertion (line 460 at HEAD) reading 340.3125 against an assertion of <= 12, so the popup's top is roughly a viewport above the swatch: the popover is unpositioned rather than offset. PRE-EXISTING, MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: the same spec text on the unmodified tree at base 2c0081b1, in a detached worktree (npm ci then npm run build, one test, desktop-chromium, workers=1, nothing else on the box), fails with the same reading, and the rail tree fails identically. So it is neither the rail's column nor a flake. The spec's own comment names the class: the popup moved from Radix's Content, which positions itself, to Base UI's Positioner, and a Popup placed straight in the portal renders unpositioned, which the class's two live sites record in general terms — `components/ui/colour-picker.tsx:200-201`, which hit the same Popup-in-portal fault and answers it with `Popover.Positioner` at `:203`, and this spec's own comment at `keyboard.spec.ts:449` — though the row's original pointer `panel.dom.test.ts:187-192` does not resolve: four files carry that name and none records it at those lines, so the earlier occurrence is recorded here as a claim rather than as a citation. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED: nothing here says whether the Positioner is absent from the portal, present and unmeasured, or anchored to a containing block the Tokens pane changes; the measuring assertion is where the test stops, so the arrow-key half below it is unmeasured rather than passing. OBSERVED AT HEAD AND NOT CLEARED (2026-10-11, 78a5575e): keyboard.spec.ts ran green, 5 of 5, in one desktop-chromium run, the palette-picker case among them, so the red is not reproducing today. One green sample does not withdraw a defect reproduced at base and measured twice, which is a measurement rather than a flake, so this row stays open pending a ruling. SAMPLE TAKEN 2026-10-12 (base 9e5d261e): `npx playwright test keyboard --grep "the palette picker lands beside its trigger, and its tracks answer the arrow keys"` is green, 1 expected / 0 unexpected in 5.5s - a second green sample at a new HEAD beside the 2026-10-11 one. Two greens do not withdraw a defect reproduced at base and measured twice, so the row still waits on the ruling it names. LINES RE-READ 2026-10-12 (base 9e5d261e), because the plan section 8.9 lists this row as citing moved ones: they have NOT moved. The measuring assertion is still `keyboard.spec.ts:460`, the Base UI `Positioner` comment still spans `:448-450`, and `components/ui/colour-picker.tsx:200-201` and `:203` are still the comment and the `Popover.Positioner` it names. That correction has nothing to apply here, and the row is otherwise unchanged.

title: A pane's title bar and footer scroll with its body, against bible section 7.7, because the aside is the only scroller
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 2's task review. `editor-shell-panel` and `.editor-shell-inspector`'s shared rule puts overflow:auto on aside.editor-shell-panel, and that aside contains the pane header, the body and the footer, so scrolling a long list takes the title bar and the toolbar off screen with it. Bible section 7.7 requires a pane's title and footer to stay outside the scrolling body, and layer-panel.tsx:809-810 carries a comment asserting exactly that property - "the toolbar stays put while the list scrolls beneath it" - about a structure that does not have it. The comment is corrected in Task 2's fix round; THIS ROW IS ABOUT THE STRUCTURE, not the comment. NOT FIXED THERE because the plan's own Global Constraint makes the aside the single scroller deliberately: choosePane restores each pane's scroll offset through it and shell-layout-scroll.dom.test.ts pins that, so moving to a scrolling body inside a fixed frame is a layout decision spanning the plan and the bible rather than a task. OWNER: unassigned - the plan that next restructures the pane frame. SEVERITY: low for behaviour (nothing becomes unreachable; the footer is still reachable by scrolling) and medium as a bible conformance gap.

RULED 2026-10-12: The STRUCTURE is the defect and DESIGN.md §7.7 wins. §7.7 is intact and says *Chrome stays still. Pane title and footer stay outside the scrolling body* (DESIGN.md:332), which is design intent recorded from the drawing; the plan's Global Constraint that made the aside the single scroller was an implementation shortcut taken so `choosePane` could restore a per-pane offset through one element, and a shortcut taken for a mechanism does not outrank the intent it broke. The rule for the next pane-frame restructure is therefore settled here: the BODY element owns the scroll, the title bar and footer sit outside it, and the per-pane offset and disclosure state are restored through the body — `shell-layout-scroll.dom.test.ts` pins the shortcut, so it changes in the same commit as the structure it pins. The row stays open with its owner named as that restructure, because none of it is cheap and none of it is a one-line fix; the severity stays low for behaviour, since the footer is still reachable by scrolling, and that low severity is the reason this is a ruling rather than a task in the current phase.

PREMISE RE-MEASURED 2026-10-16 (§8.2, and this one is not only a moved line). The row's title rests on the aside being **the only scroller**, and the rule it cites — the shell's single `overflow: auto` on the pane/inspector column — now carries **two** selectors, `.editor-shell-panel` and `.editor-shell-inspector`, in one shared block. So the citation is corrected, and the claim it supports is narrower than the title reads: it is not that one scroller exists but that the panel and the inspector share one. Whether the titled defect (a title bar and footer scrolling with the body) still reproduces under that shared rule is **not established here** and needs the browser run the row's own kind of evidence requires — this annotation records the drift rather than closing the finding.

title: The Add pane's data-vigilia-panel now scopes every add-pane locator to the whole pane, so a future asset control named with a shape word would collide
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 2's fix round and confirmed by its scoped re-review. The fix round deleted new-object-panel.ts:182's duplicate attribute and moved pane naming onto the pane itself (pane.tsx writes data-vigilia-panel={id} unconditionally), which is the right resolution - but it widens what that attribute's descendants mean. Spec locators rebuild-driver.ts:139 (addButton, hasText /^label$/), editor.spec.ts:31/789/838, composition-panel.spec.ts:1064 and author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts:73 now scope the Add pane, which also holds the asset host's buttons (asset-manager/panel.ts:30-35, labelled Import, Replace, Remove). MEASURED BENIGN TODAY: the shape filters match exact shape words and the getByRole name matches (Text, Gauge, Clock, Shape) are absent from the asset labels, and no case became ambiguous in the runs. NO CSS SCOPE CHANGED: no rule keys on a [data-vigilia-panel] button descendant, and every CSS rule on the attribute is ="layers", which sat on the pane before the fix too. NOT FIXED because nothing is broken to fix - the hazard is that a future asset control whose label is a shape word becomes ambiguous in rebuild-driver.ts:139, silently, and only in that spec. SEVERITY: low; the trigger is future work and the failure would be a strict-mode ambiguity rather than a wrong assertion.

RULED 2026-10-12: TAKE THE SPEC CHURN NOW and give the Add pane's shape controls their own scope. The row's measurement is that today's locators are benign, and the hazard is that a future asset control labelled with a shape word makes one spec ambiguous in strict mode — silently, and only in the spec that happened to scope the whole pane. A locator that any unrelated surface can invalidate by gaining a label is the flake class this repo has already paid for; the fix is one stable scope hook on the shapes section and the four locators pointing at it, which is cheaper than the first misdiagnosed ambiguity. What is NOT the fix: renaming the asset host's labels, which would be changing product copy to suit a test.

title: publish-loop.spec.ts:380 is red in the ordered suite but passes alone, at base as well as at HEAD
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 3's implementer, which verified it against the base before reporting rather than assuming. MEASURED 2026-10-15 by Task 14.1's fix round, on `develop` at `c242ad63` with the bundle rebuilt in `browser-pass-runbook.md`'s order, and re-measured at `3cbd92d8` by that round's re-review: the full suite (`npx playwright test --workers=1`) is red at this case, and the file's ordered two-case run (`npx playwright test tests/e2e/publish-loop.spec.ts --workers=1 --project=own-host`) is red at it — 1 failed / 1 passed — while the case ALONE (`-g "closing the editor puts the display back on the stored theme" --workers=1 --project=own-host`) PASSES, 1 passed in 3.1s. The group took in `editor-invalid-theme.spec.ts`, a spec about booting over a broken theme rather than publishing one, so `publish` had become a misnomer; the rename is `playwright.config.ts`'s `OWN_HOST_SPEC`.]

title: No gate runs biome check, so organizeImports is never enforced and import order drifts unchecked
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 3's task review, which noticed two files it was reviewing carried unapplied import ordering and that nothing in the repo would ever have said so. MEASURED: src/web/package.json defines format (biome format --write ..), format:check (biome format ..), lint (biome lint ..) and lint:fix, and .github/workflows/ci.yml:38 and :41 run format:check and lint - but no npm script and no CI step runs biome check. In Biome 2.x organizeImports is an assist action that biome check runs and that neither biome format nor biome lint does, so a file whose imports are out of order passes every gate the repo has. The concrete instance: publish-control.tsx:7-8 and shell-layout.tsx:1 at 2eeb4516 were both unorganised. NOT FIXED because adding a step to the repo's verification surface is a decision about the gates rather than about a task, and the two files were ordered by hand in Task 3's fix round instead. OWNER: unassigned. SEVERITY: low - style debt rather than a defect, and nothing downstream reads import order.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D1's lead ruling covering vg-213, vg-262, vg-372, vg-355 and vg-379 together: ADOPT biome check AS THE GATE. A CI step runs biome check and gates:self-test, the organizeImports findings are fixed in that commit, and every scripts/*.mjs self-test is chained into gates:self-test rather than excluded.

title: HostingStore never polls, so an out-of-band host change leaves the editor's live indicator stale until a reload
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 3's task review as a caveat, then MEASURED by the controller against the source. HostingStore (packages/editor/src/editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx:201-282) reads the host once in its constructor (:207-209) and re-emits only from its own actions - toggle() emits on the success path (:273-280) and on the refusal path (:261-270), and read() is public. So the review's phrasing 'read() runs only in the constructor' overstates it: the store does follow its own writes. What is genuinely missing is any poll or host-pushed update, so a change made outside the editor - the host CLI's own setLan (packages/host/src/cli/hosting.ts:29), or a host restart - is not observed until the page is reloaded or the control is pressed in-editor, and the live indicator renders a stale claim meanwhile. OWNER: Task 4's status bar owns the live indicator (its brief names PublishIndicator reading this store), so the fix belongs there if it is judged worth making; the alternative is to accept that the editor is the only in-session writer and close this as by-design. NOT FIXED in Task 3 because polling policy is the indicator's concern, not the header control's. SEVERITY: low - needs an external writer against the same host while the editor is open to be reachable at all.

RULED 2026-10-12: NO POLL — the host pushes, or the editor is the session's only writer. An editor polling the host for out-of-band changes is a timer the host owns, per this repo's own boundary (providers acquire; the host owns scheduling), and it would race the editor's own writes for no benefit the author can see. The channel already exists: the editor holds a live connection to the host, and the host is the only process that can observe its own `setLan` or a restart. So the ruling is a direction, not a feature: when the stale indicator is judged worth fixing, the host announces the change on that connection and the store re-reads; the editor never polls. Until then the row's own alternative stands — the editor is the only in-session writer by design — and that must be stated wherever the indicator's contract is written, so the staleness reads as a boundary rather than as a bug.

title: The theme document schema gives metadata.name no minLength, so an empty name validates
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 5's task review and CONFIRMED by the controller against the schema. schema/theme-document.schema.json defines the theme's name as $defs/metadata/properties/name = {type: string, maxLength: 200} - there is NO minLength, so an imported or hand-edited envelope carrying metadata.name: "" is schema-valid. That reaches the identity chip as an empty name: editor-main.ts:294 reads metadata?.name ?? envelope.id, and ?? falls back only on null/undefined, so "" passes through and DocumentIdentity (which hides only on undefined) renders a nameless frame - the bible section 9 failure its own comment promises cannot happen. The code side was fixed in Task 5's fix round by switching to ||; THIS row is the schema side, filed rather than fixed because adding minLength: 1 would start rejecting documents that validate today, which is a compatibility decision rather than a bug fix. Evidence it is an oversight rather than a decision: the sibling $defs/fontAssetReference/properties/license/name and the palette and typePreset group names all carry minLength: 1, and the theme's own top-level name is the one that does not. OWNER: unassigned - whoever owns document validation; the decision is whether a nameless theme is legal at all. SEVERITY: low once the read site is defensive - no data is lost, and the worst case is a chip showing an id instead of a name.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence: name GAINS minLength 1, AND THE LOADER NAMES WHAT IT FINDS UNNAMED. A theme with an empty name cannot be presented in the library, so the schema refuses it -- but a stored document that validates today is not allowed to become unloadable, so the migration supplies a name at load (from the file or a generated label) and the schema holds for anything written from now on. COST IF WRONG: a theme saved without a name gains one the author did not choose, which is visible and renameable, where the alternative is a document that cannot be opened at all.

title: The identity chip has no rule for what happens once the name is fully truncated: the fixed edited marker overflows and is clipped mid-word
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 6's completion round, from the collision assertion the controller required. At 640x360 CSS px - which is 1280x720 at the 200% browser zoom section 7.7 requires be checked - .editor-shell-identity's min-width: 0 let the chip shrink below the floor its non-shrinkable children set, so the trailing "Unsaved changes" painted from x=399 to x=483.6 while the chip's own box ended at 465 and the view cluster began at 473: a 10.6px overlap, with elementFromPoint answering SPAN where it should answer CANVAS. A comparison of the chip's BOX could never see it, which is why the assertion compares painted geometry and a point between the corners. Fixed in Task 6 with one declaration, overflow: hidden on .editor-shell-identity (the `.editor-shell-identity` rule), and that fix stands - it is containment, not surface, and R3's "do not touch the chip" ruling was about the panel/glass/elevation treatment. WHAT THIS ROW ACTUALLY IS, corrected after reading the chip's own rules rather than filing the round's framing: it is NOT that the wrong element is degraded. .editor-shell-identity-name is min-width: 0, overflow: hidden, text-overflow: ellipsis, so the name IS the only child that can shrink and it ellipsises first; the dot and the edited marker are both flex: none. So at 640x360 the name has already been truncated to nothing and the fixed marker still overflows by 10.6px - the arithmetic matches the measurement, since the chip's floor is its padding plus the 7px dot plus two gaps plus a fixed "Unsaved changes" that cannot shrink. The gap in the design language is therefore the state PAST a fully truncated name: section 7.7 licenses truncating identity's name, and says nothing about what the chip should do once the name is gone and a fixed part still does not fit. The landed behaviour is a mid-word clip with no ellipsis, which is the one presentation section 7.7 explicitly reserves for refusals and numeric edits. A future owner should NOT "make the name ellipsise instead" - it already does. The open choices are dropping or shortening the edited marker at compact widths, allowing it to wrap, or accepting the clip and saying so. OWNER: the identity chip's presentation, or Task 10's difference list; adjacent to but distinct from vg-219, which lists the chip's three mockup differences. SEVERITY: low - cosmetic, at one breakpoint, with no data, reachability or focus lost.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: REMOVE THE UNSAVED-CHANGES MARKER FROM THIS CHIP AND KEEP ONLY THE COLOURED INDICATOR DOT. The marker was the fixed part that overflowed once the name truncated, and the dirty state is already carried by the status bar at the bottom right, so the chip loses the text rather than dropping, shortening, wrapping or accepting a clip. Neither vg-219 nor vg-230 is absorbed by this: the chip's mockup differences and the status bar's reads stand on their own rows.

title: Renaming an object is written in two places, they refuse differently, and the validity guard lives in a module the ownership map does not name
detail:
FOUND by a read-only architecture survey the user asked for ('does any domain manager need clean-up — same domain spread across a few managers, a domain under another owner that should be its own'), run on 2026-10-09 with docs/architecture/ownership.md as the yardstick. Verified from source. The validity RULE has one owner and is shared correctly — renderer-core/src/theme/object-name.ts:33 isObjectName — but that module has NO row in ownership.md, and by the map's own preamble a module owning a concept while appearing nowhere in the map is invisible, so nothing warns a reader not to decide it elsewhere. The two writers of the FACT disagree on the refusal path: editor-shell/bridge.ts:323-324 (layer-row rename) returns silently at :329, while selection-inspector/appearance.ts:339 reports through errorManager.warn('controls', uiCopy.inspectorFields.invalidName) at :319-325. They notify differently too: bridge fires nothing and relies on the session subscription (bridge.ts:148), while appearance.ts:345-350 fires object:modified itself. So typing a refused name has two outcomes depending on which surface it was typed in — one author action, two behaviours. NOT ESTABLISHED: neither writer was traced past the refusal branch. OWNER: unassigned; the name write belongs with the object's identity, and both surfaces should call it. SEVERITY: low — the name is refused either way, and the divergence is in what the author is told. CONFIRMED BY THE CENSUS (2026-10-12), after a review forced it to apply one standard in both places: this row's complaint stands. The code half is exactly as described -- the guard is now shared (bridge.ts:346 and view.ts:456 both call isObjectName), and the second writer moved from selection-inspector/appearance.ts to selection-inspector/index.ts:384. The unnamed-module half also stands: object-name.ts sits in renderer-core/src/theme/, and the registry's row for that names a DIRECTORY ("Theme semantic types/validation"), which does not name a module: the census states the rule as a row names a module when the file holding the guard is fixed by the row, which a *-manager/ directory does by pointing at its index.ts entry and which renderer-core/src/theme/ does not do for any of its eleven modules. The census applies that same standard to selection-inspector's own files too, so it is one standard rather than two, and not this row being right by luck. Consequence beyond this row, and the reason to keep it: several registry rows name directories, so the map's module-level coverage is thinner than its row count suggests.

READING 2026-10-13: the unnamed-module half is discharged — the ownership map now names renderer-core/src/theme/object-name.ts as the object-name rule's owner (dd308143). The divergence half stands and the row stays open against it: a refused rename returns silently at editor-shell/bridge.ts:341-352 and reports "invalid" at selection-inspector/view.ts:440-450.

title: A text run has no identity in the persisted model, so the inspector's row keys must come from content — an edit or a same-shape middle removal changes the key and costs the row its caret
detail:
FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 3, TASK 3, during its fix loop. The run editor keys each row by a derived identity because `vigiliaText.runs` is a plain array with no per-run id. Two attempts were made and each trades one failure for another, which is the evidence that the model is the cause rather than the key. (1) Positional index keys: the row survives an edit, but removing a MIDDLE run shifts every later index, so React reconciles a row holding a draft onto the next run's data — the draft is displayed against the wrong run and the next blur can commit it there (filed as M1 in the task review). (2) Content-derived identity `` `literal:${typePreset}\u0000${text}` ``: a middle removal is then safe, because survivors keep their keys, but `ControlText` commits on ENTER (`components/ui/control-text.tsx:74`), so committing a typed reading changes the key, remounts the row, destroys the focused input and drops focus to `document.body` (N1). The shipped fix excludes the mutable TEXT from the identity, which removes the Enter failure and leaves a residual, recorded in `runs.tsx` rather than hidden: two literal runs sharing a type preset can still shift on a middle removal, and changing a run's preset or its source binding still remounts that row. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS TASK. Task 3a's brief requires it to preserve 'repeat-row identity' for chart series rows, which is the same problem over the same kind of array, so it will be met again before the plan closes. PRECEDENT, NOT A GUESS. The same class was already found and fixed once: vg-044 (archived, verified) — 'A chart's series colours and its bindings are coupled by index, so removing a middle binding shifts the colours' — and its fix was NOT an id. It reconciles at mutation time, carrying each surviving series' own paint through the removal before the array-length repair runs. So the cheap path here is probably the same shape: carry the surviving rows' state through the removal (or hold drafts outside the row), rather than adding a persisted id. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether reconciliation is sufficient for the caret case, since a lost draft and a misplaced draft are different harms, or whether the model should simply gain a per-run id — that is a persisted-schema decision (existing documents hold runs without one) and is not a task-level call. NOT CLAIMED: that the shipped fix is wrong; it is the best of the three shapes available without a model change, and its residual is disclosed in code and in the task report. OWNER: whoever owns the persisted text-run model with whoever owns the inspector's row rendering.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence: THE PERSISTED TEXT-RUN MODEL GAINS NO PER-RUN ID, AND THE INSPECTOR RECONCILES SURVIVORS AT MUTATION TIME AS vg-044 DID. An id added to persisted runs is editor bookkeeping written into the theme file, which is the line AGENTS.md draws -- persist authored state only -- and the reconciliation at mutation time is the precedent this repo already has. COST IF WRONG: the inspector carries reconciliation logic it would not need with ids; that logic already exists for vg-044.

title: isTextEntryTarget counts a range input as a text-entry target, so every shortcut the manager owns is swallowed while a slider has focus
detail:
FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 3, TASK 7 (fix round 1, commit 4bf29bf6), which added it as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer. `isTextEntryTarget` (src/web/packages/editor/src/shortcut-manager/index.ts:192-213) returns true for any HTMLInputElement whose type is not in a small exclusion set - button, checkbox, color, file, image, radio, reset, submit (:202-211). `range` is not in that set, so a focused input[type=range] is treated as a text-entry target, the handler at :143-147 sets `deferred`, and the manager returns before preventDefault() and before the bound handler. CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS WIDER THAN THE TRAILER AND THE COMMIT MESSAGE SAY: both name Ctrl+Z (undo swallowed while a slider has focus), but the predicate gates EVERY action the shortcut table binds, so Delete, Escape and the rest are swallowed too. The controller verified the cause at source rather than taking the trailer's word for it. WHY THE FIX IS NOT JUST ADDING range TO THE SET: the same predicate guards the bare-key canvas listeners (camera keys), so a range was presumably left in deliberately - an unmodified arrow on a focused slider must move the slider, not the camera. Ctrl+Z is a modifier chord with no native meaning on a range, so it should reach the manager while an unmodified arrow should not. That makes the repair a decision about which keys a non-text control still defers, not a one-line set edit. AUTHOR-FACING AND REACHABLE: click the slider, press Ctrl+Z, nothing happens. BLAST RADIUS: every ControlSlider the plan-1 control set renders, which after this plan is polygon sides, the shape sweep pair and glass blur. NOT FIXED HERE because the owner is shortcut-manager and the task that found it is the inspector, and the correct behaviour is a ruling rather than a patch.

RULED 2026-10-12: The predicate is wrong in KIND, not in membership: it answers "is this target a text-entry target" where the question is "does this target consume this key". A text field consumes everything printable, so the coarse question happens to work there; a range consumes its own navigation keys and nothing else, so a modifier chord must reach the manager while an unmodified arrow stays with the slider. The repair is a consumption rule per target shape, enumerated as data beside the control set that owns those shapes: a text-like target consumes printable keys, a range consumes exactly the keys it natively handles (the four arrows, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down), and every other control consumes nothing. That keeps the camera keys on a focused slider — which is why a range was in the set deliberately — and gives Ctrl+Z back, which is the half the row measured as broken. Enumerated rather than inferred so a control the set gains later states what it consumes instead of inheriting a default nobody chose.

SECTION 8.10 REFUTED 2026-10-16, AND THE CORRECTION WAS NOT APPLIED. The plan's drift table says this row's premise is "half-false — the deferral is action-scoped, not 'every action'" and orders the title's `every shortcut the manager owns` softened. **The row's own detail says the opposite, and says it as a measurement rather than an inference**: "the predicate gates EVERY action the shortcut table binds, so Delete, Escape and the rest are swallowed too", marked as verified at source by the controller rather than taken from the trailer. The ruling on this row agrees and goes further — the predicate is wrong in KIND, and what is wrong is *which keys* a target defers, not whether the deferral is broad. So the premise holds and the title is accurate as written; **applying §8.10 would have written a false statement into the register.** Left standing deliberately.

title: A slider in the selection column gives no live preview while dragging, so the value only moves on release
detail:
FOUND WHILE REVIEWING PLAN 3 TASK 9 (the parity capture), in the built editor at 1ab06ad2, by the task reviewer and verified at source by the controller while filing. MEASURED: with the Layer Opacity slider focused, a pointer drag to roughly 50% and then 25% left aria-valuenow AND the well reading 99 throughout, and the value jumped to 26 only on mouse-up - so an author dragging a bounded number sees nothing change until they let go. CAUSE, read rather than guessed: selection-inspector/column.tsx:183-192 renders ControlSlider with onCommit and no onPreview, although the control supports a preview callback (components/ui/control-slider.tsx:30 and :112, described in its own docblock at :17) and components/ui/control.dom.test.tsx:659-676 exercises it. The field funnel has no preview half to call: SelectionEdits exposes only commit, where the sibling CropEdits (selection-inspector/view.ts:269-274) has begin/setAspect/apply/cancel. NOT A BIBLE VIOLATION, which is why this is filed rather than fixed: design-language.md section 5 says a slider MAY preview through the existing imperative write funnel, so preview is permitted and not required, and release committing one changed value is satisfied as it stands. SHARED, NOT INTRODUCED HERE: the same field renderer draws the glass blur and panel radius sliders, so every slider in the column behaves this way and the behaviour predates plan 3's Task 9. WHY IT NEEDS A RULING RATHER THAN A PATCH: giving sliders a preview means adding a preview/cancel path to the field funnel and deciding how a preview that writes nothing interacts with the one-undo-boundary rule the same section states, across the control set, the funnel and the history boundary - a design decision with more than one owner, not a missing prop.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. A SLIDER PREVIEWS WHILE DRAGGING AND COMMITS ON RELEASE. Section 5 permits preview through the imperative write funnel; the field funnel gains a preview and a cancel path, and the preview writes no history entry -- the release commits exactly one value, which is what the one-undo-boundary rule asks. A control that shows nothing until release is a control whose value the author cannot see while choosing it, and the same renderer draws every slider in the column, so the fix is one path rather than one field. COST IF WRONG: every slider in the selection column gains a code path, and the funnel gains a state it did not have; the undo rule is the invariant this must not break.

title: writeOpacity is the selection column's sole 0-100 enforcement and has no test
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 3'S FINAL WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW (2026-10-09) as the sharpest residual of the close, and descended from Ruling AH in the plan's ledger. selection-inspector/index.ts:469-482 refuses a value outside 0-100 and warns; plan 3 Task 9 converted the Layer Opacity field from a text box to a slider (appearance.ts opacityField, control 'slider', min 0, max 100, integer true), which DELETED the only route by which an author could produce an out-of-range value - so the two text-box tests that drove the refusal had nothing left to drive and were replaced by a slider test that exercises the control's own bound. NO CONTRIVED ROUTE EXISTS, checked rather than assumed: Base UI clamps inside handleInputChange -> getSliderValue (SliderRoot.mjs:177-190) before onValueCommitted fires, SelectionInspector exposes no seam (index.ts:67-75 - root, render, setGlobals, setLocale only), writeOpacity is not exported, and editRefusal can never produce 'invalid' for this field because view.ts:380 types the opacity kind as 'number'. WHY IT STILL DESERVES AN OWNER: the guard is now the column's SOLE enforcement, so a future control reusing the 'opacity' field id with a bad value is caught in production rather than in CI. Fixing it means either a public test seam added for a test's sake or a contrived injection that would prove Base UI's clamping rather than this guard.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. THE GUARD STAYS AND NO TEST SEAM IS ADDED. writeOpacity is the selection columns sole 0-100 enforcement, the row established that no route reaches it except production (Base UI clamps before the commit, SelectionInspector exposes no seam, the function is not exported, the kind is typed number), so adding a public export purely so a test can call it widens a modules public surface for the tests benefit rather than the products. The guard is named in the code as production-only defence with the reason it is unreachable from a test, so its absence from CI is a recorded fact rather than an unnoticed gap. COST IF WRONG: a regression in the guard is caught in production rather than in CI; the comment is what makes that a decision rather than a hole.

title: Sixty-seven organizeImports findings sit in the tree invisible to every gate, because nothing in the repo ever runs biome check
detail:
FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER WHILE MEASURING TASK 5 OF PLAN 4 (2026-10-10), NOT BY A FAILING TEST. THE MEASUREMENT: from src/web, npx biome check .. reports 67 errors over 605 files, and all 67 are assist/source/organizeImports (Sort these imports) in 67 distinct files, from packages/editor/src/components/ui/control-select.tsx to packages/host/src/main.ts. npx biome lint .. over the same tree reports 0 errors and 0 warnings. THE GAP: src/web/package.json wires lint to biome lint .. and format:check to biome format .., and neither subcommand runs the assist category - assist is a third mode that only biome check reaches. biome.json carries no assist key at all, so organizeImports is on by default and fires only under check, which no npm script invokes. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the only biome steps the repo has (format:check at line 38, lint at line 41) and neither is a check. So the rule is enabled, the tree violates it 67 times, and no local gate, no CI step and no hook will ever say so. WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC: import order in this tree is authored by hand and drifts, and the drift is invisible in both directions - the gate cannot fail, and an implementer who runs npx biome check on the files they touched sees findings that no gate will ever surface or fix, which reads as pre-existing noise. Plan 4 Task 4 report hit exactly that and recorded an organizeImports finding on card-insert-surfaces.dom.test.tsx as pre-existing and untouched rather than as a signal. FILED RATHER THAN FIXED because the fix is a decision with a blast radius, not a patch: running biome check in CI, or wiring assist into the lint script, turns 67 pre-existing findings into a red gate in the commit that does it, and whether this repo wants import order enforced at all is a call nobody has made. The two candidate shapes - add check to the gates and fix the 67 in the same commit, or leave check out and delete the expectation - each need a ruling first. NOT URGENT: nothing is pushed, so no CI is red today.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D1's lead ruling covering vg-213, vg-262, vg-372, vg-355 and vg-379 together: ADOPT biome check AS THE GATE. A CI step runs biome check and gates:self-test, the organizeImports findings are fixed in that commit, and every scripts/*.mjs self-test is chained into gates:self-test rather than excluded. This row's count is corrected as it is ruled: 60 organizeImports findings, not the 67 the line reads.

COUNT CORRECTED 2026-10-16 (§8.9), and the correction is that the number MOVED rather than that it was wrong. This row records a measurement taken 2026-10-10: 67 errors over 605 files, all 67 `assist/source/organizeImports`. **By the time D1's ruling fixed them, the same measurement read 63 errors — 60 `assist/source/organizeImports` and 3 others — across 618 files** (the ledger's own record of that commit). So neither 67 nor 60 is the finding's size: the count is a property of the tree on the day it was taken, and this row's number is three days older than the fix. The finding itself is fixed and biome has been a gate since D1; what this note corrects is a reader taking 67 as the size of a defect that was 60 by the time anyone acted on it.

title: A refused colour in the Tokens pane is announced to nobody, and the control set has no channel for an invalid-but-still-editable field
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 5 TASK REVIEW (2026-10-10, commit ebe1743b), NOT BY A FAILING TEST - and that is half the finding. THE REGRESSION: before Task 5 the pane relied on the platform's own refusal, `reportValidity()` on the colour input, which announced itself to assistive technology for free. Task 5 replaced it with a local error state rendered as a bare `

` (paint-list.tsx:254-258) that is a SIBLING of the field it belongs to (the ControlText at paint-list.tsx:232-253) and is associated with nothing: no `aria-describedby`, no `aria-invalid`, no live region. A screen-reader user types an unpaintable colour, the edit is refused, and the refusal is silent. WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS NOT AVAILABLE: the control set already has this mechanism - control-well.tsx renders a reason element and control-text.tsx:70-71 wires `aria-describedby` to it - but it is reachable only through the `refused` prop, and `refused` also sets `readOnly` (control-text.tsx:68) and `aria-disabled`. That is right for a value the DOCUMENT refuses (a locked object) and wrong here: this value is refused because the author just typed something the engine cannot paint, and the field has to stay editable so they can type a different one. Using `refused` would trap them on the stale-but-valid value. Nor can the pane wire it itself: `ControlProps.data` is typed `Readonly>` (control-well.tsx:24-32), so there is no aria pass-through, and the pane does not own the input element. THE REAL FIX IS A CONTROL-SET CONCEPT - a channel for invalid-but-still-editable, distinct from `refused`, carrying `aria-invalid` plus a described-by reason without `readOnly`. That is why this is filed rather than fixed on the fly (AGENTS.md): the cause is established but the fix is a new concept in a different owner - the control set, built and closed in plan 1 - it spans subsystems, and it needs a design decision about how many refusal shapes the control set should carry. It is not Task 5's to invent, and a second ad-hoc `

` in the next pane would make three. THE TEST GAP THAT LET IT THROUGH: tests/e2e/editor.spec.ts:672-697 proves the refusal HAPPENS (not-a-colour is refused, the field stays on #123456, rgb(1, 2, 3) clears it) but never that it is announced, and jsdom cannot see platform bubbles either - so neither layer could have gone red. CLOSE THIS by adding the editable-invalid channel to the control set, wiring the Tokens pane's colour field to it, and pinning that a refused value carries `aria-invalid` and a described-by reason while remaining editable. RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: THE CONTROL SET GAINS THE CHANNEL. A value that is invalid but still editable becomes a named member of the control set rather than the platform's reportValidity() carrying it, so the state is expressed and reviewed the way every other control state is, instead of being whatever the browser does.

title: The React control set prints its refusals in hardcoded English, so a pane's own invalid-value copy became unreachable
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 8 (2026-10-10, commit 9f6252a8) IN TASK REVIEW, AND FIRST FILED WRONGLY - this row replaces a framing that was measured false, and the correction is the reason it reads as narrowly as it does. THE FINDING: `ControlNumber` (components/ui/control-number.tsx:94,99,103,107,111) writes its five refusal sentences as hardcoded English - "a value is required", "not a number", "a whole number", "at least 1", "at most 16384" - while every other user-visible string in the editor comes from `uiCopy`. The control it replaced took its message as a parameter defaulting to `uiCopy.panels.invalidNumber` (number-field.ts:88), so the artboard size pair used to say "That value cannot be applied. Enter a number in range." (ui-copy.ts:650) and now says "at most 16384". That key is not dead - it is still read by number-field.ts:88, reachable only from the settings path (settings-field.ts:115 is `numberField`'s only shipped caller) - so one editor now carries two vocabularies for one refusal depending on which numeric control a surface happens to use. WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED ON THE FLY (AGENTS.md): the cause is established but the fix is a design decision in a different owner - the copy rules are plan 6's and the control set is plan 1's, built and closed - and neither side obviously moves: `ControlNumber` could take its message from `uiCopy` (a new key, and a copy dependency the control set does not have today), or `uiCopy.panels.invalidNumber` could be retired and the hardcoded strings promoted into it (the copy module acquiring keys only one control uses). WHY THE FIRST FILING WAS WRONG, because the mistake is the useful part: I filed this as "a number field no longer says what it will accept until after a value is refused", asserting the old pane printed its bound (1-16384) at rest. It did not. `boundLine` is rendered only by `numberField` (number-field.ts:53-59), and the artboard pane used `linkedPair` (artboard-panel.ts:19,150 at 21a5135e), which calls `numberInput` directly (linked-pair.ts:1,55,66) - so no artboard author ever saw that line and the discoverability loss described did not occur. The task reviewer measured it three ways (`git log -S` over the file's whole history finds no `numberField`/`boundLine`/`field-bound`; the pane's own old tests never mention them; settings-field.ts is `numberField`'s only caller) and the controller re-read linked-pair.ts to confirm. The implementer's report Deviation 4 made the same claim, so a subagent's description of code it had already replaced became a register row unmeasured - a verify-the-claim failure, not a reasoning one, and the check that catches it is one grep of the base commit. Related: vg-113 (unit display options hardcoded English), vg-263 (a refused colour announced to nobody - the other half of the same question, what the control set owes an author whose value it will not take).

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. THE CONTROL SET TAKES ITS REFUSAL COPY FROM uiCopy. uiCopy is the repos one owner for user-visible strings and it carries a copy census, so a shared control printing hardcoded English is the drift that census exists to prevent; the control set gains a copy dependency and each consumer supplies its strings through the locale the shell already sets. The rows other half is corrected rather than ruled: the panes own invalid-value copy was never unreachable because it never existed -- the task reviewer measured it three ways -- so the live question is this one only.

title: `editor-shell.css` styles `select` elements nothing renders: the inspector pair this row named is deleted, and the surviving arms trace to an unimported `settingsField`
detail: FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING PLAN 4 TASK 10 (2026-10-10, commit 80facf67) AND CARRIED AS A `Discovered, not fixed:` TRAILER IN THAT COMMIT; both terms were re-located BY RULE in 4a283864, which deleted the two `.editor-shell-panel select` terms beside them and so moved the lines. MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: with an object selected in the built editor, `document.querySelectorAll('.editor-shell-inspector select')` is 0, `.editor-shell-panel select` is 0 and `.editor-shell select` is 0. The last `document.createElement("select")` the editor shell's own code holds is settings-field.ts:196, imported by controls.dom.test.ts alone (R68's consumer survey), so the terms style an element nothing renders. [CORRECTED 2026-10-12, see the amendment below: this sentence said "the only ... in the package" and that was false.] NOT DELETED IN TASK 10 because the rule there is delete-what-lost-its-OWN-last-consumer within that plan, and this pair's consumer left in plan 3; a cross-plan dead rule belongs in the register rather than in a sweep task's diff. TWO CORRECTIONS, both to statements rather than to the measurement. (2) The sentence above that claimed settings-field.ts:196 was the only `createElement("select")` in the package was **FALSE**: `packages/host/public/settings.html:197` and `:372` hold two more, inside `packages/`. The material conclusion survives: `settingsField` is imported by `controls.dom.test.ts` and `copy-defects.test.ts` only, while production imports only `isSettingVisible`/`settingsFieldsFor`. WHAT SURVIVES INSTEAD is four arms, located by rule as this row requires: `.editor-shell select` and the `select` arm of the `:is(...)` focus rule, both already covered by this row's own browser measurement (`.editor-shell select` = 0), plus `.vigilia-field select` and `.vigilia-field-row select`, which are dead by the static argument only -- `.vigilia-field`'s producers (`number-field.ts:55`, `settings-field.ts:236`, `new-document-chooser.tsx:236`) render no `<select>` -- and have **not** been browser-measured. Retitle rather than close: closing would lose both the measurement debt on those two arms and the fact that they are dead by the same missing-importer argument this row owns. TASK 2.4b, 2026-10-12: the browser measurement this row owed is taken on the built editor preview at base 7f88dff3. document.querySelectorAll('select') is 0 in every state read: the editor at boot with nothing selected, with a Rectangle selected, with the settings modal open on each of its three tabs, with the New-document chooser open (where .vigilia-field is 1, so that class does render), and on the Add pane. .editor-shell select, .vigilia-field select and .vigilia-field-row select are 0 in every one of those states, and the dialog is not a descendant of .editor-shell (.editor-shell [role=dialog] is 0 with the modal open), so the .editor-shell arm cannot reach a dialog's select either. The measurement debt is discharged: all four arms are dead by measurement as well as by the row's static argument. NOT DELETED HERE, and that is the one act left: the four arms are a cross-plan sweep of editor-shell.css rather than a browser pass's act, and the cost of moving them is measurable: 18 live rows attribute a line to that file, 31 such citations across them, with 33 rows mentioning the file at all, so the delete belongs to whoever can carry those citations with it.

detail:

title: The spec's acceptance instrument for native controls cannot see the class it exists for
detail:

title: The design-language fixture proves the shell's global focus rule, not the portalled control's own, because it nests the row inside `.editor-shell`
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 2'S SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-10, over 64fea389..eba81b2a), WHICH CORRECTED THE FINDING ITS OWN FIX ROUND HAD FILED. WHAT THE COMMIT TRAILER CLAIMED (commit eba81b2a): that `components/ui/control-choice-row.tsx:54`'s `focus-visible:outline-*` classes are inert, because `.editor-shell :is(button, …):focus-visible` out-specifies them. MEASURED: the specificity half is true only for an element INSIDE `.editor-shell` - the shell rule is unlayered while the Tailwind utility lands in `@layer utilities` (built CSS: `.focus-visible\:outline-2:focus-visible` at offset 20264 inside `@layer utilities{` @7990, the shell rule unlayered at 39365) and its specificity (0,3,0) beats the class's (0,2,0). But the Appearance tab does not ship inside `.editor-shell`: the modal is a Base UI Dialog portalled to `document.body` (`components/ui/dialog.tsx:44-60`), a sibling of `#app` rather than a descendant of `.editor-shell` (`palette.ts:93-99`, `shell-layout.tsx:699`), so there the shell rule cannot match at all and the control's own classes are the SOLE focus treatment. The CSS author knew: `.editor-shell-settings-tab:focus-visible` and `.editor-shell-settings-panel:focus-visible` exist precisely because the dialog is portalled, and no equivalent rule exists for the choice row. ACTING ON THE TRAILER WOULD HAVE BEEN A DEFECT - deleting those classes as redundant strips the shipped product's focus ring, while the design-language fixture stays green because there the shell rule paints the outline. THE REAL FINDING IS THE PROOF-CONTEXT GAP: `control-fixture.tsx:145-175` mounts `ControlChoiceRow` inside the fixture's own `.editor-shell` (`:62`), and `design-language.spec.ts`'s new §4e case (`~:866-1030`) asserts a `solid` outline of at least 2px there - which the shell's global rule supplies. So §4e passes even when the control's own focus classes paint nothing, and cannot detect a regression in the treatment that actually ships on the portalled modal. The implementer's own red proof demonstrates exactly this: removing the shell focus rule reddened the case with `paints the browser's auto ring, not §5's solid outline`, while the classes were the thing under test. NOT FIXED HERE because the fix is a decision about how a portalled surface is measured (a second fixture outside `.editor-shell`, or a browser case on the real modal) rather than a one-line change, and this plan's Task 6 owns the capture. OWNER: whoever owns `components/ui/` and the design-language fixture's context.

READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174; the venue is `design-language.spec.ts`'s fixture case, and the second half is the shipped portalled modal): the fixture case passes in the same run (`the control set renders in the design language`, 4156ms), and on the shipped Appearance tab a focused palette card - a `ControlChoiceRow` - computes `:focus-visible` true, `outline-style: solid`, `outline-width: 2px`, `outline-color: rgb(114, 224, 192)`, `outline-offset: 2px`, while `closest(".editor-shell")` on it is null (its only dialog ancestor is the portalled `.editor-shell-dialog`). So the ring that ships is painted by the control's own classes, and the fixture's green reads that same visual fact through the shell's global rule instead. What §4e cannot see is the control's own classes going missing.

RULED 2026-10-15: **BOTH, and they answer different questions.** A second fixture mounted *outside* `.editor-shell` makes the control's own focus classes the thing that paints, so a regression in them reddens the case instead of being masked by the shell's global rule — that is the fast regression. A browser case against the real portalled Appearance modal asserts the ring that actually ships, on a surface `closest(".editor-shell")` does not match — that is the shipped-surface proof the fixture cannot give, because the fixture is a stand-in for the modal rather than the modal. **Neither substitutes for the other**, which is why this is both rather than the cheaper one: the fixture proves the treatment is present, and the browser case proves the treatment is reachable where it ships.

title: The editor bundle has no product-version source, so the About tab can name no version for Vigilia itself
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 4'S STEP 1 (2026-10-10), BY READING, NOT BY TESTING. Measured with `grep -rn version packages/editor/src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v .test. | grep -vi canvas`: the only hits are the theme's own release version (editor-session.ts:1092 bumpSemanticVersion; panes/document/metadata-fields.tsx:101 metadata?.version) and unrelated words (Fabric's scene version 7.4.0 in new-fabric-theme.ts:188, the qr-symbol.tsx version, storage-key prose) - not one product version. `grep -rn 'VERSION|SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION' packages/host/src/main.ts packages/renderer-core/src/theme/document.ts` finds the host's const VERSION = "0.1.0" at packages/host/src/main.ts:34, Node-side and logging Vigilia v${VERSION} at :250 and not in the editor bundle, and SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2 at packages/renderer-core/src/theme/fabric-envelope.ts:16 (it was 1 in theme/document.ts, which schema v1's retirement deleted on 2026-10-11), a schema number this build can read but which is not the product's version. packages/editor/package.json is 0.0.0 and packages/editor/vite.config.ts injects no define. So the About tab (landed in the same commit) renders the schema version and the open document's release version, and nothing claiming to be Vigilia's own version. WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: giving the product one version string both the host CLI and the editor bundle import is a host change that needs a decision rather than a task, and more than one owner could fix it, so it sits outside plan 5's scope.

RULED 2026-10-12: ONE OWNER: the workspace manifest's `version` field is the product's version, and both readers take it from there rather than from a new module. The host already runs Node and can read `src/web/package.json`; the editor bundle is built by Vite, which injects it through `define` at build time. That keeps one number, written in the place a release already has to change it, with no new exported constant and no second file to forget. Two things the fix must not do: it must not make the schema version carry the product's meaning — `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays a separate fact, and the About tab keeps labelling it as what it is — and it must not present the open document's release version as Vigilia's own. The About tab gains one line naming the product version; the other two lines keep their own labels.

title: The layer row's attended state slot can intercept a press meant for the row, so a click on a name may reach its visibility or lock control
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 4A PART I'S SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-10, over 50797965..b3805273). MEASURED, in the test harness: `tests/e2e/rebuild-driver.ts:206-222` presses a layer row through `.vigilia-layer-name` at the element's LEFT END rather than at its default centre, and its own comment records why - the centre is intercepted, and five cases of `author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts` hung on it. The comment names the interceptor: the attended row's absolutely-positioned state slot (`editor-shell.css:1707-1712`, `position: absolute; right: 2px; top: 0; height: 26px`), which sits over the name because the name is `flex: 1 1 auto` (`editor-shell.css:1658`). WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether this is a product-side hazard or only a Playwright fixed-point problem. A real pointer that hovers a row to click it has already revealed that row's state slot, so a press aimed at the row can land on the slot's own controls (visibility, lock) instead of selecting the layer - but nobody has measured the slot's width against the row's, or what a press at the name's centre actually hits in a browser. The CSS author calls the related shift deliberate: the attended row's name narrows by whatever its key does not take, "charged to the one row the pointer is on, and it is deliberate" (`editor-shell.css:1700-1708`). That states the SHIFT is intended; it does not say the slot may swallow a press aimed at the row. NOT FIXED HERE because the cause is not established and the fix, if needed, is a layout decision about the attended row rather than a test edit; the harness works around it, which also means nothing reddens if the layout changes. OWNER: whoever owns the layer row's layout (`selection-inspector/` and `editor-shell.css`'s `.vigilia-layer-*` rules). TASK 2.4b, 2026-10-12: the pointer measurement this row owed is taken on the built preview at base 7f88dff3, and the hazard is REAL at the desktop viewport. With a layer row attended (hovered) and its four-control slot drawn, the name's box reads left 120 / right 240.6 while the slot reads left 155 / right 277 — the slot overlaps the name by 85.6px — and document.elementFromPoint at the name's centre returns an SVG inside the slot's first button, where the same read 6px inside the name's left edge returns the name's own span. The cause is named: the room the :has rules reserve is written on .vigilia-layer-bound (editor-shell.css:2188-2206), this row draws no bound at all, so nothing reserves it and the absolutely-positioned .vigilia-layer-state (:2121-2134) covers the name. Three citations on this line corrected by re-measurement, as symbols and lines: the slot is .vigilia-layer-state at editor-shell.css:2121, not :1707-1712; the name is .vigilia-layer-name at :2072, not :1658; the deliberate-shift comment is at :2115-2120. STAYS OPEN: the fix is a layout decision about the attended row, which the row already says.

title: Two editor specs claim a fresh starter trips the dirty guard, which the session mechanism contradicts, while a third records the opposite sample
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 4A PART I'S SECOND SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-10, over b3805273..846e451c), which retired the same claim from a fourth file. THE CONTRADICTION: `tests/e2e/author-journey-display.spec.ts:231-235` and `tests/e2e/composition-panel.spec.ts:556-558` both assert that a fresh starter "counts as unsaved work", so opening another theme asks the dirty guard. The mechanism says otherwise: `editor-session.ts:1004-1020` asks only when `isDirty`, and `persistence-manager/index.ts:34,42` compares the current key against `#savedDocument` - the snapshot the session opened on, built at `editor-session.ts:498-501`. `editor-main.ts:233-238`'s `onNew` mounts a fresh session, so a document that has just been created IS its own baseline. MEASURED, by the implementer, against the built bundle during round 2: after Create a fresh editor shows zero `[role="dialog"]`, and Open library opens the chooser with no question - which is why the fourth file's comment (`tests/e2e/rebuild-driver.ts:132-138`) was corrected in `bdce766e`. WHAT MAKES IT A FINDING RATHER THAN A TYPO: `tests/e2e/reference-theme.spec.ts:490-492` records the OPPOSITE sample - five prompts in six save-then-Ctrl+N rounds on an unchanged starter. So at least one of the three is wrong, they disagree about product behaviour rather than wording, and nobody has measured which path differs (Ctrl+N against the menubar's New is the obvious candidate, and neither the session nor the specs distinguish them). WHY THE SPECS SURVIVE: `answerDialogIfShown` tolerates the absence of a dialog, so a spec asserting a prompt that never comes still passes - the tolerant call was the right one: the driver's absolute "asks nothing on the path every caller takes" is not what `reference-theme` observed. NOT FIXED HERE because establishing which claim is true needs a browser run per path, and the fix is to the claim rather than to behaviour. OWNER: whoever owns the editor's browser journeys (`tests/e2e/`) and the dirty-guard's own contract (`persistence-manager/`). TASK 2.4b, 2026-10-12: the runs are taken on the built preview at base 7f88dff3, and the fresh-starter half of the contradiction is settled against the two specs. The dialog read is [role=dialog] — Base UI portals a div, not a native dialog[open], which is why a first pass read nothing from every path. A fresh editor, Control+n then Create: the size chooser opens and NO replacement question follows. A fresh editor, File then New theme then Create: same. A fresh editor, File then Open package: no dialog at all, and the file chooser fires, which is the guard having passed. So on a fresh starter the guard asks nothing on any of the three paths, and author-journey-display.spec.ts:231-235 and composition-panel.spec.ts:556-558 — both of which state that the starter, being unedited, counts as unsaved work — carry a premise this run refutes. reference-theme.spec.ts's five-prompts-in-six sample is a save-then-Ctrl+N state, which this run did not reproduce either way; the cell's --grep New collects TWO cases and not one, because Playwright compiles the pattern as a case-insensitive regexp: the unpiped --list exits 0 with four entries, reference-theme.spec.ts:380 (a fresh document is the reference composition, and New never touches the saved one -- the case that presses Control+n) and :2444 (a new background image is imported, and the artboard is repointed at it), each under desktop-chromium and phone-chromium, so neither case presses the menubar's New and the menubar path stays measured here rather than by the cell. STAYS OPEN: the fix is a claim correction in two spec files outside this task's file list, and correcting one side of a two-sided contradiction would leave the register claiming a disagreement the tree no longer carries.

title: FontPicker has no production mount in any package, so its 379 lines and 984-line test are kept alive by tests alone while the live font surface is FontControls
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 4A PART II (2026-10-10, over 8c666ea1..9fa7b7b4). The implementer raised it as its own concern and the controller confirmed it independently. MEASURED at head 9fa7b7b4: `grep -rn 'FontPicker' packages/*/src` returns exactly two consumers, both tests - `packages/editor/src/ui-copy.test.ts:19,238` (which mounts it because a copy literal inside it would otherwise be invisible to the copy audit) and `packages/editor/src/font-picker/font-picker.dom.test.tsx`. No production module in any package renders it and it is not in the editor's barrel, so nothing a user can reach shows this component. THE LIVE SURFACE IS A DIFFERENT ONE: `packages/editor/src/panes/tokens/preset-list.tsx`'s `FontControls` owns the font controls an author actually uses, and it was already on `ControlSelect` before this task - plan 4 converted it. So the product's zero-native-select outcome did not depend on this file. WHY IT STILL MATTERED, AND WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN NOTHING: the three native `<select>`s at `font-picker.tsx:233,260,279` were the last in the editor's source, so converting them is what makes the census true (`grep -rnE '<select|type="range"' packages/editor/src` now returns comments only, zero non-comment production hits) - but the conversion touched ~155 source lines and ~253 test lines of a surface no user reaches, and the 984-line test file now exceeds the repo's 800-line stop keeping a dead component alive. The census is honest; the maintenance cost is not addressed by it. DECISION NEEDED, which is why this is not a one-line fix: either delete `FontPicker` and its test (and then `ui-copy.test.ts`'s mount of it, which exists only because it carries copy), or wire it to the surface it was written for - and nobody has established which. The archived font-catalogue plan is the likeliest origin. OWNER: whoever owns `font-picker/` and the Tokens pane's font controls.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, on the same question as vg-268 and taken ONCE for both rows: WIRE FontPicker TO THE SURFACE IT WAS WRITTEN FOR. The ruling and its reasoning live on vg-268; this row is marked because the two rows file one question. ui-copy.test.ts's mount of the control follows its own row rather than this one.

CITATIONS CORRECTED 2026-10-16 (§8.9). The line numbers are **dropped rather than re-pointed**, because a source file this row's subject keeps being converted in cannot hold a stable line: the symbols the sentence already names — `FontControls` and `ControlSelect` in `panes/tokens/preset-list.tsx` — are the citation, and a fresh number would re-arm the same rot. **A clause here was wrong and is corrected 2026-10-16**: it read the plan's `357` → `379` as stale, but that number is this file's *length* and `font-picker.tsx` is exactly 379 lines; the third value belonged to `FontControls`' line *position* in `preset-list.tsx` (declared at 332, mounted at 346), which is a different measurement. The plan's replacement was right. COLLAPSED 2026-10-16 (§8.3). This row and `vg-268` file one question — FontPicker is mounted by tests and by no product surface — and the controller ruled it ONCE, on 2026-10-12, with the ruling and its reasoning recorded on `vg-268`. This row is marked rather than re-asked, and neither closes without the other. **§8.9's count correction is applied here**: the title's `357` was the file's length at filing and `font-picker.tsx` is now 379 lines, measured 2026-10-16, while the test is unchanged at 984.

title: A browser run at playwright.config.ts's default worker count reports 30s locator timeouts as failures at a clean HEAD, on this box
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 5 (commit 4698f233), while taking a browser baseline at 7d31622c with nothing broken. The same four specs, same commit, same built bundle: 4 failed / 23 passed at the default 10 workers, every failure a 30s locator timeout or `no control matches [data-vigilia-palette-token]`; 27 passed at --workers=2. The four: keyboard.spec.ts:18 (locator.evaluate timeout), panel-labels.spec.ts:136 (locator.count timeout), panel-labels.spec.ts:208, shell-appearance.spec.ts:85 (locator.click waiting for visible/enabled/stable). CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED beyond "the machine": another session was busy on this box at the time (AGENTS.md, a long run holds the machine), and a single sample proves nothing about load or concurrency. It matters because a green suite read as red at the default worker count costs a false fix round: plan 5 Task 5's first browser baseline read exactly this way. ADJACENT ROW, DIFFERENT MECHANISM: vg-216 is two configs sharing test-results/ and deleting each other's traces; this is one run under load. What would settle it: run the same specs at 10 workers on an otherwise idle box, and if they still time out, bisect the worker count. CONTROLLER MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-11, WHICH NARROWS THE CAUSE RATHER THAN CONFIRMING THE ONE OFFERED: running the palette sweep (shell-appearance.spec.ts:97) ALONE at the default worker count, on an otherwise idle box at 7309eb1d, takes 8.6s and 8.5s in two consecutive runs, a whole run 12.1s - roughly 3.5x inside the 30s limit. So that test's own runtime is NOT what tips it over, and the most plausible inherent explanation is now falsified rather than merely untested. Plan 7 Task 2's fix round reported the same test timing out at 30,722ms with durations of 26.8s, 28.2s and 33.3s, and those figures did NOT reproduce: they were taken while this session was itself running Playwright against the same built bundle, which is exactly the contention this row's first paragraph names. The cause is therefore CONCURRENT BROWSER RUNS ON ONE BOX AND ONE BUNDLE, and two things follow - a red at the default count is worth nothing until the spec is re-run alone at the same commit (AGENTS.md already asks this, and this is the measurement that makes it cheap to obey), and raising this spec's timeout would not fix it, because on an idle box there is nothing to fix. TASK 2.3B'S READING ON AN IDLE BOX, 2026-10-12, WHICH IS THE GATE THIS ROW NAMES: the same three files (`shell-appearance.spec.ts`, `panel-labels.spec.ts`, `keyboard.spec.ts`) on the same built bundle, with no other suite, build or browser driving it, FAILED at `--workers=10` - this box's default, its 20 logical cores halved, which is what the absent `workers` key in `playwright.config.ts` leaves in force. 4 of the 19 desktop-chromium cases were unexpected, every one a `Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded` reading 30.7-34.1s: the keyboard modal-trap row, `no control is unnamed`, the palette sweep and the treatment-boundary row. THE FINDING REPRODUCES, so the three timeouts this row already carried are the same shape rather than another session's artifact. BISECT, same three files and the same built bundle on the same idle box, one count per run: 8 workers 3 failed (33.4s, 33.2s, 30.8s), 6 workers 1 failed (the keyboard trap, 31.4s), 5 workers none failed (19 passed, 19 skipped, 59.5s, reproducing the dead attempt's reading). Every failure sits 1-14% over the 30s limit, so the count is a load threshold on this box rather than a stable boundary, and the threshold is in the worker count rather than in one spec: this row's own controller measurement had the palette sweep at 8.6s alone, and it reads 34.1s here. THE CLAUSE THE READING FALSIFIES: the sentence above saying raising a timeout would not fix it because on an idle box there is nothing to fix is half wrong - the idle box DOES redden at the default count - so what remains is a decision about which count this suite is run at here, and a decision rather than a patch because `playwright.config.ts`'s own comment defends leaving `workers` to the default (a hardcoded count oversubscribes a small CI runner). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT NOW: that decision, on this line - pin a count for this box, or accept the default and re-run the named spec alone at the same commit before believing a red. ONE CAVEAT ON THE LIST ABOVE, which this row does not otherwise carry: the treatment-boundary row IS one of the four, and Task 2.3b rewrote that row's own setup in the very commit that took this reading -- its member sets are now derived from the stylesheet rather than named. So the row does not claim the derivation is innocent of those four reds. What rules it out is arithmetic rather than a measurement: one extra `page.evaluate` per test rather than per palette, per-palette work unchanged, and the arm reading 12.2 s alone against a 30 s limit. One sample of that arm alone at 10 workers on the BASE commit would settle it, and no such sample was taken.

title: Nothing detects a committed capture that a later plan invalidates, so the shell-palette and keyboard-reference images sat two plans stale
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 6 (commit b602dd13), by reading the images it was about to re-capture rather than by any test. The seven files committed until then under docs/evidence/screenshots/ (shell-palette-* x6 and keyboard-reference) were pictures of the PRE-PLAN-2 shell: no rail, a `Layers | Insert | Assets | Document` pane bar, a palette chip in the header, `Save package`. Plan 2 rebuilt all of that, and nothing noticed, because a capture is only ever refreshed by the action that owns it running again — and every registry in docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md and docs/design/mockups/README.md names an action and a file, never a surface version or a plan that produced it. Re-captured here against rebuilt bundles. CONSEQUENCE: visual evidence in the repo can contradict the product for an arbitrary number of plans while every gate stays green, which is the opposite of what spec §13 asks a capture to be. NOT FIXED HERE: the fix is a detection mechanism (a marker recording the commit or shell generation each image was taken against, checked by a gate, or an ownership link from a surface to its captures), which is design work no active plan owns. What would settle it: decide who owns a capture's freshness and express it as a check rather than as a habit.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. THE REGISTRY OWNS A CAPTURES FRESHNESS, AND THE CHECK IS A RECORDED SHA AGAINST THE SURFACE IT DEPICTS. Each registered capture records the commit it was taken at and the surface paths it shows; a script reports a capture whose surface paths have commits after that sha, so a stale image is a finding rather than a habit. Today both READMEs name an action and a file and nothing about the product generation, which is why the shell-palette and keyboard-reference images could contradict the product for two plans with every gate green. COST IF WRONG: a new scanner and a manifest to maintain, and a capture whose surface paths are wrong is reported stale for the wrong reason -- which is visible and fixable, unlike the present silence.

title: ACTION_BUTTON is declared three times, one class string drifting across the three converted dialogs
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5'S WHOLE-BRANCH FINAL REVIEW, by reading the branch (opus, range 13370dc5..95a9bd11), and confirmed at source: the same class-name constant is declared in packages/editor/src/new-document-chooser.tsx:42, packages/editor/src/persistence-manager/replace-document-prompt.tsx:14 and packages/editor/src/theme-library-dialog.tsx:43, and used at new-document-chooser.tsx:253,261, replace-document-prompt.tsx:56 and theme-library-dialog.tsx:181,194,202,237. All three files are Task 4a's own output, so this is one concept with three owners the moment the second copy was written, and the review found them ALREADY DRIFTING. CONSEQUENCE: the dialog family's action button can diverge in treatment without any test noticing, which is exactly the drift the control set exists to prevent; it is also the shape AGENTS.md's one-owner rule names. NOT FIXED IN THE PLAN'S FINAL FIX ROUND because where the single declaration belongs is a decision (a new components/ui module, or the shared dialog primitive) and plan 6 (2026-10-08-iconography-and-copy) owns the single-owner census over the surfaces plans 1-5 landed. What would settle it: name the owner and import from it in all three, then delete the other two declarations.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. THE SHARED DIALOG PRIMITIVE OWNS ACTION_BUTTON. It is already declared in dialog.tsx:43, every one of the three dialogs already imports that primitive, and the three declarations were already drifting -- so the fix is that new-document-chooser.tsx:253,261, replace-document-prompt.tsx:56 and theme-library-dialog.tsx:181,194,202,237 import it and their own copies are deleted. A new components/ui module was rejected because the primitive that every consumer already depends on is the owner it already has. COST IF WRONG: the token sits beside the primitive rather than in a neutral module, which is a move, not a redesign.

title: RESERVED_LETTERS refuses a bare-modifier chord but not its Shift variant, so Ctrl+Shift+T, N and W are accepted as bindings and can never fire
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5'S WHOLE-BRANCH FINAL REVIEW, range 13370dc5..95a9bd11, and confirmed at source. shortcut-manager/bindings.ts:75 lists the reserved letters (l, n, p, q, r, t, w) and :299-305 refuses one only when `binding.modifier && binding.shift !== true`, so every Shift variant of those letters passes validation and is stored as a binding the browser owns: Ctrl+Shift+T (reopen closed tab), Ctrl+Shift+N (new private window) and Ctrl+Shift+W (close window) are taken in every Chromium build, so the author binds a chord and nothing ever happens. The rule's own doc comment states the Shift exclusion as fact without stating why, which is the claim-without-a-reason shape this plan hit repeatedly. CONSEQUENCE: the refusal exists precisely so the author is told where the limit is rather than binding a chord that will never fire, and it does not cover the case that is most likely to be tried. NOT FIXED IN THE PLAN'S FINAL FIX ROUND because the correct membership is a data decision - which chords the editor's actual browser matrix reserves - and over-refusing is its own defect (it would reject chords that do work). What would settle it: state which browsers the editor runs in, measure the Shift variants against them, and make the reserved rule and its comment reflect that evidence.

RULED 2026-10-12: A DEFECT, and the Shift exclusion is backwards: three of the four chords most likely to be tried are exactly the Shift variants the browser keeps, so the rule misses the case its own comment says it exists to catch. The rule becomes TWO sets rather than one guarded by `shift !== true` — the letters reserved with a modifier and no Shift, unchanged, and the letters whose SHIFT variant is reserved too — because the blanket exclusion was never a measurement, it was an assumption that Shift makes a chord safe. Membership is measured, not guessed: the starting evidence is Chromium's documented page-unreachable accelerators, Ctrl+Shift+N (new private window), Ctrl+Shift+R (reload ignoring cache), Ctrl+Shift+T (reopen closed tab) and Ctrl+Shift+W (close window), and Firefox is checked against them, because the host opens the editor in the author's own browser rather than one this repo chooses. The comment carries the browser and the date it was measured against — a reserved set with no provenance is the claim-without-a-reason shape this row already names. The `ponytail:` note stays: a longer list, or a key-capture API, is still the upgrade path.

title: The drawings invent the treatment of two controls no original draws - the segmented control and the in-button chord - so a surface the product has is given a gold target that no normative source states
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 9'S TASK REVIEW (2026-10-10), reviewing commit 5773f652 against the user's ruling that the original mockup style is the gold target while the content is corrected to the product. THE GAP: `docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html` and `shell.html` draw two surfaces that no original draws and that the bible's closed control vocabulary does not name - the segmented control (Left/Centre/Right, Top/Middle/Bottom; the product's `control-segmented.tsx`) and the chord drawn INSIDE the publish trigger (the product renders `<kbd class="editor-shell-primary-key">` as a child of the trigger at `publish-control.tsx:145`, where the original drew a standalone chip). The drawings are right that the surfaces exist - that is content, and the user's ruling puts content on the product's side - but their **treatment** is invented by extending the well idiom, and treatment is the half the user ruled is gold. CONSEQUENCE: the in-button chip's border is `#06131a59` in the drawing, about 35%, where the product composes `color-mix(currentColor 45%, transparent)` - a numeric drift between the drawing and the product that no `PARITY` row asserts, because no row reads either drawing today. Under spec section 13 as amended a deliberate difference must name a normative source that requires it, and there is none for a treatment nobody has ruled on. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the drawn treatment is what the original's author would have drawn, or the implementer's reasonable extension - the review found no original that draws either control, so the question cannot be answered from the drawings. FLAGGED AS MINOR BY THE REVIEW, and filed rather than fixed because the fix is a ruling on the treatment, not an edit. OWNED BY NO PLAN: plan 7 Task 8 makes the two control drawings read by a test (its Step 1 adds the PARITY rows), which is what would catch the drift once the treatment is settled.
