title: The derived-palette ladder is asserted as order only, so a palette whose three surface rungs collapse to steps of 0.0001 keeps its ordering and passes every assertion
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 4 OF THE SHELL-PARITY PLAN (2026-10-11) IN ITS OWN DELIVERABLE, reviewing `a3d2c407` at `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/task-4-review.md` finding 4. MEASURED BY READING THE ASSERTION: `design-language.spec.ts`'s derivation case compares `--bg`/`--panel`/`--panel-2` by luminance ordering (`bg < panel <= panel2`), which is what the plan's Step 5 asked for - "the luminance ordering ... matches graphite's" - and the plan's Step 3 asks for more: "takes from graphite the relationships between roles: the luminance separation". A palette whose three surfaces sit 0.0001 apart satisfies the ordering and shares nothing of the separation, so the assertion that exists to keep six transcribed value sets from drifting apart cannot see a collapse. TASK 4's FIX ROUND TIGHTENS WHAT CAN BE STATED WITHOUT INVENTING A NUMBER: strict `bg < panel < panel2` for the five derived palettes, editorial's equal `panel`/`panel-2` named as the one licensed exception. What is left is the magnitude, and that is why this is a row rather than a constant: a floor of "at least X luminance" has no rule behind it in the bible, and picking one is the move this plan has already had to undo once (the `designLanguagePx` allowlist entry added to make a gate pass, R25). NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a magnitude floor is worth having at all, since a derivation is re-derived rather than edited, or whether the bible should state a minimum surface separation - section 4 gives the roles and no spacing between them. What would settle it: a bible rule naming the minimum separation between a ground and the panel above it, and then an assertion reading it. PLAN 7 TASK 6 SEARCHED FOR THE RULE AND FOUND NONE (2026-10-11). Read, and this is the search rather than the conclusion: section 3 (`design-language.md:64-109`, the spacing, radius and elevation tables) states no surface separation; section 4 (`:111-140`, the role table) gives the roles and no relationship between `--bg`, `--panel` and `--panel-2`; section 5 (`:141-206`) gives contrast ratios only (3:1, 4.5:1), which bind a boundary against its ground rather than the distance between two grounds; the drawing (`current/shell.html:17-18`) declares three literals with no stated relationship. No constant was added and this row stays open, because a magnitude floor with no rule behind it is the `designLanguagePx` move (R25) this plan has already had to undo once.

READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174; the venue is `design-language.spec.ts`, and the magnitudes are read off the live `:root` custom properties resolved through an element): the ordering case passes (`graphite's roles are the drawing's, and the other five keep its ladder`, 3404ms), and the magnitude the row asks about, measured as WCAG relative luminance, spans 40x across the five palettes that can be measured. panel minus bg / panel2 minus panel, with the three luminances: graphite 0.0036 / 0.0035 (L 0.0043, 0.0079, 0.0113); ember 0.1454 / 0.0581 (0.6428, 0.7882, 0.8463); moss 0.1307 / 0.0680 (0.7016, 0.8324, 0.9003); plum 0.1438 / 0.0652 (0.6511, 0.7949, 0.8601); editorial 0.1008 / 0.0000 (0.8815, 0.9823, 0.9823 - the licensed equal pair). light's `--bg` is `linear-gradient(145deg, #d8ebe4, #afd4d1)` and has no single luminance, so its bg rung is unmeasured here rather than estimated; its declared surfaces are `#eff9f2bf` and `#f8fffbdf`, both carrying alpha. A magnitude floor would bind graphite first: a threshold above 0.0036 reds it. RULED 2026-10-14: ASSERT THE VALUES. The three surface rungs are asserted against what the derivation produces rather than against each other's order, so a palette whose rungs collapse to steps of 0.0001 fails because the value is wrong rather than because it crossed a threshold — no magnitude floor is introduced, and the reason is measured: a floor above graphite's 0.0036 / 0.0035 would red the tightest legitimate palette, so a floor would need a per-palette constant and would still only catch collapse by accident. The values are available to assert because the derivation is the owner: the assertion reads the produced rungs, not a hand-copied table.

title: light is the one palette whose chrome is still translucent, so "chrome is opaque" holds in five of six palettes and light composites against a gradient ground
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 5 (2026-10-11) while making the chrome opaque, and reported to the controller as the brief asked rather than settled here: "where a palette's chrome has no derivation to read that is a finding for me, not a literal invented here". MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER after the change, reading `getComputedStyle().backgroundColor` on `.editor-shell-rail`: editorial `rgb(255,253,247)`, graphite `rgb(18,22,28)`, ember `rgb(247,226,210)`, moss `rgb(228,239,217)`, plum `rgb(236,227,247)` - all opaque - and light `rgba(239,249,242,0.75)`. CAUSE ESTABLISHED: `.editor-glass` now paints the palette's own `var(--panel)`, and light is the only palette whose surface roles carry alpha at all - `--shell-surface: #eff9f2bf` and `--shell-surface-strong: #f8fffbdf` - while its `--shell-backdrop` is the set's only gradient, so no role light declares is an opaque surface and plan 7 Task 4's derivation (graphite's relationships: the luminance ladder, the edge's weight against its surface) produces none. It is not expressible in CSS either: deriving the composite needs `color-mix` over `--shell-backdrop`, which is a gradient and is invalid inside `color-mix`. CONSEQUENCE: the rail, both panes, the inspector and the header each composite 25% of the mint gradient behind them, so light's chrome contrast is not one composited value and its boundary ratio (measured 1.40:1, `vg-200`'s pin) moves with the ground. The treatment assertion in `shell-appearance.spec.ts` names light as its one exemption and reads the translucency it carries, so a value that lands reds the gate and the exemption has to be deleted rather than left to excuse a regression. NOT FIXED IN TASK 5: choosing an opaque light surface is a palette value decision, and the task that owns the derivation is the one that should make it.

READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174; the venue is `shell-appearance.spec.ts`, and the surfaces are `.editor-shell-rail`'s computed background per palette): five rails are opaque - editorial rgb(255, 253, 247), graphite rgb(18, 22, 28), ember rgb(247, 226, 210), moss rgb(228, 239, 217), plum rgb(236, 227, 247) - and light is rgba(239, 249, 242, 0.75), the field the browser reports for the declared `#eff9f2bf` surface, over the set's only gradient ground (light `--bg` = linear-gradient(145deg, #d8ebe4, #afd4d1)). No value moved. The treatment case is green in the same run (`chrome is flat and opaque, and the canvas clusters keep the glass`, 11894ms). RULED 2026-10-14: MAKE LIGHT OPAQUE. Light gains a declared opaque surface — the mint gradient composited into one value, measured from the composite the rail, both panes, the inspector and the header each produce today (25 percent of the gradient behind them) — so "chrome is opaque" holds in six of six palettes and light's boundary ratio stops moving with the ground under it. `shell-appearance.spec.ts`'s light exemption is then deleted rather than left in place to excuse a regression, which the row says is what the exemption becomes if a value lands. The new value is derived and measured rather than picked, because the derivation is the owner and the row's cause is that light had no derivation to read.

What would settle it: a ruling on whether a per-palette flat flag is wanted at all (the treatment is selector-driven today), and if not, the two declarations and the `NOT_A_COLOUR` entry deleted in one commit.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller as a code/architecture correctness question: THE TOKEN GOES. --shell-flat's two declarations (editor-shell.css) and its NOT_A_COLOUR entry (editor-shell.tokens.test.ts:398, with the prose at :78) are deleted in one commit. It is not one of ADR-0040's three roles declared ahead of a consumer on the user's instruction -- those are named and this is not among them -- and the flat treatment is selector-driven after Task 5, so a per-palette flag no var() reads is a knob that lies: changing it moves nothing and fails nothing. COST IF WRONG: a future per-palette flat flag is a one-line declaration plus its consumer, which is what the pattern would need anyway.

title: `current/shell.html` draws no Add-pane asset preview, so the surface the product renders at `file-section.tsx:189` is one no gate can check
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 7 (2026-10-11, as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `7efea17f`) and adjudicated by its task review rather than left as the implementer's observation. MEASURED: `current/shell.html:128-140` draws the Add pane's Asset group as a select, then `Import a file`, then Replace/Remove, and a case-insensitive search for `preview` in that file returns nothing, while the product renders an `img.vigilia-asset-preview` carrying `data-vigilia-asset-preview` at `panes/add/file-section.tsx:189-194`, styled at `editor-shell.css:1107`, and both `editor-shell-add-desktop-chromium.png` and `pane-add-desktop-chromium.png` show it. THE DRAWING HALF IS DISCHARGED (2026-10-11, artefact 221bf1a1, Task 7 fix round 1): `current/shell.html` now draws the preview well between the Asset select and the `Import a file` row, in the drawing's own idiom, with the class it stands for named in a comment beside it - `height:120px;aspect-ratio:1672/941` taken from a live measurement of `[data-vigilia-asset-preview]` on the built bundle (213.3x120 at the pane content's left edge, flush under the select), and a gradient standing in for the chosen picture. The frozen original is untouched and nothing was renumbered. The parity table re-ran green with the drawing changed and no row's answer moved (9 passed at `--workers=1`, re-run by the controller against `design-language.spec.ts` rather than taken from the report). WHAT REMAINS, AND WHY THIS ROW STAYS OPEN: the title's second clause is untouched - a surface the drawing omits is still one no gate can check. No reader row was built, and the reason is measured rather than laziness: the product's contract is `max-height:120px` with `object-fit:contain`, a bound and not a size, and the Add pane is `display:none` while Document is open, so a row would read no element. This class - a drawing that omits a surface the product renders - needs a surface-inventory check and belongs to `vg-304`'s family; the row stays open as that family's member rather than closing on the half that was repaired. REOPENED 2026-10-12 BY TASK 2.3a OF THE BACKLOG-DRAIN PLAN, on review: a close in this task was reverted rather than defended. THE INSTRUMENT EXISTS AND IS GREEN, AND IT STILL CANNOT CARRY A `verified`. What it proves: the surface this row names is named on all three sides — the component that renders it (`img.vigilia-asset-preview` carrying `data-vigilia-asset-preview`), the `editor-shell.css` rule that treats it, and `current/shell.html`, which draws the box beside the name. What it cannot prove, and this IS the class the row exists for: the list of surfaces it reads is HAND-WRITTEN AND ONE ENTRY LONG, so a product surface that is not on the list reddens nothing — the instrument re-asserts the one surface already found and cannot discover the next. AND THE DRAWING SIDE READS A NAME, NOT A DRAWN ELEMENT: the drawn box at `current/shell.html:134` is an anonymous inline-styled div with no class and no hook, so that side is satisfied by the `<!-- asset preview (.vigilia-asset-preview) ... -->` comment at `:133` — delete the drawn box and leave the comment and the instrument stays green. DERIVING THE SET FROM THE PRODUCT WAS MEASURED AND DOES NOT CONSTRUCT: the panes render 73 distinct `data-vigilia-*` hooks, 5 of them named anywhere in `editor-shell.css`, and NO checked drawing names any of them — the drawings are hand-authored HTML that names a product surface by its class, in prose beside the box, never by a hook on a drawn element. Measured 2026-10-12 by walking `src/web/packages/editor/src/panes/**/*.tsx` and testing each hook against the stylesheet and the six checked drawings; a derivation that required the drawing to name every hook would red the suite at 73 entries — or at 5, scoped to the hooks the stylesheet names — with no way to satisfy any of them. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an enumeration of the product's surfaces that the drawings can be held to — either the drawings gain a mechanical way to name a product surface, or a product-side registry of surfaces exists for the drawings to be checked against. The §8.11 path correction and the §8.2 line correction recorded above still stand and are unaffected: the surface is `src/web/packages/editor/src/panes/add/file-section.tsx:192-193`, and the `.vigilia-asset-preview` rule is `editor-shell.css:1229`.

title: Shipped source cites a plan's git-ignored execution state, so the citation points at a file no clone has
detail:
FOUND WHILE CLOSING PLAN 7 (2026-10-11, as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `0c6a17c0`). MEASURED: `src/web/tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:494` introduces the `PARITY` table with "The shell's regions, as the census adjudicates them (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/adjudication.md`)" - a path inside `.superpowers/sdd/`, which the repo's own plan README (`docs/superpowers/plans/README.md:7`) calls "ignored execution state", and which the subagent-driven-development skill deletes when a plan's final review comes back clean. So the citation names a file no clone has, and the census it points at (the region-by-region adjudication every `PARITY` row's licence and disposition comes from) has no durable home. THE CONVENTION IS ALREADY IN USE IN TRACKED DOCS, which is why this is a question rather than a one-line fix: `.github/bug-player-chart-throw.md:123`, `docs/decisions/0003-authored-text-box-outlives-the-text.md:186` and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-dashboard-authoring-design.md:605` each cite a different `.superpowers/sdd/` workspace the same way, and `docs/decisions/0003` is an accepted ADR, so the pattern predates this file. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the right answer is to keep the workspace (the plan's evidence then outlives the plan, at the cost of a git-ignored directory nothing prunes), to move a census worth keeping under `docs/evidence/` when the plan closes, or to treat the citation as provenance that a reader is expected to reconstruct from the archived plan plus the register. The third is the cheapest and is what the other three sites already rely on; the second is the only one that makes the claim checkable. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a user ruling on where a closed plan's evidence lives, since this decides whether the census a parity gate argues from is reviewable by anyone but the session that wrote it. Owned by whoever closes the next plan, not by plan 7, which is closed. RULED 2026-10-14: PROVENANCE ONLY. A citation into a plan's git-ignored execution state is provenance a reader reconstructs from the archived plan plus the register, which is what the other three sites already rely on — no closing step is added and nothing is moved under `docs/evidence/`. The cost is accepted explicitly: a citation of that kind is not checkable by a fresh clone, and the rule is that a claim needing to be checkable cites something else.

SECTION 8.7's REPLACEMENT IS NOT APPLIED, because it cannot be verified and the number is the wrong instrument. The plan orders this row's count corrected to "six tracked `.superpowers/sdd/` citations, not four"; **the row itself names four sites as a census it took by hand** — `mockup-values.ts`, `.github/bug-player-chart-throw.md`, `docs/decisions/0003`, and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-dashboard-authoring-design.md` — and each is a different workspace. A grep for the string across tracked files returns **25**, but that measures something else entirely: files that *mention* `.superpowers/sdd` (this plan, `AGENTS.md`, `check-status.mjs`, the register itself) rather than documents citing an ignored workspace as evidence for a claim. **Neither number is the row's number, and the count is what rots**: what this row is about is a *capability* — a tracked doc can point at execution state no clone carries, and the census such a pointer leans on then has no durable home — so the sites are named and no total is asserted. The row's own question is unaffected and still open.

title: Section 3's row-density rhythm is read by no gate: the drawings gate holds spacing to the step list and never to the 26/30/32 rule, which is where 75 corrected well insets would have shown

IT IS NOT vg-320, which is a drawing measured against the frozen original; this is a drawing measured against a written rule no arm reads. STILL OPEN AFTER TASK 2.3a OF THE BACKLOG-DRAIN PLAN (2026-10-12). The arm the row wants was attempted and not landed, and the reason is a measurement rather than a shortage of effort: §3's row rhythm is 26/30/32 and the product expresses it through `ControlWell`'s `WELL_HEIGHT`/`ROW_MIN_HEIGHT` density tables, but **no caller in the workspace passes `density="dialog"` or `density="settings"`** — every call site takes the default — so nothing renders at 30px for an arm to read, and a rendered arm built on the densities that do render would assert one number three times, which is the shape `vg-233`'s first pass closed on and the review refused. What the run established: the drawings gate is green over all six checked drawings with the field row at 26px in a panel reading its rhythm, and the deliberate decision §3 makes (26/30/32 are densities, not gutters, and are `design-tokens.mjs`'s `SPACING_PROPERTY` comment's reason for excluding them from the step list) still holds. What would close it: a rendered arm with a comparator for a surface's density, which needs at least one surface to render at the dialog density first. ONE CLAUSE CORRECTED 2026-10-13. This row reads the drawings' `font` shorthand as setting no line-height, which is true of the element rules and not of the files: the page furniture does state one - `settings-about.html:10`'s `font: 12px/1.45` on the page body, inherited by every drawn element - so a drawn row is not metric-dependent at the inherited ratio, only where an element overrides the size and keeps it. The ratio itself is off section 2's scale and is filed as `vg-440`; this row's subject, section 3's density rule (26/30/32) and the well-height disagreement it hides, is unchanged.

title: Settings is a modal today and the user has ruled it should be a pane like Add and Composition, opened from the rail's gear, with the settings drawing redrawn as a panel
detail:
FOUND BY THE USER (2026-10-11), reading the current mockup capture, in answer to the modal width question this round put to them: 'Setting should not be a modal but a panel like add, composition.' Three further sub-rulings came with it, each asked with a recommendation and each answered as recommended. PARKED BY THE USER (2026-10-11): 'Let's park the settings becomes a pane spec.' The row stays OPEN and nothing is queued against it; the sequencing sub-ruling above is unchanged, and what it invalidates stays invalidated until a spec is written. RULED 2026-10-14: UNPARKED. Two rows whose subjects this invalidates are to be revisited inside that spec rather than before it: `vg-318`'s scrim measurement measures a container that will not exist, and `vg-322`'s whole subject is the modal's width. RULED 2026-10-15 (two answers this spec inherits): **THE THREE TAB HEADINGS BECOME A VERTICAL LIST inside the pane** — a pane holds a list that the fixed 560px modal could not, and the shell already has list chrome to draw it with, so the pane is not the modal with a different frame. **AND THE PANE'S NAME IS `Editor Settings`,** which the pane's own header carries in both the redrawn `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html` and the product. `vg-328` is the ruling this inherits: the pane's header names the surface, so one name covers the gear, the pane and the drawing.

title: The palettes carry one accent and the user has asked for a second highlight, orange for graphite, whose role is an attention or in-flight state and must be defined before any colour is chosen
detail: FOUND BY THE USER (2026-10-11), looking at the current mockup capture: 'graphite needs another highlight/accent color, like orange, on top of the current pallete (other themes to follow once we define the role of this color).' THE ROLE WAS ASKED AND ANSWERED FIRST, because a colour chosen before its job is a colour that will be used for the wrong thing: it is an ATTENTION or IN-FLIGHT STATE -- something that is neither the primary action nor destructive, such as unsaved or unpublished changes, a reading that is stale or awaiting the author, or a pending operation. Two alternatives were offered and declined: a second colour for emphasis with no state meaning, and re-hueing graphite's existing --shell-accent to orange instead of adding a role. WHAT THE ROLE REQUIRES BEFORE ANY HEX IS PICKED, and each is a decision rather than a lookup: a name that says the JOB and not the hue (--attention, not --orange); a bible section 4 clause saying when it may appear, since section 4 already rations --accent to at most one accent-filled element visible and a second colour with no stated job is exactly the competition that rationing exists to prevent; and a rule keeping it off the same element as --accent, so the two can never both claim a surface. IT IS NOT GRAPHITE'S ALONE: the user's own framing is that the role is defined once and the other five themes follow, so the output is a section 4 role plus a per-palette value in each of the six, not a graphite-only token. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the section 4 clause and the six values, which is spec work rather than a task, together with whatever gate reads a state colour -- the contrast instrument measures text and boundaries and has no state-colour row today. RELATED: `vg-330` is the other change the user asked for in the same sitting, and both are sequenced after plan 6.

title: The colour picker's four track sliders announce their test id, so a screen reader reads out a CSS-selector-shaped token instead of a word
detail:
SURFACED BY PLAN 6 TASK 5'S REVIEW (2026-10-11) while adjudicating the copy walk's skip rule, and it is THE ROW `vg-194` HANDED OFF AND NOBODY FILED: that verified row's own closing paragraph ends 'each track's `aria-label` is its `testId`, so what a screen reader announces is `picker-saturation, slider, 0`, and the words an author would want are a copy decision rather than a mechanism one. That is a separate row, not a reopening of this one.' This is that row; the mechanism half `vg-194` owned is done and is not re-opened by it. THE MEASUREMENT: `components/ui/colour-picker.tsx`'s `Track` renders `aria-label={testId}`, so each of the four tracks (the saturation/brightness area, hue, and the two strips) has an accessible name of `picker-saturation`, `picker-hue` and so on -- a token shaped like a selector rather than a word. `vg-194` closed the keyboard path and the declared `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` in the same component, so the value announcement is sound; what a person hears first is the name, and the name is the defect. WHY THE COPY WALK DOES NOT CATCH IT, which is the part worth recording: the walk's rule skips any element whose `aria-label` equals its `data-testid`, and the reviewer ruled that rule CORRECT -- a driver's hook is not a word a translator would change, and forcing these into `uiCopy` would be wrong. So the net is right to skip them and the label is still wrong: the two facts are independent, and the skip rule must not be weakened to catch this. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: each track's `aria-label` reads a word from `uiCopy` (`Saturation`, `Hue`, `Alpha`, `Value`) while the `data-testid` hooks keep their current values, so the skip rule stays and the announced name becomes a word. The wording is a copy decision, which is why it is not an agent's to take silently. RELATED: `vg-194` (verified, archived) is the row that identified this and deferred it; `vg-179` is an unrelated picker row.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. THE FOUR PICKER TRACKS ANNOUNCE Saturation, Hue, Alpha AND Value FROM uiCopy, and they keep their current data-testid hooks so the specs that address them do not move. The reasoning is vg-264s: user-visible strings come from the copy owner, and an accessible name is user-visible text. COST IF WRONG: four strings move into the copy catalogue and the census grows by four keys, which is what that census is for.

title: The one control that renders a chart setting descriptor has no production caller, and its module doc names a consumer that does not exist
detail:
FOUND BY the final whole-branch review of plan 6, which recorded it as out of that plan's range; it is not a plan-6 finding. `settingsField()` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/controls/settings-field.ts` has ZERO production callers: read in node across `src/web` (dist excluded), all twelve of its call sites are tests - one in `copy-defects.test.ts:138` and eleven in `controls.dom.test.ts`. Its module doc at `settings-field.ts:13-14` reads "The inspector's per-kind column mounts that same rendering, so the loop is this control rather than a second copy of it". The call sites were removed deliberately, not lost: `f254259b` (2026-10-06) added the file, then `4dc220c6` (2026-10-09) - "a chart's fields are React views, not DOM", plan 3 Task 3a - turned `chart-manager/panel.ts`'s descriptor loop into a view-model projection, and `settingsField` has had no production caller since. `SettingsFieldDescriptor` is referenced in production only by `settings-field.ts` itself and its owner `renderer-core/src/charts/settings-fields.ts`. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED for the doc half: whether the inspector's per-kind column was meant to be migrated to this control and never was, or renders descriptors by another route, the record does not settle, and this row does not guess which. Two fixes are possible and they are a design decision rather than a task: delete the now-unused control, or migrate the column to it. Checked for duplicates first: the archive's three `settings-field` mentions are `vg-145` (a gauge end angle), `vg-121` and `vg-122` (unreachable descriptor keys), and none owns this.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: MIGRATE THE INSPECTOR'S PER-KIND COLUMN TO IT. The module doc names a consumer that does not exist and the doc was right about the intent -- the column is re-pointed at settingsField rather than the control being deleted, so the descriptor route becomes the control's real caller. BLOCKED ON A CONFLICT WITH THE REDESIGN'S SETTLED ARCHITECTURE, FOUND 2026-10-13 BY THE CONTROLLER, WHILE LOOKING FOR THE NEXT UNBLOCKED PIECE OF THE REDESIGN'S SIXTEENTH ACCEPTANCE ITEM -- WHICH NAMES THIS ROW AS ONE OF THE `fix` DIFFERENCES THAT DISCHARGES IT, SO THE CONFLICT IS ON THE CRITICAL PATH RATHER THAN BESIDE IT. The ruling above directs that the inspector's per-kind column be re-pointed at `settingsField`. **Measured: `settingsField()` returns an `HTMLElement`**, built from `addEventListener`, `setAttribute` and DOM nodes (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/controls/settings-field.ts`), so re-pointing a React column at it puts an imperative DOM island inside that column -- which is exactly what the redesign's Acceptance forbids ("Every editor surface is React, including chart fields ... no imperative UI island survives under a React wrapper") and where ADR-0039 draws the boundary. `4dc220c6` (2026-10-09, "a chart's fields are React views, not DOM") is the commit that deliberately removed the call sites, so **the ruling as written reverses a decision the redesign was built on rather than restoring one**. The half of the ruling that has moved is its premise: it rests on the module doc's claim that "the inspector's per-kind column mounts that same rendering", and `4dc220c6` superseded that intent. **NOT TAKEN IN EITHER DIRECTION, DELIBERATELY.** Deleting the control for a React view is not what was ruled; re-pointing the column is what was ruled but contradicts the redesign's own acceptance clause. A controller's licence covers code and architecture correctness, not the reversal of a user's design ruling, so the two readings need the user's word. Task 6.5b declined this same close on 2026-10-13 for the adjacent reason (a rendered-surface rewrite that would reverse `4dc220c6`), and Phase 6's close recorded the row open rather than resolving it. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT:** either the ruling is re-read as "the descriptor route should have a **React** owner", which makes the work a control in `selection-inspector/` and lets `settings-field.ts` retire unused; or the imperative island is accepted on purpose, in which case the Acceptance section's React clause gains a named exemption beside ADR-0033's. Either answer is small; guessing it wrong is a rendered-surface rewrite in the wrong direction. RULED 2026-10-14: THE RULING IS RE-READ AS "THE DESCRIPTOR ROUTE SHOULD HAVE A **REACT** OWNER." The work is a control in `selection-inspector/` that renders the descriptor as React, `settings-field.ts` retires unused, and `4dc220c6`'s removals stay removed — ADR-0039's boundary holds because the new owner is React rather than the imperative island the earlier reading would have put in a React column. The Acceptance section's React clause therefore needs no exemption here. Cost if this reading is wrong: a rendered-surface rewrite in the wrong direction, which is exactly what the row waited for the word on.

RULED 2026-10-15: **THE DESCRIPTOR ROUTE GETS A REACT OWNER.** The work is a control in `selection-inspector/`, and `settings-field.ts` retires with it. This reverses `4dc220c6`. **One consequence stated so it is not rediscovered:** the sixteenth acceptance item's React clause therefore stands absolute and gains **no** named exemption — ADR-0033's exemption is not extended to this case, because the case is being fixed rather than licensed.

title: A chart's scalar settings are validated on neither path, so a v2 envelope carrying min above max, windowSeconds 0, or innerRadiusPercent above outerRadiusPercent is accepted
detail:
FOUND BY the review of ad94e5ed (finding 5), which asked the retirement report to stop justifying the deleted chart-content cases as coverage the Fabric half performs. It does not: fabric-envelope-validate.ts chartPaintReferences (line 513, called at line 96) reads a chart's settings for PAINT fields only - gauge track/progress, line stroke/area/palette, bar fill/track, pie remainderFill/palette - and its isRecord guard means a chart whose settings is not an object skips even those. WHAT WAS SEARCHED, so the negative can be judged rather than trusted: grep -rn for windowSeconds, maxPoints, innerRadiusPercent, outerRadiusPercent, min, max and total across src/web/packages/*/src and src/web/tests (excluding *.test.ts), plus schema/theme-document.schema.json. The only hits that touch these scalars are charts/settings-fields.ts (authoring bounds for the inspector, which ADR-0028 explicitly says must not become document validation), charts/line.ts and charts/pie.ts (render, where pie clamps via clampPercent and never refuses), data/store.ts and fake-source (Math.max(0, windowSeconds) floors the window rather than refusing it), and editor/src/preview-source.ts. schema/theme-document.schema.json carries no settings property at all, because a v2 scene is opaque Fabric JSON, so no JSON-Schema bound exists either. MEASURED, not inferred: calling validateFabricThemeEnvelope on a conforming envelope whose chart object carries gauge {min: 10, max: 1}, line {windowSeconds: 0}, line {maxPoints: -5}, pie {innerRadiusPercent: 80, outerRadiusPercent: 20}, pie {total: {kind: fixed, value: null}}, or settings: ["windowSeconds"] returns ok: true for all six. PRE-EXISTING, NOT CREATED BY THE RETIREMENT: the deleted v1 validator did own these (validate.ts validateSettingsRange required gauge/bar max > min, line windowSeconds and maxPoints above 0, pie outer above inner and a finite fixed total), but the v2 path never reached it - fabric-envelope-validate.ts called validateThemeDocument with a synthetic {schemaVersion: 1, nodes: []} document, so no node-level case ever ran against an envelope. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: whether a scalar chart bound is meant to be enforced at the envelope boundary (refuse) or recovered at render (clamp, as pie already does); if recovery is the intent, this closes as intended behaviour with the clamping owners named.

RULED 2026-10-12: REFUSE AT THE ENVELOPE BOUNDARY, and the range comes from the descriptor table rather than a second table written into the validator. `charts/settings-fields.ts` already owns each scalar setting and already carries its own `min` (windowSeconds 1, maxPoints 2, lineWidth and markerSize 0), so the validator READS that owner instead of re-deciding it — which is what the deleted v1 validator did, and deleting it removed the refusal without moving the ownership anywhere. The relational cases are the same rule one step out: Y `min` above `max`, and `innerRadiusPercent` at or above `outerRadiusPercent`, are a PAIR the family's own descriptor owns, so they are refused where the pair is complete rather than by a range on either half. `settings: ["windowSeconds"]` is the third shape of the same rule — the allowed key set is the descriptor table's own reading, not a list the validator keeps. The pie's render-time clamp STAYS, as defence for the in-memory path that never passes through the envelope, but it stops being the only thing between an impossible document and a drawing. A document whose saved numbers disagree with what is drawn is the authored-versus-derived split this repo forbids, and a clamp at render is exactly that disagreement made invisible.
check: NOT YET RUN - the case to add: validateFabricThemeEnvelope over a chart whose scalar settings are out of bounds (gauge min above max, line windowSeconds 0, pie innerRadiusPercent above outerRadiusPercent) must be refused. Measured today all three are accepted, so that case fails until a validator owns chart scalar settings.

title: The settings drawing light preview bar is the one bar no gate reads, because its ground is a gradient rather than a solid colour, so a wrong light ground passes every row
detail:
FOUND BY the task-1 review round of 2026-10-11 (finding 2, reviewed commit 6da1716a). THE RULING OPERATIVE SENTENCE IS NOW MET FOR FIVE OF SIX BARS: mockup-values.ts carries one colour row per solid-ground palette - editorial, graphite, ember, moss, plum - each reading a bar background-color in current/settings.html against the product .editor-shell-palette-swatch[data-shell-palette=...]. THE RESIDUAL IS light: its bar (current/settings.html:82) paints background:linear-gradient(145deg,#d8ebe4,#afd4d1), and no row reads it, so repainting it to any other gradient reddens nothing. WHY THAT IS NOT A GATE - the reason this is a row rather than a test: the five rows key on background-color, the light bar declares the background shorthand, lookup (mockup-values.ts:364) matches property names exactly and returns the drawing silence for a property it does not declare, colourValue (:514) answers null for a gradient, and a length comparator cannot read a colour - so a sixth row of the same shape would fail on a drawing that is currently correct. OWNER: whoever owns the drawing preview bar; the instrument is the mockup-values.ts comparator set. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either the light bar declares a solid background-color like the other five, in which case a sixth row is the same shape and the drawing becomes a worse depiction of a product whose light ground really is a gradient; or the reader grows a comparator that resolves a gradient first stop and compares it with the product --shell-backdrop, which needs a ruling on which stop of a multi-stop gradient is the ground. The second is the honest solve and is a decision, not a silent choice. NOT A DUPLICATE: vg-310 is light translucent chrome, and vg-321 (now withdrawn, archive) is the ruling this residual belongs to - its own detail already named light a backdrop gradient.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: THE LIGHT PALETTE'S BAR BECOMES A SOLID background-color LIKE THE OTHER FIVE. One ground per palette and one rule in the reader, so the drawing is corrected to the shape the other five already have rather than the parity reader growing a gradient comparator plus a ruling on which stop is the ground. This does not absorb vg-322, which still owns which role a palette preview ground bar depicts.

title: The §1–§10 marker range is a shared namespace, so rule 3 accepts a bare §N from another document's numbering as a claim on a DESIGN.md marker
detail:
FOUND BY the Task 2 review (2026-10-11, reviewed commit 127ff808), finding 1, filed rather than fixed. WHAT: scripts/design-md.mjs's citation rule 3 asserts that every `<!-- §N -->` marker in DESIGN.md is claimed by at least one citation, but its claim test is a bare text match over `docs/`, `src/` and `scripts/` with no notion of which document is speaking, and §1–§10 is a shared namespace. docs/product/requirements.md marks its own requirements `## §N — title` and carries a bare §7 (requirements.md:20, the Product and scope heading); docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-editor-design-language-design.md numbers itself §1–§13. So an in-range §N from another document satisfies rule 3 for a DESIGN.md marker that nothing has actually cited. FAILURE SHAPE: if DESIGN.md's §7 marker's genuine citations were later removed, requirements.md's own §7 heading would keep rule 3 silent — the check would pass while the marker went unclaimed. DORMANT TODAY: §7 carries 178 genuine DESIGN.md claims and it is the only overlap (requirements' other markers are §31 and above); the review's independent census found each of the 18 markers carries 6–198 real claims, so no marker is currently satisfied only by a foreign §N. WHY NOT FIXED HERE: a correct fix needs a decision the plan does not make — whether a citation must come from a document that is *about* the design language, and if so which documents those are; inventing that policy inside a fix round would either over-exclude real claims or set a rule the plan owns, and the fix round was scoped to findings 2 and 3. THE SPEC'S D3 IS THE SOURCE: it claims every other §N in the range belongs to the redesign spec, which is false because requirements.md also uses §7. OWNER: whoever next touches the citation rule — the design-md-replaces-the-bible prose and code sweep (Tasks 4–5), or a follow-up to scripts/design-md.mjs. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ruling on which documents' §N may claim a DESIGN.md marker, then encode that set as a source filter in the check. ALSO A SWEEP GUARD: Tasks 4 and 5 must not re-point a requirements.md §N as if it were a bible citation.

RULED 2026-10-12: A DECISION THE CHECK ENCODES: the citation namespace is DECLARED BY SOURCE, not inferred from the number. `scripts/design-md.mjs --cite` accepts any `§N` in the canonical range from any document, so `requirements.md`'s own §7 — which numbers that document's requirements — reads as a claim on `DESIGN.md`'s §7. The fix is a SOURCE SET: the check takes the list of documents whose `§N` are design-language citations (the redesign spec and the specs that build on it), declared where the canonical range is declared; `requirements.md` is NOT in it, because a document about the product's requirements is not a document about the design language and its numbers belong to itself. Two consequences stated so they are not rediscovered: `DESIGN.md` is the target and never a source, and the sweep's guard stands — Tasks 4 and 5 must not re-point a `requirements.md` §N as though it were a bible citation. Over-exclusion is the risk the row names, and the set bounds it: a document joins by being ABOUT the design language, which is a property a reviewer can check, unlike a number.

title: DESIGN.md's front-matter `fontFamily` is owned by nothing: no CSS token declares it, `--sync` ignores it, and the design.md linter does not require it
detail:
FOUND BY the design-md final review (2026-10-11). Every one of the six typography entries in DESIGN.md's front matter carries `fontFamily: "system-ui, sans-serif"`, and nothing owns that value. `editor-shell.css`'s `@theme static` block declares no `--font-*` token -- the stack is written inline at the use sites -- so `--sync`, which reads only the `spacing`, `rounded` and `typography` groups, never compares it. And the format does not require it: a copy of DESIGN.md with every `fontFamily` line deleted lints 0 errors / 0 warnings under `@google/design.md@0.4.0`, so the spec's step-1 claim that `fontFamily` is required by the format's Typography is not borne out. The value is therefore a transcription that no gate keeps honest and no rule forbids changing -- neither a second owner of a CSS value (the front matter's other groups are locked to the CSS) nor an enforced transcription. IT IS CORRECT TODAY; it will silently lie if the UI stack changes. THE CONTROLLER'S RULING: unresolved, and closing it needs a decision rather than a patch -- either the shell gains a `--font-*` token the front matter can be synced against (making it a real transcription like spacing/rounded/typography, the same shape the rest of the front matter has), or `fontFamily` is declared `omitted` with a reason (the format's own mechanism, already used for `colors` and `components`) so its absence is documented rather than silent. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: one of those two landed, with the front matter and the CSS agreeing afterwards.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. THE FRONT MATTER AND THE CSS AGREE, RATHER THAN fontFamily BEING DECLARED OMITTED. The shell already declares its display stack per palette (--shell-display), so the front matters fontFamily syncs against the shells default display stack: --sync compares them and the design.md linter requires the key, which makes one fact declared once instead of a field no consumer reads. COST IF WRONG: a DESIGN.md front-matter field that must be kept in step with a CSS declaration, which is exactly what --sync exists to check.

title: `design:check` and `gates:self-test` are wired and green but run by no CI job and no hook, so the design gates' verdict depends on someone running them
detail:
FOUND BY the design-md final review (2026-10-11). WHAT WAS SEARCHED, and the negative result: `git ls-files '.github/**'` lists seven paths -- three issue templates, two markdown files, and two workflows (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `.github/workflows/visual-evidence.yml`); `grep -rn -E 'design:check|gates:self-test|design:md|design-tokens' .github/workflows/ .claude/settings.json` matches nothing; the only tracked hook config is `.claude/settings.json`, whose PreToolUse, PreCompact and SessionStart hooks run only `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs` and `scripts/sdd-checkpoint.mjs`; `git config core.hooksPath` is unset; no husky or githooks files are tracked; and `.git/hooks/` holds only the shipped `.sample` files. So both commands are reachable only by hand. NOT A REGRESSION: this matches the pre-existing `design-tokens` ratchet, which CI has never run either -- it is convention for this repo rather than a break introduced by the design-md plan. CI's `npx vitest run` does collect `tests/scripts/design-md.test.ts`, so the checks' logic is exercised in CI; only the live-tree verdict (`--lint`, `--sync` and `--cite` over DESIGN.md and editor-shell.css) is not. An unrun gate and a green gate look identical from outside, which is why this is filed rather than assumed harmless. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a CI step or a hook that runs `design:check` (and `gates:self-test`), or a recorded decision that they stay manual like the ratchet.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D1's lead ruling covering vg-213, vg-262, vg-372, vg-355 and vg-379 together: ADOPT biome check AS THE GATE. A CI step runs biome check and gates:self-test, the organizeImports findings are fixed in that commit, and every scripts/*.mjs self-test is chained into gates:self-test rather than excluded. This row is the CI half of that answer: design:check and gates:self-test are run by CI, not by hand, so no manual-by-design record is owed.

title: A bare editor mount resumes whichever theme won a millisecond mtime tie, so the document a run starts from is not reproducible
detail:
FOUND BY Task 1 of the keyboard-only walkthrough plan (2026-10-12), as the reason its first census was not reproducible. OBSERVED: two runs of the same spec against the host app directory reseeded identically by tests/e2e/global-setup.ts opened two different documents -- the first resumed E2E missing (one object in the Layers tree, census 18 presses) and the second E2E deliberate bleed (three objects, census 26 presses). Nothing in either run touched the library. THE MECHANISM, READ FROM SOURCE rather than inferred from the two runs: theme-library-client.ts reports updatedAt, the host store sets it from stat.mtime.toISOString() (themes/store.ts, entryFor), the listing sorts by id (themes/store.ts, list), and boot-theme.ts latestOwnTheme keeps the first strict maximum -- so equal updatedAt strings are broken by id order, and toISOString truncates to milliseconds. A filesystem listing of the fixture themes shows why ties are ordinary here: e2e-bleed, e2e-bleed-all, e2e-media and e2e-missing-sensor all carry the identical mtime 2026-10-12 01:16:55.827373400, because seedHostTheme writes all ten in one pass. The part NOT observed: whether the first run seeds straddled two milliseconds -- that is what the two different winners require, and the winning id under a tie (e2e-bleed) is exactly what the second run opened, but the first run state is gone and that half stands as the explanation that fits rather than as a measurement. IMPACT: a browser test that does not name a theme starts from a document it did not choose and cannot predict, which is how a press count and a scene assertion move for a reason that is not the change under test. Two saves inside one millisecond is not something an author does by hand, so the visible product impact is small and the measured one is in tests. CLOSE THIS when the tie-break is decided and written down -- by id, by name, or by a stored save counter rather than an mtime -- or when a store with two equally-recent themes is ruled to have no right answer and the bare mount stops being used as a starting state. The walkthrough plan worked around it by pinning ?theme= and did not repair it, which is the shape this row records. OWNER: whoever owns boot-theme.ts and the theme store listing, and the decision is theirs because more than one answer is defensible.

RULED 2026-10-12: RANK BY ID — most recent save first, then `id` ascending as the tie-break, written in the store that lists themes. No new persisted field: a save counter would add a column to every theme document to cover two saves inside one millisecond, and it would need a migration and would have to stay honest forever, while `id` is already stable, already unique and already persisted — which is the whole point of a stable id. Name is rejected as the tie-break because a name is editable and two themes may share one, so it converts a rare tie into a common one. This closes the row: the bare mount may keep starting from the store's own answer, because that answer is now reproducible.

title: The manager ownership review asked for on 2026-10-09 was deferred to plan 3's close, that condition has long passed, and its seventeen rows are still open

title: scene-fabric/src/persist.ts lists "locked" in SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES with no row owning that decision
detail:
FOUND BY the manager census (2026-10-12), carried as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on commit a2fe5a89 and materialised here as its own row. scene-fabric/src/persist.ts:81 lists "locked" in SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES, so whether an object's lock state persists is decided in the persist list. That is a decision about the persisted scene with no row and no map entry, and the rule that only authored state persists makes it a question rather than an oversight: a lock is authored state if the user set it deliberately and derived state if it merely mirrors a transform flag. Whether the two can disagree after a restore is not established here.

RULED 2026-10-12: `locked` IS AUTHORED STATE and persists — and the decision is already made and stated in code, which is why the missing thing is the RECORD and not the behaviour. `object-lock-manager/index.ts:92-94` says it in as many words: undo rebuilds the scene, so a revived locked object is a new instance back at Fabric's defaults, `locked` is the persisted state, and the transform flags are re-derived from it rather than persisted alongside it; `onHistoryLoaded` is the re-derivation. A lock is the author's deliberate refusal of a transform, and dropping it on save would silently re-enable editing on whichever machine reloads the file. The ownership-map entry and this row's closure belong to the ownership map's filing pass, which is the pass that exists for exactly this shape. `selectable` and `evented` beside it in the same list are NOT covered by this ruling and are not the same case: the lock writes `hasControls` and the `lock*` flags and never those two, so nothing in the lock path makes them authored — whether some other writer does is a separate question this row does not answer, and it is named in the map entry rather than answered by it.

title: The authored box's minimum dimension is decided in two places, and consolidating the writers applied one of them to the resize path
detail: FOUND BY Task 9 candidate rank 4's review (2026-10-12). Commit dd7c3365 moved the three writers of vigiliaText.box onto writeAuthoredBoxDimension, and the owner's `value < 1` / non-finite refusal (authored-box.ts:203, pre-existing, deliberate and documented there) now applies on the text-manager resize path, which previously wrote unconditionally. THE DELTA: a resize whose `target.width * scaleX` falls below 1 now returns without writing, so the authored box keeps its previous width while Fabric's width moves -- a silent no-op rather than a visible refusal. Reachability is NOT ESTABLISHED: it needs a text object carrying a non-1 scaleX, because Fabric floors its own width at 1 and only the scale can push the product under; the review derived that from vendored Fabric 7.4.0 and the editor's resize controllers but did not execute it, and no test fires the sub-unit input -- text-manager's resize specs run at scaleX 1 and widths 170-120. THE SECOND SITE: selection-inspector's funnel floors the same dimension with MIN_DIMENSION = 1 (index.ts:272, per-kind-column.ts:281), which serves all geometry and so cannot simply move to the text owner. The two floors agree today and neither is wrong; the open question is which site owns the box's minimum, and whether `< 1` is the right floor for a path a user drags. One browser check settles it together with vg-233 -- scale a text object, drag a side handle, compare vigiliaText.box.width against width * scaleX. SEVERITY: low, because the affected input class is a text object under about two scene units wide. MEASURED 2026-10-12 (Task 2.1, the one browser check this row asked for), in editor.spec.ts's 'resizes a scaled text by its side handle, and reopens the box it wrote': the starter wordmark is scaled to scaleX 0.7432 by a real corner drag and its mr handle is then dragged to a scene x of left + 0.4 -- a requested rendered width under one unit. THE REFUSAL DID NOT FIRE AND THE BOX WAS NOT SKIPPED: the box was written 460 -> 26.485, and the edge landed at a rendered width of 20.427 (Fabric width 26.485), so no sub-unit width was ever produced for the value < 1 guard to refuse. The drag's landing is 20.0 scene units away from where the pointer asked to put it (62.4 units on the widened drag that follows it, in the same case). RE-RUN 2026-10-12 after commit 6cec8acf fixed the resize path's stored units (it now writes the box unscaled): the same sub-unit drag writes 460 -> 35.637 and lands at a rendered width of 27.228 -- the pre-fix numbers times 1/scaleX -- so a sub-unit width is STILL never produced and the refusal is still not reached, now 26.8 units from the ask, and the widened drag that follows lands within 1.31 units. REACHABILITY IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED, and the 'silent no-op' this row describes is not reproduced. The landing-versus-request disagreement is filed as vg-393; this row's own question -- which site owns the box minimum -- is untouched by the run and stays open on it.
