title: The sweep's `redundant-export` tier counts a declaration-shaped occurrence as a use, so a symbol kept alive by its own object key or its own re-export reads as live
detail:
FOUND BY Task 4's independent review of the dead-code sweep (2026-10-12), verifying a claim the sweep's implementer raised and deliberately did not file. MECHANISM: the tier's liveness test is an occurrence of the symbol's name outside quoted strings in its own declaring file, and `panel:` inside an object literal satisfies it while being a KEY rather than a read. OBSERVED at the sweep's base commit `5854bed5`: the row for `panel` in `packages/editor/src/new-fabric-theme-globals.ts` read "the symbol is LIVE: its own declaring file uses it (2 occurrence(s) of the name outside quoted strings, the declaration that names it excluded)", and both occurrences are property keys -- `starterPalette.panel` (now `:84`, `panel: { name: "Panel", value: { kind: "solid", color: "#081523d9" } }`) and the second map's `panel: "#081523d9"` (now `:163`). Neither is a reference and the const had no reader, so the sweep deleted it in `93bb2c5f`; what flagged it was `noUnusedVariables` once the `export` keyword came off, so TYPECHECK IS THE BACKSTOP for this class rather than the tier. CONSEQUENCE, and it is the safe direction: every symbol whose name happens to appear as an object key in its own declaring file is withheld from the removal list, so this tier can only over-retain; the cost is survivors, never breakage, and the plan's bias prefers a survivor to a bad delete. It is nonetheless a precision defect in the instrument that produced the removal list, and it hid one deletion behind a verdict that read as evidence. FIX DIRECTION NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the tier should stop counting property keys, or whether the tier is meant as a pre-filter whose survivors typecheck re-tests -- deciding that is the work. Owner: `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs`. VERIFIED by the review report at `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-12-the-dead-code-sweep/task-4-review.md`. SECOND INSTANCE, found 2026-10-12 by Task 5's independent review of the same sweep (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-12-the-dead-code-sweep/task-5-review.md`, attack 6) and carried by that task as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in commit `c9ed9dcc`. The same self-use test is satisfied by a RE-EXPORT STATEMENT: `packages/player/src/artboard-crop.ts` re-exported `countable` and `EDGE_TOLERANCE`, and the tier read those re-export lines as in-file uses, which withheld both rows from the removal list. Verified in `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs`: the tier asks `usesIn(selfUse.get(file), name)`, and `declaredExports` reads `export { x };` as declared exports, so a re-export is counted as a use of the name it re-exports. Task 5 removed the dead re-export anyway, on the grounds that the re-export line is the thing that needed removing rather than evidence that the symbol was live. CORRECTION TO THE TRAILER, for whoever picks this up: the trailer quotes the scanner as printing "(2 occurrence(s))" where it prints 1, because `usesDeclaration` subtracts the import specifier. AND THE TWO INSTANCES SHARE ONE FIX, which is why this is an amendment rather than a second row: the self-use test counts an occurrence that DECLARES the name (an object key, a re-export) as though it READ it, so the fix direction is stated once -- either the test excludes declaration-shaped occurrences, or the tier is treated as a pre-filter whose survivors typecheck re-tests. Owner: `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs`.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: A DECLARATION IS NOT A USE. The self-use test excludes declaration-shaped occurrences, so an object key or a re-export stops counting as a read of the name it declares and the redundant-export tier reports a symbol kept alive only by its own declaration.

title: The sweep's `barrel-only-export` tier is unreachable, so 133 candidate exports were never reported and the report's zero reads as a measurement
detail:
FOUND BY the final whole-branch review of the dead-code sweep (2026-10-12), a read-only seat, as one of its two load-bearing findings; REPRODUCED by the controller against the real classification loop before this row was written, because the seat's own evidence sat in an ignored directory a clone does not carry.  THE MECHANISM, and it is structural rather than a property of this tree. `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs:705` is `if (prodConsumers.length > 0) continue;`, and it runs before the `barrel-only-export` branch at `:708`. A file's own package barrel reaches it by a re-export edge the scanner does follow, and the barrel is not a test file, so `prodConsumers` is non-empty for exactly the shape `:708` exists to report. Its condition can therefore only be evaluated when it is already false: the tier cannot fire for any input.  THE PLAN REQUIRES THAT SHAPE, in those words. Step 2 of Task 1: "`barrel-only-export` - a name whose only importer is its own package's `index.ts`." So the requirement is unimplemented, not merely unexercised, and the difference matters to whoever acts on this row: an unexercised kind may fire tomorrow, this one cannot fire at all. The ledger parked it at line 838 as "remains unexercised", which understates it by exactly that gap.  MEASURED, by a copy of the scanner with one filter corrected to exclude the file's own barrel from `prodConsumers`, run over the same tree at `93fa9a5a`: 240 candidates, of which `barrel-only-export` is 133, and the other kinds come out at exactly their HEAD counts (dead-export 8, redundant-export 83, test-only-consumer 7, unreachable-branch 9, and `no-importer-file` at 0, so it has no rows). The 133 are therefore pure additions and the existing 107 do not reclassify. By package: editor 1, fake-source 2, host 21, renderer-core 91, scene-fabric 18.  TWO DEFENSIBLE DEFINITIONS, and the disagreement is part of the defect rather than noise around it. The plan's literal wording - the only importer is the barrel, tests included - yields 76: those of the 133 whose evidence names no test importer. The code's own intent at `:708` - no production consumer other than the barrel, with test consumers disclosed in the row - yields all 133. Both measured: 76 rows have an empty test-importer list and 57 name test importers. Which one the tier means is a decision, and that is why this is filed rather than fixed on the spot, even though the filter itself is one condition.  NOT PROVEN DEAD, and nothing may be deleted on this row alone. A candidate is not a verdict. renderer-core's 91 (49 strict, 42 test-consumed) is consistent with a private library barrel wider than its consumers, but no row was adjudicated and the string-resolved vocabulary this repo resolves at runtime is invisible to the graph.  WHY IT MATTERS DESPITE THE SWEEP'S REMOVALS BEING SOUND. Nothing the sweep removed had been reported by the missing tier, so the removals stand. What does not stand is the picture: `docs/architecture/dead-code-candidates.md` reports this kind as 0 in its by-kind table and again in its delta table, which reads as a measurement that there are none, and its own disclosure said the kind "has never fired in this tree" - inviting the same conclusion instead of naming the incapability. The sweep's after-picture, 312 candidates to 107, is a floor rather than a measurement of what remains, and the report now says so.  REMEDY, and it is deliberately not taken inside the sweep: correct the filter, decide the tier's definition, re-run, and adjudicate the newly visible rows as a sweep of its own. Reopening a phase three reviews had closed, to make the candidate count larger rather than more correct, was the wrong trade at that plan's close.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: the barrel-only-export tier means NO PRODUCTION CONSUMER OTHER THAN THE BARREL, WITH TEST CONSUMERS DISCLOSED -- 133 candidates, not the plan's literal sole-importer shape's 76. A test importing a barrel export is disclosed in the report and does not hide the export from the tier, because a survivor costs a ticket and a deleted live symbol costs the product, so the bias stays on detection. The filter is corrected, the sweep is re-run, and the newly visible rows are adjudicated as a sweep of its own.

title: An in-app store where authors submit themes and anyone can browse and download them
detail:
RAISED BY THE USER on 2026-10-12 as a brainstorming exercise: not accepted work, and the user does not intend to start it soon. DESIGN RECORD: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-theme-store-design.md, Status draft. SHAPE AGREED IN CONVERSATION: GitHub is the whole backend, so nothing is run and nothing is paid for. The catalogue is item.json files in one public repo; identity is the author's GitHub account reused for everything; a submission is a pull request; the review instrument is the diff, which a theme being JSON makes readable; merging lists the item; a login added to a verified-authors list makes that author's own PRs auto-merge, and that auto-merge must be scoped to the author's own catalogue path or one compromised account rewrites the store's CI; media rides on release assets, which carries a native download_count. THE EXCHANGE UNIT ALREADY EXISTS, which is why this is small: §139, ADR-0004 and 0017 fix the validated package ZIP as the portable artifact, §141 fixes validation, and host/src/themes/store.ts already enforces 32 MiB per asset and 128 MiB total, on save and on load, so the store defines no format, no validator and no size policy. IDENTITY IS SKIPPABLE: browsing is a static index.json and downloads are plain URLs, so neither needs a token nor an API call, favorite COUNTS still render anonymously because the Action bakes them into index.json, and sign-in is a just-in-time prompt on the heart only. VIEWS ARE DROPPED: GitHub exposes no free per-item view count, so 'most viewed' is not a sort and sorting is created, updated, downloads and favorites. MEDIA: video is expected to be common and rides inside the package, so an unbounded video is what would break a zero-cost host; the existing size cap needs a companion duration cap (proposed 30s) and resolution ceiling (proposed 1920 long edge) or an author cannot predict the outcome, and a publish-time normalizer holds the envelope. OPEN, each needing a decision rather than a patch: hosting the bytes (release assets versus an object store with zero egress), the ffmpeg source for the normalizer (a probed system binary versus a bundled static build carrying GPL parts such as x264), index.json freshness, who inspects imagery for moderation, and removal semantics. UNVERIFIED: every free-tier limit the design leans on, listed in the spec, because a false one changes the architecture. NAMING: the owner ruled on 2026-10-12 that the existing editor-to-phone publish route is renamed so the store owns the word; 'activate' was the suggestion but collides with keyboard-activation in editor/src/viewport-manager/navigation.ts, cast and go-live are the clear candidates, and the rename is a family spanning the route, the published store in host/src/server.ts (a watched path) and publish-loop.spec.ts, so it can land alone before any store work. WIDGETS ARE OUT OF SCOPE: widget packages do not exist yet because §139 defers them until they have an authoring workflow, so the widget store needs its own spec.

RULED 2026-10-15: **SCHEDULED AHEAD OF THE TRIAGE, and it enters a phase** rather than waiting for one. The user set the order: this row and `vg-405` outrank the 95 rows no phase carries, because they are the two the user raised themselves. This one is a feature with a spec rather than a fix.

RULED 2026-10-15 (brainstorming, before the spec is revised): **THE STORE CARRIES THREE KINDS, AND THE SPEC IS SCOPED AS STOREFRONT-NOW, KINDS-FOLLOW.** The user's own words: the store should carry **dashboard themes, widget presets and editor themes**. The spec that follows covers the catalogue, the submission and review flow, identity and the client surface **kind-agnostically**, and specifies the theme package as the only kind v1 ships; widget presets and editor themes each get an addendum when their own artifact is designed. **This supersedes this row's own `WIDGETS ARE OUT OF SCOPE` sentence and the draft spec's scope line**, which both said the widget store must be a later spec that the theme spec must not pre-empt — the later spec still exists, but the storefront is now specified once for all three rather than three times. The reason the split is affordable: of the three kinds **only the dashboard theme has an exchange unit today** (ADR-0004/0017/§139/§141 plus `host/src/themes/store.ts`'s bounds), and the draft spec's leverage claim — that the store defines no format, no validator and no size policy — is true only while that is the only unit.

**A WIDGET PRESET IS A THEME ENVELOPE MINUS THE ARTBOARD**, defined by the user on 2026-10-15: a scene **subtree** plus its `bindings`, `globals` and `assets`, and no artboard. That is deliberately larger than the alternative reading (a subtree plus bindings alone) and it is the cheaper one, because it reuses the envelope's own sections and therefore its validator and its bounds rather than inventing a second format for a second kind. `card-library.ts`'s insertable cards are the authoring-side precedent — one Fabric `Group` over its parts, with readings in the envelope's `bindings` and a `provenance` key — and §139 still defers widget packages until an authoring workflow exists, which is what the addendum waits on.

**AN EDITOR THEME HAS NO ARTIFACT AT ALL TODAY, and that is a design decision rather than a gap:** §35 states that editor-shell theming is separate from authored dashboard theme globals, so an editor theme is a token set for the editor chrome, not a scene. Its addendum therefore has to settle what the artifact is before the store can carry it, and nothing about the dashboard theme's package shape answers that.

title: Escape out of a layer rename drops focus to the document body, so a keyboard author loses their place
detail: FOUND BY TASK 4'S REVIEW of the keyboard walkthrough plan (2026-10-12), MEASURED rather than read: the reviewer's probe on the committed bytes printed `PROBE-AFTER-ESCAPE BODY|`, where the walk expected to still be on the row it was renaming. WHAT: with a composition row's rename field focused, Escape cancels the draft and the field unmounts, and focus is left on `document.body` -- nothing returns it to the row. The next Tab therefore restarts from the top of the document instead of continuing from the author's place. WHY IT MATTERS: section 13.1's keyboard-only walkthrough requires focus to be where an interaction left it, and this is the one sub-step in the assembled walk where it is not; the helper that drives it re-tabs from the document root under a bounded press count, which works and is not the behaviour a keyboard user gets to rely on. It is NOT in the assembled §13.1 walk: that walk's field interaction is the inspector's ControlText, whose Escape leaves focus in the field, and the rename cancel lives in the plan's separate Task 4 test. WHAT IT COSTS the plan that found it: the walk is less continuous there than it reads, and Task 5 must not assume it resumes in place -- recorded in that plan's ledger. NOT FIXED THERE ON PURPOSE: the walkthrough plan's Out of scope reads "No new focus management. If a region is unreachable, this plan records it; changing the shell's focus order is its own change with its own spec." A register row is that record. OWNER: whoever owns the composition row's own focus -- the rename field is opened by Enter or F2 on a treeitem and is unmounted by the cancel without a focus return. WHAT THE EVIDENCE DOES NOT SHOW: whether the same cancel-by-Escape inside a settings row or a dialog does the same; only the composition row was driven.

title: Two plans' parity comparisons no longer exist, and the acceptance item that requires them has no wording for that
detail:
FOUND BY the counted acceptance pass of 2026-10-12, which walked every item of the design-language spec's Acceptance section and found this the only one not discharged. WHAT: that section's last item requires every plan's parity capture to exist beside its mockup in docs/design/mockups/ with every difference either fixed or backed by a cited rule. Plans 6, 7 and 8 have captures (shell-capture-add.png, shell-capture-graphite.png, shell-capture-glyphs.png beside shell.html; settings-capture-graphite.png and settings-capture-editorial.png beside settings.html, registered in docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md). Plans 1 and 3 do not: current/controls.html and current/controls-light.html have no capture beside them, no .superpowers/sdd/ workspace survives for either plan, and the archived acceptance ledger in docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-08-iconography-and-copy.md records in its own words that Plan 1's ten differences no longer exist anywhere. WHY IT MATTERS: the item cannot be met or refused as written, because for those two plans the thing it asks to be checked is gone; the verdict the archived ledger records for the item (met) was taken on the capture half only and never addressed this half. WHAT IT NEEDS: a decision rather than code -- either reproduce the comparison from each capture and the commit body that carried it, or narrow the item's wording to the plans whose reports survive. OWNER: whoever owns the spec's Acceptance text; the item is the spec's, so the decision is the user's. WHAT THE EVIDENCE DOES NOT SHOW: whether any of plan 1's or 3's differences were in fact fixed later under another plan's name; only that no record of the comparison survives to establish it. THE CAPTURE HALF IS NOW PLACED FOR EVERY DRAWING, MEASURED 2026-10-13, WHICH CHANGES WHAT THIS ROW OWNS BUT NOT WHAT IT ASKS. The paragraph above said `current/controls.html` and `current/controls-light.html` have no capture beside them; they do now. `controls-capture-graphite.png` and `controls-capture-editorial.png` sit beside those two drawings (`988d1788`), placed from the registered action `the control set renders in the design language` (`captureVisualReview(page, testInfo, "control-set")`, `design-language.spec.ts:1410`) and registered in `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md`. **And the same pass closed the modal's third sheet**: `settings-keyboard.html` and `settings-about.html` had no capture either, though the one action already photographs all three tabs, so `settings-keyboard-capture-{graphite,editorial}.png` and `settings-about-capture-{graphite,editorial}.png` were added beside their drawings and the existing two were re-shot, because the committed six were taken 2026-10-11 (`f7078e93`) and the dialog moved under them on 2026-10-13 (`69e6e7f1`'s `dl > div` padding, `7a92d0fe`'s dialog section-2 body role) — the Appearance and About renders are now 2px shorter and the Keyboard render 6px narrower than the committed bytes (`e412c98d`). **So as of `e412c98d` every drawing in `docs/design/mockups/current/` has a capture pair beside it** — six drawings, twelve PNGs — and the first half of the acceptance item is met for every plan whose matching mockup is one of them. **WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, AND IT IS THE ROW'S ACTUAL SUBJECT.** The item says *each plan's* completion report carries *its* capture, and the prose attributes captures to plans 1, 3 (`988d1788`), 6 (`shell-capture-glyphs.png`), 7 (the shell pair) and 8 (the three settings pairs). **No durable record names a capture for plans 2, 4 or 5** — their completion reports died with their `.superpowers/sdd/` workspaces, and the register holds no row for it. Whether their captures were the shell and settings images already beside those drawings, or were never distinct, is not recorded anywhere this repository keeps. **WHAT IT NEEDS IS UNCHANGED**: a decision rather than code — either reproduce plan 1's and plan 3's comparisons from each capture and the commit body that carried it, or narrow the item's wording to the plans whose reports survive, and settle whether plans 2, 4 and 5 are inside that wording at all. NEAR ROWS: `vg-436` (the `controls-light.html` naming question, which this row's own paragraph names by that filename); `vg-434` (references that resolve to nothing); `vg-316`, `vg-319` (the open `fix` differences that keep the item's second clause unmet regardless of the capture half). THE OPEN QUESTION THIS ROW NAMED IS NOW ANSWERED, 2026-10-13: the row said "whether their captures were the shell and settings images already beside those drawings, or were never distinct, is not recorded anywhere this repository keeps". **They were, and the mapping is now recorded.** **THE PLANS, FROM THE SPEC'S OWN TABLE** (`2026-10-08-editor-design-language-design.md:396-405`): 1 the control set, 2 the shell and rail, 3 the inspector, 4 the panes, 5 settings and appearance, 6 iconography and copy, 7 shell parity, 8 settings parity. **WHAT EACH DRAWING ANSWERS FOR.** `controls.html` and `controls-light.html` draw plan 1's set, which plan 3's column is built on. `shell.html` draws plans 2, 3 and 7 at once: its Position, Paint and Spends sections are the inspector's (`grep` finds those words in it and finds Composition, Tokens and Document in no drawing at all), and it is the drawing both parity plans were pulled to. The three settings sheets draw plans 5 and 8. **SO THE CAPTURES EXIST FOR PLANS 2, 4 AND 5, WHICH IS WHAT THIS ROW COULD NOT ESTABLISH.** Plan 2's surfaces are `shell-capture-graphite.png`; plan 4's Add pane is `shell-capture-add.png`, and its other three panes are the `pane-composition`, `pane-tokens` and `pane-document` files in `docs/evidence/screenshots/`, which sit beside no drawing because no drawing draws them; plan 5's surfaces are the six settings files. Plan 6's glyph work has no drawing of its own either, and `shell-capture-glyphs.png` is its evidence. **WHY THE RECORD READ AS IF THEY DID NOT EXIST.** `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md` already carries drawing-adjacent passages, and they name plans **1, 3, 6, 7 and 8**. Plans 2, 4 and 5 are named in none of them, so a reader pairing captures to plans finds those three absent and concludes the evidence is gone. **That paragraph is now written**: the README records which surfaces each of the six drawings and their eleven captures show, explicitly not as a claim that a plan's own report names its capture. **WHAT THE RULING THEREFORE TURNS ON, WHICH IS NARROWER THAN THE ROW FIRST PUT IT.** It is not "reproduce plan 1's and plan 3's comparisons or narrow the item", although plans 1 and 3's own comparisons are still gone with their workspaces. It is **whether the item counts a capture that shows a plan's surfaces when the durable record attaches that capture to a later parity plan instead** — the situation for plans 2, 4 and 5, whose surfaces are photographed and drawn but whose own reports never named the image. Plan 4's three undrawn panes and plan 6's missing drawing are the residue the item still cannot reach at all: for those, there is no matching mockup to carry a capture beside. THE WORDING QUESTION HAS A NORMATIVE RULE ON ONE SIDE, FOUND 2026-10-13: `docs/design/mockups/README.md` is not only a description of the set -- it carries a rule for keeping it current, under **Keeping them current**: "**The current files are refreshed when the set of surfaces changes.** A pane, a tab, a section or a rail slot that appears or disappears is drawn -- in the original's treatment, never in a treatment of the product's devising." **So the undrawn panes are not merely unreachable; the drawings' own rule requires them to have been drawn.** Composition, Tokens and Document are shipped panes and they are named in no drawing (`shell.html` draws the shell and the Add pane, and the three panes' captures sit beside nothing). Scope stated exactly: that sentence names a pane, a tab, a section and a rail slot, so it binds plan 4's three panes and **does not** bind plan 6's glyph sheet, which is not one of the four things the sentence lists. **What that makes the decision.** The item's residue for plans 4 and 6 is not "narrow the wording or leave it open" but a three-way choice the repository's own documents frame: (a) draw the three panes, per the README's rule and in the originals' treatment, and the captures then have a matching mockup to sit beside -- the item's second clause becomes reachable for them; (b) narrow the item to the drawings that exist, on the reading that the acceptance instrument is the six current files and the README's refresh rule is a maintenance duty rather than an acceptance one; or (c) leave both as they are and carry the residue. **And (a) is deliberately not taken by this session**, because a drawing is the acceptance instrument rather than a description of one: the README's own warning is that a mockup which no longer matches is worse than none because it is believed, and the user's ruling of 2026-10-10 made the drawing the target the product is pulled to. Authoring three new targets is the ruling owner's act, not a session's. **Verified beside it, so the capture half is not doubted later**: `docs/design/mockups/current/` holds six drawings (`shell.html`, `settings.html`, `settings-keyboard.html`, `settings-about.html`, `controls.html`, `controls-light.html`) and eleven captures -- `shell-capture-graphite/add/glyphs`, `controls-capture-{graphite,editorial}`, and a pair for each of the three settings panels -- so every current drawing carries a capture. The two unpaired PNGs a reader might expect to have drawings, `inspector-controls.html` and `inspector-language.html`, are **originals**: the README freezes them as "the record of the first cut, not the target", so no capture is required beside them and their absence is correct rather than a gap. THE SECOND CLAUSE'S RESIDUE IS EVERY PLAN'S, MEASURED ACROSS ALL EIGHT ON 2026-10-13, AND IT IS NOT THREE ROWS. The spec's discharge paragraph counts plan 8's three, which is right for plan 8 and understates the clause, because the clause reads "every plan's parity capture ... every difference it lists". Walked plan by plan, five of the eight list a difference whose owner is an open row today, and plan 1's ten have no owner recorded at all. PLAN 1 (the control set) - ten, OWNER UNKNOWN: `1f991845`'s body is the only trace ("Ten differences are listed in the task report"), and `docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-08-iconography-and-copy.md:759-768` records that they "no longer exist anywhere". PLAN 2 (the shell and the rail) - four: its 25-row table (`archive/2026-10-08-the-shell-and-the-rail.md:731-757`) puts rows 7, 17, 18 and 22 on `vg-227`, `vg-222`, `vg-225` and `vg-230`, and rows 19, 24, 25 name `vg-231`, `vg-217` and `vg-226`, all `verified`; nine further rows are adjudicated "deliberate, deferred to a later plan" (plans 3, 4, 5), which is a claim about those plans and not a row state. PLAN 3 (the inspector) - none: its four differences survive in `9ee1fc21`'s body, each owned by a drawing, a cited section rule or that commit, and the one item its report called a difference is withdrawn there as a parity match. PLAN 4 (the panes) - five: `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-the-panes/task-12-report.md:62-136` numbers 32 entries and puts four on `vg-269`, `vg-260`, `vg-265` and `vg-270`, and one (`vg-230`) on a shell-level row added in fix round 1. PLAN 5 (settings and appearance) - none: `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-settings-and-appearance/task-6-report.md:339-371` lists eleven differences, ten recorded deliberate and one fixed in-plan. PLAN 6 (iconography and copy) - none: `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-iconography-and-copy/task-9-report.md:127-150` lists eleven, one fixed in-plan and one "no difference". PLAN 7 (shell parity) - two open among its own `fix` rows: `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/adjudication.md:58` and `:92-97` name A11 `vg-217` (verified), A12 `vg-230` and A17 `vg-222` among the `fix` rows another owner holds, and hand 13 more to the next plan; its residual list (`task-7-report.md:205-219`) names `vg-308`, `vg-310` and `vg-274`. PLAN 8 (settings parity) - three: `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-11-settings-parity/adjudication.md:82-102` numbers 19 rows and its row 19 is the Close, owned by `vg-316`; `vg-319` and `vg-322` sit in the spec's list beside it. THE DISTINCT OPEN OWNERS: `vg-222`, `vg-223`, `vg-225`, `vg-227`, `vg-228`, `vg-230`, `vg-260`, `vg-265`, `vg-269`, `vg-270`, `vg-316`, `vg-319` and `vg-322`, with `vg-308`, `vg-310` and `vg-274` from plan 7's residual list. Every one was read as `state: open` in `docs/product/backlog.jsonl` on 2026-10-13, parsed line by line, and none appears in the archive; `vg-223` and `vg-228` are the two plan 2 files as owned elsewhere rather than visible in its captures. `vg-254` is open in the same neighbourhood but its plan files it as a `Discovered, not fixed` item rather than a drawing difference, so it is not counted. AND EVERY ONE OF THOSE ROWS IS A ROW THE ACTIVE DRAIN'S PHASE 1 SESSIONS TAKE - `vg-222`, `vg-223`, `vg-225` and `vg-227` in D3; `vg-228` and `vg-274` in D5, already ruled 2026-10-12; `vg-260` in D6; `vg-230` in D10; and the browser-pinned `vg-308`, `vg-310`, `vg-319`, `vg-265` and `vg-270` in the Phase 1 follow-up session at Task 2.5 Step 4 - EXCEPT TWO: `vg-316`, which Phase 2 ran in Task 2.4 and could not close because what it needs is a DESIGN.md decision (`vg-441`), and plan 1's ten, which no row carries. WHAT THAT DOES TO THIS ROW'S ASK: the wording decision is still the user's, and it is now ORDERED rather than parallel - the item's second clause cannot be met before the drain's Phase 1 ruling sessions run, and the plans 1-3 narrowing is the one half no other plan will move. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether plan 2's nine "deferred to a later plan" adjudications were in fact discharged by plans 3, 4 and 5 - the later plans changed the shell and the modal materially and plan 2's own report is optimistic on several, but those owners are named as plans and not as rows, so no row state can settle it. BOTH HALVES OF THIS ROW WERE RE-MEASURED ON 2026-10-13, AND THE PROSE ABOVE IS NOW HISTORY RATHER THAN A GAP. FIRST, PLAN 1'S COMPARISON IS RE-MADE. Its ten differences are still gone, but its drawing and its capture are both current, so a read-only census re-derived the comparison from `docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html` and the shipped control set (brief `dispatch-a658c22eac7f428fd.md`, drain workspace; read-only, no file touched). Only two checks against that drawing survive in the tree at all — `tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:913-934` (two `PARITY` rows reading the label column's width) and `design-language.spec.ts:2540-2552` (two `productRows` reading the plain-DOM button box's padding against `controls.html:112`). The re-made census places every drawn element in one of four classes. IMPLEMENTED: the field row's 74px label column and `flex:1` cell, the well's `--panel-2` fill with a 1px `--edge` and `--radius-md`, the slider's 36px well with its 3px accent track, the refusal line under the toggle, and the plain-DOM boxes' 12px control text (the D9 fix). OWNED BY AN OPEN ROW: the well's horizontal padding (`vg-202`, three-way between product 6px, drawing 8px and §3's 4px) and the segmented control's whole treatment (`vg-301`). RULE-BACKED, i.e. the DRAWING is the stale side and no work exists: seven differences where a cited § clause requires what the product already does — the eyebrow's colour (`controls.html:29` draws `--faint`, §2 (`DESIGN.md:144-147`) makes an eyebrow muted), the field row's label-to-value gap (`:36` draws 10px, §3's step table gives 8 between a label and its control), the select value's family (drawn `system-ui`, §2 makes values mono), the chevron mark (§5's well-with-chevron entry specifies a `▼` in `--faint`), the slider's track and thumb radius (drawn 2px and a circle, neither on §3's radius ladder), the toggle's resting boundary (§5 rule 6 brightens the toggle's border), and the read-only row's label family (`:177` draws the label in mono, §2 says labels are sans). UNOWNED: five, filed as `vg-443`, `vg-444`, `vg-445` and `vg-446` — with the honest boundary that this was a declaration-level pass and says where it cannot settle a question: a value the product inherits rather than declares, a shorthand the drawing writes that has no counterpart (the 26px row height arrives through `padding` plus a `font` shorthand, which `mockup-values.ts` refuses by design), and the drawing-local `--value` token, which has no §4 role. SECOND, PLAN 2'S TWELVE DEFERRED ADJUDICATIONS ARE NOW CHECKED AGAINST THE PRODUCT. Plan 2's table defers twelve differences to plans 3, 4 and 5 (tally at `archive/2026-10-08-the-shell-and-the-rail.md:768-771`). NINE LANDED, each verified in the product rather than in the later plan's report: the pane re-cut to 246px (`editor-shell.css:988`, `7bdd4ea0`), the header palette chip's move into Settings (`64fea389`), the printed `⌘⇧P` (`shortcut-manager/index.ts:77`, `3fe3f22e`), the rail-foot settings gear (`rail.tsx:85-102`, `13984ab9`), the Add pane's diagram tiles, glyph tiles and text row (`add-pane.tsx:127`, `:171-182`, `:139`, `96099ba8`), Assets absorbed into Add (`c8dc0b1a`), and the inspector's empty state and five sections (`f1a35b82`, `cdd6ecc0`). **THREE DID NOT LAND**, and two of them are owned by no row: the Add title bar's count (`vg-269`, which plan 4 declined and filed — already one of the open owners this row lists), and the two copy differences filed as `vg-445`. **So the 'not established' sentence above is established, and what plans 1 and 2 leave in the second clause is a named list rather than an unread claim.** ONE CAVEAT THAT STANDS: the re-made census is not plan 1's own list — it is a comparison taken now, so it must be read with its method beside it, not as the ten differences the deleted report held. DISPOSITION CORRECTED 2026-10-13, because the sentence above is one step stale. It says the census's five unowned differences were "filed as `vg-443`, `vg-444`, `vg-445` and `vg-446`", which is not what happened to them. Of the five: TWO WERE FIXED rather than filed — the subject's name weight and the section count's family and colour, both already stated by the drawing (`controls.html:24`, `:30`) and required by §2's mono list and title weight and by §4's `--faint` role, landed with their red-proved browser case; ONE BELONGS TO `vg-441` — the plain-DOM control box's label colour, which is a property of the control §5's closed vocabulary does not name; and TWO ARE `vg-444` — the read-only rows' dashed dividers and the section headers' trailing rules. `vg-443` and `vg-446` are findings the census surfaced rather than members of that five: the serif family the count inherited, which a declaration-level pass could not settle and a browser then measured, and the case whose name asserts §7.4 while its assertion pins a literal that names no place. Recorded rather than left, because the earlier sentence would let a reader count four rows against five differences and conclude one was lost. ONE CENSUS ENTRY CORRECTED 2026-10-13, ON THE SAME EVIDENCE THAT CLOSED IT. The re-made plan-1 comparison called the read-only row's omitted dashed divider *unowned*; it is rule-backed — `selection-inspector/column.tsx:191-194` records the product's reason and cites it ('no well, no border, because a border means editable (DESIGN.md §5.1)'), four lines above the JSX the census read. The census read declarations and structure; a product note that states why a declaration is absent is a source it did not weigh, and that is the failure mode this correction is recorded against rather than quietly fixed. The same pass implemented the one hairline that had no such note (the section header's trailing rule), so `vg-444` closes with one half implemented and one half backed.

RULED 2026-10-15: **A CAPTURE THE REGISTER ATTACHES TO A LATER PARITY PLAN COUNTS FOR THE PLAN WHOSE SURFACES IT SHOWS.** The item is therefore met on this clause rather than narrowed: what was lost was plans 2, 4 and 5's own *reports*, and their surfaces are photographed and the captures resolve, which is what the item asks for. This is the last word-shaped item on the sixteenth acceptance item.

title: No spec asserts the player's update loop reaches the canvas now the case that did was deleted with display-fabric.spec.ts
detail: FOUND BY Phase 0 of the backlog drain (2026-10-12), filing the residual spec section 3.2 states for vg-196 rather than reading the coverage out of a row whose subject was deleted. WHAT CLOSED, AND WHY THAT LEAVES A HOLE: vg-196's subject was `display-fabric.spec.ts`'s case `keeps repainting as samples arrive`, held by that row's own words to be a STANDING RED -- a 30 s timeout landing before its assertion, reproduced at `af499716` -- so the coverage the file believed it had for the update loop was absent rather than passing. Commit `ad94e5ed` deleted the spec and with it the red; it did not repair the loop, and whether the loop is still covered was never answered. WHAT IS VERIFIED AT HEAD (2026-10-12): `openCanvasPlayer`, the shared helper that case awaited, has zero occurrences repo-wide; `page.clock` survives only as the shared `tests/e2e/clock.ts` helper `installFixedClock`, whose call sites are `tests/e2e/editor.spec.ts`'s two determinism captures (`:4435`, `:4518`) and `clock.ts`'s own `openPaused`, an exported helper with no callers anywhere (measured 2026-10-12), so no player spec installs a clock; and no surviving spec reads the artboard canvas twice with a sample between the reads -- `tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts` proves samples arrive (its `batchCount` reading and the disappearance of `#vigilia-connection`) and that the artboard canvas is visible, neither of which is a repaint. The case in `src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/scene/mount.dom.test.ts` that does drive `handle.update` asserts DOM span identity, which is the DOM renderer, not the Fabric canvas the player mounts. WHY IT MATTERS: the deleted case's own comment recorded its failure verified by sabotage -- the update call cut, and it goes red -- and it was the only thing in the suite that would notice the update loop ceasing to reach the canvas. OWNER: the refresh path that reaches the canvas is `src/web/packages/player/src/main.ts` (`refresh()`, which drives `hydrateCharts` and `refreshBoundText` and then calls `handle.canvas.requestRenderAll()`, scheduled by `startChartRefresh(refresh, 30, ...)`), whose binding helpers come from the scene-fabric package — `refreshBoundText` in `fabric-text.ts` and `startChartRefresh` in `chart-refresh.ts`, with `hydrateCharts` local to the player — while `src/web/packages/scene-fabric/src/adapter.ts` is the mount path (`createSceneAdapter`), not the refresh; a replacement case belongs in `src/web/tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts` beside its live-sample test. WHAT SETTLES IT: one browser case that reads the artboard canvas, drives at least one sample, and requires the pixels to differ between the two reads. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the coverage is wanted at all -- the close is legitimate without it, and this row exists so the hole is tracked rather than reconstructed from a row whose subject is gone.

title: The inspector's write funnel is unreconciled: its writers left selection-inspector/index.ts, but the dispatch and the closure state it reads stayed behind
detail: FOUND BY Phase 0 of the backlog drain (2026-10-12), filing the residual spec section 3.2 states for vg-255. WHAT CLOSED, AND WHY THAT LEAVES A QUESTION: vg-255's subject was a line count -- `selection-inspector/index.ts` past AGENTS.md's 800-line stop -- and its own AMENDED note already recorded that commit `3e8c9523` had taken the file back under the stop (822 -> 736) while the archived plan's own 540-line constraint still stood. The file is 707 lines today, so the close holds. THE QUESTION THE CLOSE DROPS, in that row's own words: splitting the write funnel out 'means deciding where the write path lives and how it reaches `described` and `targetRevision`, which are closure state the funnel reads at call time'. THE SPLIT HAPPENED; THE FUNNEL DID NOT MOVE WITH IT: the writes now live outside `index.ts` -- `writePanelField` and `writeShapeGeometryField` in `selection-inspector/panel.ts`, `writeGlassField` in `selection-inspector/glass.ts`, `writeMark` in `selection-inspector/bleed.ts`, and the run and binding writes in `selection-inspector/run-edits.ts` -- while the state they are asked from stayed in the closure. WHAT REMAINS UNRECORDED: the revision-and-lock refusal is `view.ts`'s `editRefusal`, read against the live target inside `createSelectionInspector`'s `edits.commit`; the dispatch that picks a writer by `fieldId` (the `panel-` and `glass-` prefixes and the shape-geometry fall-through) is that same function; and the state that makes the read correct is the closure's `let described` and `let targetRevision`, which each writer receives second-hand as an argument rather than reads. So the per-kind writers are named owners and the funnel that asks them is not, and nothing decides whether the next converted field adds another branch to `edits.commit` or moves the funnel out. `docs/architecture/ownership.md` names the writers (`panel.ts`, `glass.ts`) and the directory, and says nothing about the dispatch or the closure state. WHY IT MATTERS: it is vg-255's question one refactor later -- the file is under the stop because leaves were extracted, not because the shape was decided -- and `panel.ts` is now 751 lines, close to the same stop. OWNER: `src/web/packages/editor/src/selection-inspector/` (`createSelectionInspector` and its closure state); the decision is a design one, and `docs/architecture/ownership.md` is where a ruling would land. WHAT SETTLES IT: a recorded decision on where the write funnel lives -- in the closure, in a module of its own, or in the per-kind writers -- and how it reaches `described` and `targetRevision`. NOT A RUNTIME DEFECT: vg-255's reviewer found no behavioural problem, and none is claimed here.

title: A side-handle resize of a scaled text lands its edge tens of scene units away from the edge the pointer asked for
detail: FOUND while writing the browser check vg-233 and vg-370 asked for (Task 2.1 of the backlog-drain plan), in editor.spec.ts's 'resizes a scaled text by its side handle, and reopens the box it wrote'. THE MEASUREMENT, AS IT STANDS AFTER COMMIT 6cec8acf: the starter wordmark carries scaleX 0.7432 and its mr handle is dragged to a scene x the test names. Dragged to left + 240 the edge now lands within 1.31 scene units of the request -- that drag has LEFT this row, it was the resize path storing width * scaleX, and it is fixed and measured with vg-233 (the 240-unit request landed at 177.58431831416544 before the fix, so it was 62.4156816858345 short (exactly `asked - landed`). CORRECTED 2026-10-12: this row called that landing 'the request times scaleX', and it is not -- 240 x 0.7431987269831705 is 178.36769447596086, 0.78 above it. The equality that IS exact is on the box: the pre-fix `boxAfter` 237.94593984979582 is the post-fix 320.1646224767875 times `scaleX`, so the scaled write shrank the object by exactly `scaleX`). The subject that remains is the OTHER drag in the same case: to left + 0.4 the edge lands at a rendered width of 27.228 where 0.4 was asked, 26.8 scene units away, with the box written 460 -> 35.637 for the ask. WHAT THE FIX DOES NOT EXPLAIN: the sub-unit gap moved from 20.427 to 27.228 -- the pre-fix number times 1/scaleX -- and is still 26.8 units wide, so a wrong stored unit explains neither its size nor its direction. The relation this row flagged for a tracer (the landed rendered width being 0.740 of the request) is therefore explained and closed; the sub-unit landing is not. One number to trace by: the landed Fabric width is 35.637, neither the sub-unit value asked for nor the floor at 1, so the value < 1 refusal is not what decides it. THE HARNESS IS NOT THE SUSPECT: the same helper (resizeRightHandleTo with editor-canvas.ts objectHandleScenePoint) lands group-ram-card's mr handle within 3 units of where the pointer was put in 'snaps a resize onto a neighbour's line', and the test's own askedLanding is the pointer's scene x read back through the canvas' getScenePoint, so the pointer was where the test says it was. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED for this drag: whether Fabric's changeWidth measures a pointer in another frame once a scaled Textbox is near a unit wide, or an editor path re-derives the width after guardBoxWidth restores it, is not traced. OWNER: scene-fabric/src/authored-box.ts's guardBoxWidth and the editor's text-manager resize path, whichever the trace lands on. SEVERITY: low for the product -- an author sees the edge stop short and drags again -- but it is why vg-370's sub-unit input could not be reached, so it blocks that row's settlement. EVIDENCE: the pre-fix numbers were identical in every run of that case (three runs, one report retained per run at C:/tmp/vg21/vg-233-vg-370-resize.json), and the post-fix numbers are from C:/tmp/vg21/vg-233-vg-370-resize-r1.json -- both outside the tree, each read from that run's own JSON report.

title: Entering and leaving a selection inside a scaled or rotated group moves its members, so align and distribute measure a displaced scene
detail: FOUND BY THE USER (2026-10-12), reported as `Alignment and distribution inside a group is broken, they got transported to outside of the canvas`. THAT REPORT IS TWO DEFECTS, and the one below is the half the user's phrasing does not name. The other half -- a grouped selection aligned in a group whose transform is a pure translation -- is FIXED in the same commit as this row (`arrange.ts`'s `move` measured in canvas coordinates and wrote in the parent's plane, so a group's translation was applied twice; red-proved at `expected 934.5 to be close to 434.5, received difference is 500`). THIS ROW IS WHAT REMAINS, and it is not `arrange.ts`'s to fix by choosing a plane. MEASURED in jsdom (`arrange.dom.test.ts`'s sibling probe, since deleted): a `Group` of two `Rect`s at `left: 200, top: 120, scaleX: 2, scaleY: 2, angle: 30`, wrapped in a real `Canvas`, then `new ActiveSelection([a, b], { canvas })`, `canvas.setActiveObject(selection)`, `canvas.discardActiveObject()`. The anchor's `getBoundingRect().left` reads 86.051 before the selection exists and 293.678 after only the discard -- with the object's OWN state identical either side (`left: -65.5`, `top: -20.5`, `angle: 0`, `scaleX: 1`) -- so what moved is the group's own transform, not the child's. Re-selecting restores 86.051, so the pair round-trips and nothing is permanently lost; what breaks is that `applyArrange` measures and moves INSIDE that displaced window, so an align that is arithmetically correct in the state it can see lands 22.487 units out in the state the author sees (`expected 86.05067210423853, received 108.53778516388122`). WHY IT IS A ROW AND NOT PART OF THE FIX: the cause is inside Fabric's `Group._enterGroup`/`_exitGroup` + `ActiveSelection` interaction for a parent whose matrix has a linear part, which is reachable from `grouping-manager` and from Fabric upstream but is not reachable from `arrange.ts`; the owner is a design decision, and the fix may be to stop discarding the selection at all. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the app reaches this state as shipped -- a pure-translation group does not, and a rotated or scaled group was NOT exercised in a browser, only in jsdom, and the browser run is what Phase 2 holds. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a browser reading of a rotated or scaled group's members before and after entering the selection (the displaced reading above), then the fix at whichever owner that establishes, with the same numbers re-taken.

title: The context menu's horizontal anchor arm allows a 2px drift where the placement it asserts is tighter than that
detail: FOUND BY the Task 2.4a task review (2026-10-12), as observation 6 of ten, and filed rather than fixed because the fix widens an assertion that a red proof stands on. WHAT THE ARM IS: `tests/e2e/editor-context-menu.spec.ts` adds a case asserting the canvas menu opens where the pointer is, as `Math.abs(menu.popupLeft - point.x) <= ANCHOR_X_PX` with `ANCHOR_X_PX = 2` (`:108`), and a second-use arm at `:341` and `:351` asserting a second click moves the menu by the same distance. THE REVIEW'S NUMBER: it reports the measured offset as 1.4-1.8 px, leaving 0.2-0.6 px of headroom, and calls it flake risk of the `vg-141`/`vg-143` class. THAT NUMBER IS NOT REPRODUCED HERE, and the row says so rather than restating it as measured: the run reports this task left behind carry no numbers on a green run (an assertion's values appear only when it fails), so the controller could not re-derive 1.4-1.8 from any artifact on disk, and the review did not record where it read it. THE FIRST THING THIS ROW OWES IS THEREFORE THE MEASUREMENT ITSELF. WHY IT MAY MATTER ANYWAY: `ANCHOR_Y_PX` next to it is 8, and the case's own docblock says the failures it exists to catch are 'hundreds of pixels wide' -- a popup at the window's corner reads left ~ 0 -- so the arm does not need 2 px of discrimination to do its job, while a threshold that close to the placement it measures is a false red waiting for a second device pixel ratio. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: read the popup's actual placement rule (the menu's own offset, not a sample) and either widen the horizontal tolerance toward the vertical one, keeping a red proof that a corner-anchored popup still reddens the arm, or record that the 1.4-1.8 reading was wrong and the arm has real headroom. NOTE: the case's red proof was taken at `83072e99` against the 2 px threshold, so widening it invalidates that proof and it has to be re-taken -- which is why this is a row and not a drive-by edit.

title: A triage cell's own command can collect nothing and still read as a repro, and three such cells have no owner
detail: FOUND BY the Task 2.4b task review (2026-10-12), observation 9 of eleven, and filed rather than fixed because the repair is a sweep of every cell rather than one line. WHAT IT IS: each row's triage cell names the command that is supposed to reproduce it. Some of those `--grep` patterns match no case title, so the command exits non-zero with 'No tests found' and proves nothing -- while the cell still reads as a repro a reader will trust. THREE KNOWN INSTANCES, each already recorded on its own row rather than here: `vg-028`'s cell grep collects zero tests; `vg-158`'s cell runs `--grep "delet"` and collected nothing until Task 2.4a added a matching case, the archived row carrying the precedent for recording this on the row; and `vg-259`'s cell runs `--grep "diffuses it by the same amount"` against `glass-circle-parity.spec.ts`, which matches no title -- measured unpiped it exits 1, 'Total: 0 tests in 0 files'. A FOURTH FLAVOUR: `vg-259`'s cell names a config whose viewport is a desktop 1680x1000 while the row's title narrates the phone, so the command it names is not the surface the row is about. A FIFTH: a `--grep` value can match an assertion MESSAGE rather than a case title, so it looks like it collects a case and does not. SCALE: the six tables under `docs/product/triage/` carry 36 `--grep` occurrences, two of them prose mentions rather than commands; how many of the rest collect nothing is NOT established, and establishing it is this row's first task. WHY IT COSTS MORE THAN TIDINESS: a cell that collects nothing returns a red exit that reads like a failing repro, so a reader triaging the row cannot tell it from a command that ran and failed, and no one owns the class. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a sweep running each cell's own command in its `--list` form -- collection only, no browser, no preview port -- correcting each pattern to a real title or recording on the cell that it collects nothing. PATTERN NOTE for that sweep: Playwright compiles `--grep` as `new RegExp(pattern, "gi")`, so a pattern is a case-insensitive regexp, not a literal substring.

title: The inspector's geometry funnel refuses a non-finite value but still commits a coercible one, where the branch above it refuses an unreadable path
detail: FOUND BY the Task 2.4b task review (2026-10-12), observation 8, while the task was adding a finiteness guard to that same branch. WHAT THE TASK DID: the Line-endpoints branch of `writeShapeGeometryField` in `selection-inspector/panel.ts` wrote `object.set(key, Number(value))` unfenced, and Task 2.4b added a `Number.isFinite` refusal, which is how `vg-376` closed. WHAT THAT DOES NOT COVER: `Number` coerces before the guard can see it, so `Number("")` is 0, `Number("  ")` is 0, `Number("0x10")` is 16 and `Number("1e5")` is 100000 -- every one finite, every one committed. The sibling branch in the same function refuses an unreadable value outright through `parsedPath`, and the React control's own `parse` refuses those four inputs too, so the funnel is the one caller that disagrees with both. WHY IT IS A ROW AND NOT A DRIVE-BY FIX: whether the funnel's contract is 'a finite number' or 'a complete number' is a decision, and the two callers the funnel feeds do not agree today; guessing it would change what an author can type. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: decide the contract, then either refuse everything `ControlNumber.parse` refuses or record that the coercion is intended. NOT A LIVE REGRESSION: the guard is strictly tighter than the write it replaced, so nothing this row names was reachable only before it.

title: The rebound-chord case's red proof plants the shared projection, so the chip assertion fails first and the sheet's own read is never exercised
detail: FOUND BY the Task 2.4b task review (2026-10-12), observation 7, on the browser case Task 2.4b added for `vg-284` -- 'a chord rebound in the Keyboard tab is the chord the `?` sheet prints'. WHAT THE CASE ASSERTS, IN ORDER: the Keyboard tab's chip for `publish.surface` starts on its default chord; after arming the row and pressing a free chord the chip prints that chord; and after closing the dialog the `?` sheet's row for the same action prints the same chord. WHAT ITS RED PROOF ACTUALLY EXERCISES: the review reports the plant was made on the shared projection, which fails the CHIP assertion before the sheet assertion is ever reached -- so the proof establishes that the case can fail, not that the sheet half tests what it claims. THE HAZARD IT EXISTS FOR is the one `vg-284` named: a rebind that reached the Keyboard tab and stopped reaching the sheet, which is exactly the half a chip-first failure cannot reach. THE TWO SURFACES READ ONE LIVE TABLE TODAY (`editor-shell/shortcut-reference.tsx`), which is why no plant on that table can separate them. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: plant the sheet's own read rather than the shared table and confirm the sheet assertion is the one that reddens; if the two readings cannot diverge by construction, record that on the case and narrow its stated hazard to what it actually tests.

title: The Line-endpoint geometry field could not be typed into by the browser probe, and whether the field refuses or Playwright's editability wait is the obstacle is unestablished
detail: FOUND BY the Task 2.4b task review (2026-10-12), observation 5, and filed because the finding otherwise survives only inside an archived row. WHAT HAPPENED: driving the Line-endpoints geometry field with a non-numeric string in a browser, the implementer's Playwright `fill` did not complete, and the failure was never explained. TWO READINGS, NOT DISTINGUISHED HERE: if the field was in a refused state at that moment, `ControlNumber` renders `readOnly={refused !== undefined}` and Playwright waits for editability before it fills -- a mundane explanation and no defect at all; if the field was NOT refused, then an untypeable field is a live product defect and the row is a real one. Both readings fit the single observation, which is why this row states the observation and not a cause. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: record which actionability check failed and what the field's refusal state was at that moment; the second reading additionally needs its own repro. WHY IT IS NOT AN AMENDMENT TO `vg-376`: that row closed on a jsdom proof of the funnel contract, which is the right venue for a pure function over a `FabricObject`, and says nothing about whether a browser can drive the control that feeds it. Different surface, different owner, so it gets its own row rather than widening a closed one.

title: Nothing in the repo re-shoots the captures beside the drawings, and three of the five predate the chrome weight collapse
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 2.5 OF THE BACKLOG DRAIN (2026-10-12) while re-shooting vg-341's seven, not by a failing test. WHAT: nothing in the repo re-shoots the five PNGs that sit beside the drawings in `docs/design/mockups/current/` (`shell-capture-add.png`, `shell-capture-graphite.png`, `shell-capture-glyphs.png`, `settings-capture-graphite.png`, `settings-capture-editorial.png`), and three of the five predate Task 2's weight collapse (`ef81b183`, 2026-10-11) by the test vg-341 uses - their last-touch commits are ancestors of it: `shell-capture-graphite.png` at `7efea17f`, and `settings-capture-graphite.png` and `settings-capture-editorial.png` both at `b78ee264`. THE ONE THAT IS ESTABLISHED: `shell-capture-graphite.png` is byte-identical to the pre-re-shoot `shell-palette-graphite-desktop-chromium.png` (sha1sum `1998cbf2ff05a8788687ff23d3498120bc3ef98b`), so the README route is a literal copy of the evidence frame, and when Task 2.5 re-shot the seven the evidence frame moved to sha1sum `1c0eb8ad9a469888afc64e8e0948522ff935755a` while this copy kept the old bytes - a whole-shell capture whose subject is the chrome the collapse rewrote. THE ONE THAT IS NOT: for the settings pair `b78ee264` is ancestry only. The collapse did rewrite the modal's three tab glyphs (`settings.tsx`'s `SETTINGS_TAB_GLYPHS`), but at size 14 the vocabulary's weight is 1.7 (`icons.ts`'s `glyphWeight`), the same weight the file already carried, so that hunk is not evidence their pixels moved, and neither image was read against the chrome's pixels. Stated as measured, not as established. THE README'S CLAIM: it says both drawings-adjacent shell captures are 'produced by the registered actions above' (the graphite one by `captures each palette's own surface`), but running exactly that action writes only into `docs/evidence/screenshots/` - the capture helper's default directory - and leaves the drawings-adjacent file untouched; a grep of `src/web/tests` and `scripts/` finds no writer for that name at all. So the production route the README documents is a copy step nobody wrote down, which is how the set goes stale without a run failing. NOT FIXED HERE: refreshing the three means either a manual copy of the evidence frames into the drawings directory or a capture-directory override, and which of those the parity instrument means is a decision about the drawings set (vg-390 is the neighbouring question). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: each stale capture re-shot, plus either the README's production step written down or a spec that writes the file.

MEASURED SINCE FILING, same session, on the shell pair's siblings: `shell-capture-add.png` (`f069e56c`) and `shell-capture-glyphs.png` (`f7078e93`) postdate the collapse commit by ancestry, which is not the same as being right - neither was read against the chrome's pixels, so no claim is made about them here. THE DRAWING-SIDE SET IS TWELVE FILES ACROSS SIX DRAWINGS, AND ALL TWELVE ARE CURRENT AS OF 2026-10-13, THOUGH THE MECHANISM THIS ROW IS REALLY ABOUT IS UNCHANGED. **The set grew from five to twelve.** The row counted five PNGs beside the drawings; six drawings now carry a pair each. Added: `controls-capture-{graphite,editorial}.png` beside `controls.html` and `controls-light.html` (`988d1788`), and `settings-keyboard-capture-{graphite,editorial}.png` and `settings-about-capture-{graphite,editorial}.png` beside the two comparator sheets plan 8 Task 4 added (`e412c98d`). **Eight of the twelve were stale and were re-shot from the actions' own output rather than copied.** The settings six (`e412c98d`) and the shell three (`9b25aecb`). Each was measured before it was replaced, and the two families failed differently, which is worth keeping because it is how a stale capture is recognised: **the settings modal's moved in geometry** — the fresh Appearance and About renders are 2px shorter and the Keyboard render 6px narrower, read off the IHDR (312/224 against 314/226; 498 against 504) — while **the shell's moved in pixels at identical dimensions**, `shell-palette-light` being 1280x720 in both at 415108 bytes against 421995. The causes are the 2026-10-13 commits: `69e6e7f1`'s `dl > div` padding and `7a92d0fe`'s dialog section-2 body role for the modal, `7a92d0fe`'s dark-base tokens, `d0c67844`'s canvas clusters and `8b1b9106`'s rail for the shell. **The controls pair is the exception, and it is the useful one.** Its fresh capture is byte-identical to the images already committed, so the fixture page's rendering did not move under the same commits that moved the shell — which is what makes this staleness a per-surface fact rather than a global one, and why re-shooting everything was not the conclusion. **The `docs/evidence/screenshots/` copies were refreshed wherever a drawing-side file was**, so the two copies of each capture agree. **WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS THE ROW'S OWN SUBJECT.** Nothing in the repo re-shoots these; every one of today's was manual, run under `VIGILIA_CAPTURE` with `VIGILIA_CAPTURE_DIR` pointed at the drawings' directory. And no gate notices a stale image: the drawings gate enumerates `*.html` and skips a PNG beside a drawing without reading it. **The rest of the committed corpus was not measured** — the same shape applies to any capture shot before the 2026-10-13 chrome fixes, and which of the sixty-nine files in `docs/evidence/screenshots/` those are is still an open measurement. NEAR ROWS: `vg-435` (the gate that does not run `design:check`, the same class of a rule the repo believes is enforced); `vg-390` (the acceptance item whose evidence these captures are); `vg-436` (the drawing name one of the refreshed pairs sits beside). SECOND MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-13 -- THE CORPUS WAS SAMPLED RATHER THAN LEFT UNMEASURED: of the sixty-eight PNGs in `docs/evidence/screenshots/`, **thirty were re-shot and six were verified current; thirty-two are still unmeasured**. **METHOD, because the method is the finding.** Every capture action was re-run on a bundle built from HEAD with `VIGILIA_CAPTURE=1` and `VIGILIA_CAPTURE_DIR` pointed at a scratch directory outside the repo, then each output was compared against the committed file with `cmp` **after an existence check**. That check is not decoration: `cmp` fails on a missing file exactly as it fails on a changed one, and the first pass at the inspector column read three captures as stale when the scratch directory simply did not hold them -- they were in three other tests. Anyone repeating this must check existence first or they will manufacture staleness. **WHAT CAME BACK STALE, AND IT IS NEARLY EVERYTHING THAT PREDATES 2026-10-13.** The thirty re-shot: the settings modal's six (`e412c98d`), the shell's eight (`9b25aecb`), `pane-document` and the inspector column's three (`26dd3661`), and the editor spec's twelve (`559d3346`). Two signatures, and both are how a stale capture is told from a corrupt copy -- **the modal's moved in geometry** (IHDR 312/224 against 314/226, 498 against 504) and **everything else moved in pixels at identical dimensions** (the shell 1280x720 both, 415108 against 421995 bytes; `editor-toolbar` 392276 against 399286; `editor-inspector-chart` 276x1281 both). The cause is the 2026-10-13 chrome work: `69e6e7f1`'s `dl > div` padding and `7a92d0fe`'s dialog section-2 body role for the modal, `7a92d0fe`'s dark-base tokens, `d0c67844`'s canvas clusters and `8b1b9106`'s rail for the rest. The editor spec's twelve were all written by one commit, `f069e56c` on 2026-10-12, so they were a single day stale. **WHAT CAME BACK CURRENT, WHICH IS THE USEFUL NEGATIVE.** Six: `control-set-desktop-chromium`, `control-set-editorial-desktop-chromium`, `pane-add`, `pane-composition`, `pane-tokens` and `editor-inspector-card`. Each is byte-identical to a fresh run, and each renders a surface the 2026-10-13 fixes did not touch -- the control fixture page, three of the four rail panes, and the card-shaped inspector column. **So this is a per-surface staleness, not a global one**, and re-shooting the whole corpus blind would have been the wrong conclusion even though nearly everything sampled was stale. **THE THIRTY-TWO STILL UNMEASURED, NAMED SO THE NEXT PASS IS A LIST RATHER THAN A SEARCH**: `composition-panel-{document,starter,two-hundred}`; `editor-reference-{capture,dpr2,journey,new,overlap}`; `editor-snap-resize` and `editor-snap-resize-ctrl`; `keyboard-{armed-row,reference,tooltip}`; `host-theme-thumbnail-desktop-chromium`; `player-reference-desktop-host`; `publish-loop-live-publish`; and fifteen more editor captures (`artboard-gradient`, `assets`, `background-media`, `chart-creation`, `glass-authoring`, `live-text`, `palette-reassignment`, `palette-solid`, `panel-authoring`, `starter-backdrop`, `starter-cpu-card`, `text-reads`, `type-preset`, `type-reassignment`, `zoom-readout`). Most belong to specs other than the editor shell's, so they need their own runs and their own projects -- `player-reference` is `desktop-host` and `publish-loop-live-publish` is `own-host`. **WHAT REMAINS THE ROW'S OWN SUBJECT.** Nothing re-shoots any of this automatically; all thirty of today's were manual. No gate notices a stale image -- the drawings gate enumerates `*.html` and skips a PNG beside a drawing without reading it. **And the sampled result is an argument for the mechanism rather than for thirty more manual passes**: at thirty of thirty-six stale, the periodic re-shoot is the load, and whether it becomes a checked instrument or a scheduled act is the decision this row has always been asking for. COVERAGE, NOT ONLY STALENESS, MEASURED 2026-10-13. Re-shooting the registered Add pane capture (`editor-shell-add` / "captures the shell with the Add pane open and nothing selected") to place it beside the change that gave the pane free control boxes their own type, the fresh frame was inspected and shows NONE of the changed region: the Asset group draws its Import, Replace and Remove boxes below the pane fold, and the capture is a viewport frame, so the drawing `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html` carries three controls the frame registered for the same state does not show. The re-shot file was therefore left uncommitted, its pixels differing only by re-encode. That is a second face of this row: a capture can be current and still compare nothing for a region the drawing draws, and no gate reads either property.

title: Eleven register rows cite a design file that was deleted, five of them live
detail: FOUND BY the Task 2.5 fix round 2 (2026-10-12), which corrected this defect on `vg-306` and then measured the class rather than the instance. WHAT: `docs/design/design-language.md` no longer exists -- `db000c40` (2026-10-11) deleted it when the bible became the root `DESIGN.md` -- and rows still cite it by line, so a reader following one lands on nothing. MEASURED 2026-10-12 by grep over both register files: **five live rows carry eight line citations** (`vg-308` 1, `vg-317` 1, `vg-319` 4, `vg-320` 1, `vg-326` 1), and the archive carries **six rows with ten** (`vg-295` 1, `vg-294` 2, `vg-303` 1, `vg-321` 1, `vg-296` 3, `vg-325` 2). Rows that mention the name without a line number are historical prose and are not counted here (8 live rows mention it, 7 archived). WHY IT IS A ROW AND NOT A DRIVE-BY FIX: three of the five live rows (`vg-317`, `vg-320`, `vg-326`) belong to other tasks, and a citation to a deleted file is the rot that reads as current until someone follows it -- `vg-306`'s was fixed only because that row was being read for another reason. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: rewrite each live citation to the `DESIGN.md` marker and line that now carries the rule, or record on the row that the number has no successor; the six archived rows are for the record and need nothing. THE TRAP FOR THAT REWRITE: `DESIGN.md` carries `§N` body markers and `design:md --cite` fails when a citation names a number with no marker, so a number must be re-derived rather than ported -- `vg-306`'s own §5 bound is now `DESIGN.md:411`, under the `<!-- §5 -->` marker at `DESIGN.md:398`.

title: The colour picker and the gradient editor are barely usable, in the user's own words after using them
detail:
FOUND BY THE USER, 2026-10-12, in one sentence and without a repro: "Both the color picker & gradient editor is barely useable at the moment btw. Do a research of common solutions and follow them." WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: the two components exist at `src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/colour-picker.tsx` and `gradient-editor.tsx`, they are reached from the paint surfaces in `panes/tokens/`, and the gradient editor holds at least one raw literal no token owns (`gradient-editor.tsx:79`, the 1px ring `vg-334` rules on). WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and is the reason this is a row rather than a fix: which properties make them hard to use -- the user gave a verdict, not a measurement, and the components have not been read against a pattern set. WHAT CLOSES IT: a research pass naming what established tools do (the consensus pattern set and the genuine forks), an assessment of each component against that set with file:line evidence, and then the rebuild or the amendments that follow -- which is this row plus whatever the research files. ROUTE: the rebuild touches `DESIGN.md`'s section 5 control vocabulary, so it needs a design decision before code, and it is not part of the active plan (the backlog drain), so it takes its own spec and plan rather than a task inside another.

RULED 2026-10-15: **SCHEDULED AHEAD OF THE TRIAGE, and it enters a phase.** It is a defect rather than a wish — the user's own verdict after using the picker and the gradient editor is that they are "barely usable" — so it is fixed, not parked. It and `vg-388` are the two user-sourced rows among the 95 and both move ahead of the rest.

title: ADR-0040 requires the guard's self-test to live in the same file, so the mandate now forces design-tokens.mjs past the 800-line stop
detail: FOUND BY THE TASK 4.2 TASK REVIEW (2026-10-12), finding L2, and filed rather than fixed because the fix contradicts a recorded decision. WHAT: `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` was 640 lines at Task 4.2's base and is 975 after its first two commits -- the set-shaped ceiling, the site-keyed exemptions and the allowlist-consumer rule, each with its self-test cases. `AGENTS.md` calls 800 a stop for normal source files, so the file is past it by 175 lines. THE TWO CANDIDATE CUTS DO NOT REACH, measured by the reviewer: extracting the 78-line CEILINGS record leaves 825, and extracting the self-test (264 lines) contradicts ADR-0040, whose own words are *the guard's own test lives behind `--self-test` in the same file and is wired into `gates:self-test`*. Both together would land near 560, which is why the pair is the shape that works and the pair is what the ADR forbids. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an amendment to ADR-0040 letting the self-test or the record live in a sibling module, provided the sibling is still chained into `gates:self-test` -- the property the ADR exists to protect is that the self-test runs, not which file holds it -- or an explicit recorded exception naming the file, as AGENTS.md allows for proven vendored source and this is not that. INTERIM RULING BY THE CONTROLLER (2026-10-12): the file stays at its length for now; the length is not squeezed to 799 and the self-test is not moved, because either action taken to satisfy a line count is the worse trade. Separate from `vg-327`/`vg-332`/`vg-340`, which are that file's rules rather than its size.

title: docs/engineering/dependencies.md's declared-dependencies table omits six names its heading claims to list, so it is not the complete provenance record it says it is
detail: FOUND BY TASK 4.3 (2026-10-13) while adding vg-385's four missing licence entries, and carried as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on commit 8477e70a rather than fixed there, because `docs/engineering/dependencies.md` is outside that task's Files and the register is another task's file. MEASURED at 8477e70a: six declared names are absent from the table - `react-dom`, `@base-ui/react`, `tailwindcss`, `@tailwindcss/vite`, `@types/react`, `@types/react-dom` - while every one of them is declared in a `src/web/**/package.json` and already present in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`. THE SAME DEFECT CLASS AS vg-385, one file over: that row's licences job reads the manifests against the notices, and nothing reads the manifests against the dependencies map, so the map can fall behind silently while `AGENTS.md` requires both files to be updated when a dependency is added. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the six were ever listed and removed, or never added; no git archaeology was done. OWNER: whoever owns `docs/engineering/dependencies.md`. SEVERITY: low as code, medium as a provenance record that reads as complete.

title: serialiseScene strips every object's derived `styles` table unconditionally, while `authoredOnly` keeps it on a run-less object as authored — so an imported package whose text carries Fabric's own per-character styling loses it silently on the next save
detail: FOUND BY TASK 5.1 (2026-10-13), by its task reviewer, while the strip that closes vg-129 was being verified. Two owners state contradictory models of the same key. `scene-fabric/src/persist.ts`'s `removeDerivedTextStyles` deletes `styles` from every object at every depth, because vg-129 measured that nothing reads it back; `editor/src/persistence-manager/index.ts`'s `authoredOnly` deliberately KEEPS `text` and `styles` on an object with no `vigiliaText.runs`, with the comment 'An object without runs owns its `text` and `styles`, so they are kept there and a real edit is never hidden'. For a product-authored document the two never disagree, because the only writer of `styles` is `fabric-text.ts` computing it from runs. They disagree for a package the product did not author: an imported or hand-edited theme whose run-less text object carries Fabric per-character styling passes the validator (scene objects are not key-enumerated - `KNOWN_KEYS` covers endpoint bags only), revives with the styling visible, and loses it on the next save with no report, unrecoverably. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED for the foreign path: no imported-package case has been driven. The decision owed is which model is true - if `styles` is unrevivable state wherever it appears (vg-129's finding) then `authoredOnly`'s comment and its `styles` branch are stale and should be amended; if a run-less object's `styles` is authored, the strip must be scoped as `removeDerivedTextClips` is, by `vigiliaText` presence, and an imported styling must survive the round trip. D7's `vg-041`/`vg-188` ruling owns what a derived property is in general, and this is that question at one key.

title: An over-large `theme.json` is answered as absent, so `bootTheme` returns `none` and the editor mounts the template under a success report over a theme it never opened — the visible defect vg-110 fixed, one trigger over
detail: FOUND BY TASK 5.3 (2026-10-13), by its task reviewer: vg-110's fix covers a theme that fails validation and leaves the row's third clause open for a theme that is refused for size instead. CAUSE ESTABLISHED, `host/src/themes/store.ts:504-506`: `readStored` returns `undefined` when the file exceeds `MAX_THEME_FILE_BYTES` (32 MiB, `:163`), before validation runs, and the file's own comment says the choice is deliberate — 'The size bound still answers `undefined`: an over-large document is not a validation failure, and naming it one here would be a different decision.' What the choice costs is that `readStoredOrAbsent` (`:522-530`) folds it into the same absence the listing and the write path use, so the open route answers `404 Theme not found`, `boot-theme.ts`'s `bootTheme` returns `none`, and `editor-main.ts` mounts the template and writes success — over a document the user has on disk, at a path the editor named. NOT THE SAME ROW AS vg-110, which is closed: that fix routes a validation failure to `422` with the validator's issues, and this path never reaches the validator. THE DECISION OWED: whether a size refusal is a third answer (`ThemeTooLargeError` with its own status, the way `ThemeConflictError` and `ThemeAssetLimitError` already sit beside `ThemeValidationError`), or whether the absence is correct and only the editor's report must stop claiming success — the second is smaller and does not answer what a caller that wants to *show* the user their theme is too large would need. Not established here: whether any real document reaches 32 MiB, and whether the write path's own refusal (`ThemeAssetLimitError` at `:751`, for assets rather than `theme.json`) already tells the user at save time. REPRODUCES with a >32 MiB `theme.json` in an `--app-dir` library and `bootTheme` against it, the instrument Task 5.3's own browser case uses.

title: `grouping-manager`'s `ownerGroup` spells the group-holder fact a third time, in a `Group | undefined` shape the new `holderOf` contract cannot take
detail: FOUND BY TASK 6.5a (2026-10-13), which was landing `vg-248`'s ruling (*scene-fabric owns 'which collection holds this object'*) and hit it while re-deriving that row's cites. `grouping-manager/index.ts` defines `const ownerGroup = (object) => object.parent` and uses it once, at `:243`; it is the same Fabric fact `holderOf` now owns, in a third shape. CAUSE ESTABLISHED. `holderOf(canvas, object) -> Canvas | Group` was deliberately not widened to it: `ownerGroup` has no canvas in scope and wants `undefined` for a top-level object, which is the shape `vg-248` deleted from `deletion-manager` rather than the one it kept, so the canvas-in contract does not fit and folding it would mean computing a holder only to narrow it back with `instanceof Group`. NOT FIXED IN THAT TASK because the contract change is a decision, not a line: either `scene-fabric`'s holder module gains a second entry point (`parentGroupOf(object): Group | undefined`, which `grouping-manager` and the projection reader below would both use) or the two are genuinely different questions that the ownership map should name apart. THE SAME SHAPE, TWO OTHER SITES, both judged NOT this fact by that task and worth re-judging together with it: `editor-shell/layer-tree.ts:466`'s `ownerOf(root, id)` answers from the projection tree by id with no canvas in scope (its own comment says the tree read is deliberate; the map gives it 'Semantic layer projection'), and `editor-shell/bridge.ts:300` uses the same test to pick a nested group's first child for the grouping manager -- a nesting question rather than a holder. REPRODUCES with `grep -rn 'parent instanceof Group' src/web/packages --include=*.ts | grep -v test` at 9eec23db, which now finds only those sites plus `object-holder.ts`'s own. D7's `vg-041`/`vg-188` ruling owns what a derived property is in general; this is an ownership question, not a derived-state one, so it is not that ruling's.

title: `arrangeEligible` re-derives the arrange refusal from a pure `ObjectTarget` while the same module also asks `canArrange`, so eligibility is a second owner of one decision — the shape `vg-365` closed, one layer up
