title: A spec interpolates a product paint into a stylesheet string, so a renamed key would render `background:undefined` and no assertion would fail
detail: FOUND BY THE TASK 11.2 REVIEW ON 2026-10-14, WHILE CHECKING THAT A RE-OWNED LITERAL STILL MEANS SOMETHING. `reference-theme.spec.ts` shows the capture it just took by handing the browser a `page.setContent` document whose body is `background:${solidOf.background}` — the value comes from `new-fabric-theme-globals` at run time and is interpolated into a string, so a palette entry that is renamed or absent renders `background:undefined`, which the browser drops as an invalid declaration and the page falls back to white. NOTHING THEN FAILS: `expect(page.locator("img")).toBeVisible()` passes, the length check on the data URL passes, and `captureVisualReview` writes a screenshot that is not a golden file — so the only reader who would notice is a person looking at the wrong-coloured picture. It is the same vacuity `tests/e2e/shell-tokens.ts`'s `themeToken` throws to prevent, in the one place the value is read from a product module instead of a stylesheet the reader parses. OWNER: the spec's own read of `solidOf` — a reader that throws on an absent key, or an assertion that the value is a non-empty string before it is interpolated. SEVERITY: low, because it is a future rename rather than a present defect; the same shape is worth a look wherever a product value is templated into CSS text.

title: `editor-fixture.ts` restates the product's `solidOf.text` as its own `INK_PAINT`, so the fixture and the palette can drift
detail: FOUND BY THE TASK 11.2 REVIEW ON 2026-10-14, IN THE FIXTURE THE TASK ITSELF ADDED. `tests/e2e/editor-fixture.ts` declares `INK_PAINT = "#ecf5ff"`, which is the value `new-fabric-theme-globals`'s `solidOf.text` owns, so the fixture is a second copy of a product value rather than a read of its owner — the same shape the task exists to remove, one level out. It is an ownership smell and not a defect: the spec pins no product value with it, so a drift would change what the fixture draws rather than what the test asserts. `PLATE_PAINT = "#101318"` beside it has no product owner at all (confirmed by grep), so it is legitimately the spec's own and stays. OWNER: the fixture. SEVERITY: low. Worth doing together with the aliasing the review also noted — `#101318` now sits in three fixtures and `#00b8d9` in two, each authored independently for its own document, which is fine until one of them means the same thing as another.

title: No command runs a typecheck, so `npm run gate` reads green over source its own compiler rejects
detail: FOUND BY THE AGENT FIXING THE LINE CADENCE (2026-10-14), filed from that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer (`fd27dee6`). `npm run gate` is `biome check .. && gates:self-test && design:check && test`, and `test` is `vitest run` — vitest transpiles without typechecking, so **no `tsc --noEmit` runs anywhere in the one command that means green**. MEASURED: at `f790b77d` the commit landed with `npm run typecheck` exit 1 — `packages/editor/src/chart-manager/index.dom.test.ts:906`, TS2345, a chart built with `family: "line" | "gauge"` into a discriminated union on that key — while every gate step it did run was green. Repaired in `fd27dee6`; `npm run typecheck` is exit 0 across all seven workspaces at that commit. So the gap is not theoretical: one commit carried a type error through a green gate on 2026-10-14, and only a reader of a subagent's report found it. RELATION TO `vg-192`, which is the neighbouring row and NOT the same one: `vg-192` says no tsconfig includes `tests/e2e`, so a browser spec is untypechecked because it is unowned. This row says the gate runs no compiler at all, so **`vg-192`'s fix is inert on its own** — adding a tsconfig for `tests/e2e` changes nothing while no command runs `tsc`, and equally nothing runs it over the packages. Whatever fixes this one is what makes that one's tsconfig mean something. NOT FIXED IN THE SAME PASS because the fix is a decision rather than an edit: adding `typecheck` to `gate` changes what the gate costs (seven workspaces, seconds each) and what a phase close may claim, and it is a change to the command every other close is measured against — the register's own rule sends a fix that needs a design decision to a row rather than to a commit.

title: Nothing reads the shell drawing's view cluster, so the three glyph squares can return to 22px with every check still green
detail: FOUND BY THE REVIEW OF `d7ef633b` (2026-10-14), which is the change that moved the three zoom/fit squares to §5's 26px. The value is now pinned by two things that cannot see it: the drawings README states the bound as prose, and `PARITY` in `tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts` has no region reading `current/shell.html`'s view cluster — the nearest regions are the controls pair, which is a different drawing. `mockup-values.test.ts` reads drawing values only through `PARITY` rows, so it stays green. `editor-display.spec.ts` asserts only that hover does not move the box, and `display-switch.tsx` sets the class with no inline size, so the product side is not asserted either. MEASURED at the review: `shell.html:160,163,166` read `width:26px;height:26px; border-radius:6px`, and nothing in the suite reddens if they read 22px again. NOT FIXED IN THE SAME PASS because the guard belongs to the parity instrument, not to the drawing: a `PARITY` row is the shape Phase 10.2 is already adding regions in, and the product is 26px at `editor-shell.css`'s `.editor-shell-view-step`, so a row on the squares' `width` would redden on a drawing regression without moving the product. The row is filed rather than folded into Phase 10.2's list because 10.2's subject is the settings modal's regions and nothing yet says the shell drawing's view cluster is in scope.

title: A fake drive's capacity drifts, because `disk.total` and `disk.data.total` end in `total` and are answered by the fallback profile
detail: FOUND BY TASK 12'S `vg-029` FIX (2026-10-15, commit `728f03e0`), which gave `ram.total` and `vram.total` a constant through a lookup table. The same shape reaches a drive: any vocabulary key whose last segment is `total` has no entry in `PROFILES`, so it falls to `FALLBACK_PROFILE` (min 0, max 100, period 37 s, unit ""), and a capacity that drifts across 0..100 is nonsense in the preview. MEASURED at that task's verification: `disk.total` answered 81.29 and `disk.data.total` 10.167 nineteen seconds apart, in unit "" — the value moves and the unit is wrong for a byte count. NOT FIXED THERE because `vg-029`'s ruling covers RAM and VRAM alone, and deciding a fake drive's capacity is a design question the ruling does not answer: what a drive holds is a property of the themed device rather than of the waveform, the per-device `disk.<id>.total` keys need an answer too, and the unit has to become a byte count. The fix is a decision before it is a table entry, so it is filed rather than guessed.

title: A licence's date attaches to the first line of its quotation, so a wrapped quotation reworded on a later line still dates to the older commit
detail: FOUND BY THE SCOPED RE-REVIEW OF THE LICENCE POLICY (2026-10-15, of `13015088`), which otherwise confirmed both ruled corrections landed: `ci.yml:37-44` sets `fetch-depth: 0`, and `requireFullHistory` proved on a real `git clone --depth 1` refuses loudly (exit 1, seven failures each naming the shallow checkout). THIS IS THE ONE REMAINING HOLE IN WHAT THE POLICY REFUSES. `tests/e2e/mockup-values.test.ts:896` blames the quotation's FIRST LINE alone, so a quotation wrapped across lines whose LATER lines the citing commit rewords still dates to the commit that wrote the first line — and the refusal that exists to catch a rule amended by the commit citing it does not fire. DEMONSTRATED at `C:\tmp\vigilia-drain\blameprobe\`: with a three-line quotation, line 2 blamed to commit A and line 3 to commit B after B reworded only line 3, the policy read A. The fix is that the date is the newest commit among the lines the quotation spans, not the commit its first line carries. NOT FIXED IN THE SAME PASS because the change is to the policy's own dating rule and its regression case has to be built from a wrapped quotation whose later line is amended — a fixture rather than an edit — and the controller was mid-Phase-13 with four implementers holding the tree.

title: LicenceLedger.design is declared and filled but read by nothing, so the ledger carries a field the policy never consults
detail: FOUND BY THE SCOPED RE-REVIEW OF THE LICENCE POLICY (2026-10-15, of `13015088`). The field is declared at `tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:816` and filled at `mockup-values.test.ts:934`, and nothing reads it: `licenceSources` reads `sections` instead, and a grep for `\.design\b` over both files returns no match. SO THE LEDGER CARRIES TWO VIEWS OF THE SAME DRAWING AND ONLY ONE IS CONSULTED — which is the shape that misleads a later reader into filling the wrong one, and the same shape `vg-386`'s sweep was looking for. Either the field is read or it goes; the reviewer could not establish which was intended, since both were written in `13015088` by the same hand.

title: The three scrollbar tokens are :root literals that follow no palette, so a dark shell paints a light thumb
detail: FOUND WHILE CONSUMING THEM, in `3328ae33` (the user's item 1, `vg-458`), and reported in that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer. `--vigilia-scrollbar-thumb`, `-thumb-hover` and `-track` are declared once on `:root` in `editor-shell/editor-shell.css` as literal colour values and are produced by no palette, so every palette that is not a light one paints the light thumb. Item 1's own words are "themed to be consistent with the shell theme", and that holds in the light palettes only — a graphite shell reads a `#c9c2b1` thumb against its own ground. NOT FIXED IN `3328ae33` because the fix is a palette-aware trio, which is a NEW PAINT VALUE, and that task's brief forbids adding one. THE DECISION IS THEREFORE A PALETTE OWNER'S, not a CSS edit: either the trio joins the palette token set so every palette declares its own, or the scrollbar is built from tokens a palette already owns (`docs/architecture/ownership.md` names the paint owner). A register row rather than an on-the-fly fix for that reason — the correct behaviour is not yet written down anywhere. **THE CASE THIS FIX WILL MEET, added 2026-10-15 from the 13.5 review:** 13.5’s new case "both shell scrollers carry the scrollbar tokens" (`shell-appearance.spec.ts`) fixes its expected value by appending a reference `div` to `document.body` and reading `--vigilia-scrollbar-*` from there. That anchor resolves whatever `:root` declares, so a fix that moves the trio to `.editor-shell` (or any narrower scope) leaves the reference unresolved — and an unresolved `var()` makes the declaration invalid at computed-value time, which reds the case on its own guard ("the reference's own scrollbar-width did not resolve") rather than on the scrollers. Expect that red and update the anchor with the scope; it is not a regression in the scrollers.

title: Two scrollers are portalled outside .editor-shell, so the context menu and the settings sheet keep the platform scrollbar
detail: FOUND WHILE MEASURING WHERE THE SCROLLBAR TOKENS REACH, in `3328ae33` (the user's item 1, `vg-458`), and reported in that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer. The canvas context menu's popup and the settings dialog's sheet are both portalled, so the two rules the commit adds — on `.editor-shell-panel` and `.editor-shell-inspector` — never reach them and they paint the OS scrollbar. ITEM 1 AS THE USER WROTE IT IS "anywhere in the GUI", so the commit satisfies it for the pane column and the inspector and not yet for the interface as a whole. NEEDS A DECISION RATHER THAN A PATCH: the tokens reach these surfaces only if the rule moves to a scope a portalled node also resolves (the document root, or wherever the shell's portalled layer mounts), or if each portalled surface opts in by name. The first is one owner and a wider blast radius; the second is two edits and a list that must not go stale. Not fixed in `3328ae33` because its brief owned the two shell scrollers, and this row names the boundary it left. **THE CASE THIS FIX WILL MEET, added 2026-10-15 from the 13.5 review:** 13.5’s new case "both shell scrollers carry the scrollbar tokens" (`shell-appearance.spec.ts`) queries `.editor-shell-panel` and `.editor-shell-inspector` by class and asserts each one's computed `scrollbar-width`/`scrollbar-color`. Either remedy this row offers — widening the rule to a scope a portalled node resolves, or opting each portalled surface in by name — moves or duplicates those selectors, so the case must be widened to the portalled surfaces in the same change. As it stands it pins the two shell scrollers and says nothing about the menu and the sheet, which is exactly the boundary this row names.

title: The dock's :disabled rules style a greyed half that no longer exists, and the dead-code sweep runs over them without a finding
detail: FOUND BY TASK 13.1b while materialising its own `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer (`82692760`). `.editor-shell-dock button:disabled` and `.editor-shell-dock button:disabled:hover` (`editor-shell.css:2514` and `:2518`) paint a refused arrange button — the opacity and the transparent hover border the dock used while it greyed the eight instead of withholding them. **`4927f2f0` (`vg-463`) moved those eight to the inspector and made this surface filter**, so no button in the dock can be in that state: `grep -n disabled canvas-dock.tsx` returns nothing, and the dock's one action button (`canvas-dock.tsx:47-56`) sets no `disabled` attribute at all. Both rules are therefore dead. **WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A DELETION:** the same two rules would match any future dock button that does disable, so they are only correct to remove while nothing does — and that is a measurement rather than a fact about the selector. **Two consequences worth separating.** First, this is the same class as the four pieces of text `13.1b` corrected: something describing a surface the phase replaced. Second, and larger — `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs` runs inside `gates:self-test`, which `npm run gate` runs, and it reported nothing here. **That is `vg-386`'s subject** (its sweep of 133 candidates, none proven dead) and this is a concrete instance its scope did not reach rather than a reason to reopen it. The reading is a grep and a source read; no test asserts either way, so what a later session needs is the measurement, which is above.

title: Two DESIGN.md citations name source lines that moved, and design:md --cite passes over them because it checks the marker rather than the target
detail: FOUND BY TASK 13.1b while rewriting `DESIGN.md` §7.4 (`82692760`), and reported in that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer. The subject sentence cited `ui-copy.ts:207` and `inspector-sections.spec.ts:786`. **Both were correct when they were written at `303dfdf6`, rotted at `785a0a2e`, and 13.1b's own three added lines moved the target a third time, to `:291`** — so a line citation rots on any commit that edits above it, including the commit that reads it. **`npm run design:check` exits 0 over all of it.** `design:md --cite` validates that a citation names a `§N` marker which exists — the rule `§N` markers are stable and never renumbered is what makes them dependable — but it does not check that a cited `file:line` still holds what the citing sentence says. So a citation can point at an unrelated line and the gate stays green, which is how these two survived two commits and were caught only by an implementer reading the file. **THIS IS `vg-434`'s GAP IN A SECOND FILE**, not a reopening of it: that row owns plans-directory references resolving to nothing (55 of 70 register rows, 32 of 82 path tokens), and this is a citation whose target exists but no longer says that. THE DECISION IS WHETHER A CITATION MAY NAME A LINE AT ALL, or must name a symbol — a line cannot be stable in a file any commit may edit, and the fix is either a check that resolves the target or a convention that the target is a name.

title: ControlIconButton ignores ControlProps.describedById, so a control handed the pane's standing note loses it silently
detail: FOUND BY TASK 13.3 while correcting ADR 0044's claims, and reported in that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer (`e572c302`). `ControlProps` declares the field at `components/ui/control-well.tsx:38` with the reason written beside it — *'An element outside this control that describes it — the pane's own standing note, whose id the control cannot mint'* — and four controls read it (`control-number.tsx:62`, `control-select.tsx:90`, `control-pair.tsx:45`, `control-well.tsx`). `components/ui/control-icon-button.tsx` reads `refused` at `:65` and routes it to `aria-describedby` at `:92` and to a drawn reason at `:102-104`, and **never reads `describedById` at all** — so an icon button handed a standing note is announced without it, and nothing fails, which is why it took a reader to find. **WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX:** the cause is named and the fix is a few lines, but *which* icon buttons are handed a note and *what* the note is are owned by the panes that draw them, so the correct behaviour is not yet specified anywhere — it needs the panes' owners looked at, not this file. `ControlProps.describedById`'s own comment names the artboard's size note as the case that motivated the field, and the artboard draws a control well rather than an icon button, so the unmet case is a surface the field was not written for. **Consequence worth separating:** ADR 0044 records its second path (`components/ui/`) as claimed and not taken because of this, so the note and the code now disagree about whether that path is in play.

title: A construction dispatched through bridge.run reaches the session façade unwrapped, where the Add pane's private constructing() is what reports a refusal
detail: FOUND BY TASK 13.3 while implementing `vg-460` (the pane footer's constructions), and reported in that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer (`e572c302`). The footer now offers the constructions (`CONSTRUCTION_ACTIONS` in `object-actions.ts`), `bridge.can` exempts them from the selection gate, and `bridge.run` dispatches them — but **the rail the Add pane uses is not the rail they now take**: `panes/add/add-pane.tsx`'s own `constructing()` is what catches and reports a refused construction, and it is private to that pane. A construction that arrives through `bridge.run` is not wrapped by it, so **a refusal is silent from the footer** — in the bare case a theme with no usable token. **ALREADY TRUE, NEWLY REACHABLE:** the canvas context menu shares that route today, so this is not a defect 13.3 introduced; what 13.3 changed is that a second and more prominent surface now takes it. **WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX:** the cause is named but the remedy is a decision rather than a line — either the refusal reporting moves to the session façade (one owner, and the Add pane's private helper retires) or the facade returns an outcome each caller reports (two owners, and the footer and the menu must agree on the words). That is the shape the bug rule files rather than fixes, and `vg-422`'s subject (who owns a refusal's words) is adjacent without being the same.

title: A File menu row's accessible name now carries its chord, so six e2e locators that match with exact: true no longer match it
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by the controller while reading the browser suite, and ROOT-CAUSED rather than left as a flake: `composition-panel.spec.ts:931` and `:1111` fail at 30s and at 120s alike, in the shared helper `openPackageWithTiming` (`:682`), whose second line is `getByRole("menuitem", { name: "Open package", exact: true })`. **Playwright's failure snapshot shows the menu open and the row present** — `menuitem "Open package Control O" [ref=e16]` — so the element the case wants is rendered and its accessible name has simply grown the chord. **MECHANISM, read from the source rather than inferred from the symptom:** `editor-shell/shell-menu-bar.tsx:182` gives the row's `<kbd>` child `aria-label={shortcutSpokenLabel(shortcut)}`. A child with its own accessible name contributes it to the parent's computed name, so a row that prints a chord now announces as `"<label> <spoken chord>"` and an `exact: true` match against the bare label fails. The rows affected are exactly those the same file gives a fourth `item()` argument — `openPackage` and `savePackage`, i.e. the two the snapshot shows as "Open package Control O" and "Save package Control S"; `New from starter`, `Release package` and the library rows carry no chord and are unaffected. **SIX SITES IN FIVE FILES, listed so a fix does not fix two of them:** `composition-panel.spec.ts:690` and `author-journey-display.spec.ts:229` (`"Open package"`), and `author-journey-display.spec.ts:199`, `author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts:926`, `editor.spec.ts:5274`, `glass-authoring.spec.ts:177` (`"Save package"`). **Three of the six were not executed while this was found** — only `composition-panel.spec.ts` was run — so whether they are red today is unmeasured and must be measured rather than assumed. **WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX:** the cause is named but the correct side is a decision and not a line. The product's behaviour is defensible — a screen reader hearing the chord is the point of the `aria-label` — which makes the six specs the stale side; but the `exact: true` may have been deliberate in one of them, and dropping `exact` from a menu locator widens it to substring matches, which is a different risk. **AND THE LARGER POINT THE REVIEWER'S vg-210 ALREADY PAID FOR:** this case was red at base once before (the `enterLayer` failure), was measured then, and is red again now at a different line for a different reason. A browser suite whose reds are re-attributed by hand every phase is one where a real regression cannot be told from a rotted locator, which is the gap `vg-179`'s neighbours own.

title: grouping-manager.group() removes each member with the same canvas.remove that disposes it, so a grouped chart is disposed exactly as a reparented one was
detail: FOUND BY TASK 13.3's fix round while fixing `vg-461`'s reparent disposal (P1 of that task's review), and reported in that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer (`154e55ef`). The fix replaced the reparent path's root-side `canvas.remove` with a `detachFromRoot` that splices `_objects` and does not fire `object:removed`, **because `canvas.remove` synchronously triggers the scene adapter's `target.dispose()` (`scene-fabric/src/adapter.ts:62`) on an object the document still holds** — an object that still serializes, so a save that looks right reloads wrong. **The same call sits on a second path with a different owner.** `grouping-manager.group()` removes each member from the canvas by that same `canvas.remove`, so with the scene adapter installed a chart inside a grouping is disposed identically. **Measured, not inferred:** the fix round's probe returns `{grouped: true, disposed: true}`. **WHY A ROW AND NOT A FIX IN THAT COMMIT:** it is the manager's own write rather than the reparent path's, so the change belongs to the manager's owner — and the manager may have a reason to want the removal event that the reparent path did not, which is a question about `group()` rather than about `moveLayer`. **The two are the same defect with two owners**, which is the bug rule's own case for filing rather than fixing on the fly. **What an owner needs is the probe, which is above**, since the symptom is invisible: the grouping is correct, the serialized scene is correct, and only the rendered backing canvas is gone. **RE-REVIEWED 2026-10-15 (`a93f010206bcb668d`): the shared cause is named, and it is the adapter's listener rather than either caller.** `scene-fabric/src/adapter.ts:61-64` subscribes `canvas.on("object:removed", ({ target }) => { target.dispose(); })`, so *any* foreign root removal disposes the target. **There is a third `canvas.remove` call site, and it is not a third defect:** `crop-manager/index.ts:84` removes a locally-constructed transient `Rect` (`:114`) that was never a document object, so that disposal is correct and the defect sites stay two — this one and `bridge.ts`'s reparent. The adapter's rule is still the one question both share: it disposes what *anyone* removes rather than what **it** removes, and that is why the crop site is named on this row at all — the fix moves the disposal obligation onto every genuine removal site, `crop-manager` included. **That fix is a design decision on a watchlisted path** — `scene-fabric/src/adapter.ts` is on `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs`'s WATCHLIST, so it needs an ADR claiming the path — and it moves the disposal obligation onto every genuine removal site (the adapter's own `clear`, `reusable` and `removeStale`, plus the editor's `deletion-manager` and `crop-manager`), which is why it is a row rather than this task's fix round. **Interim:** 13.3's fix round 2 makes `detachFromRoot` restore the state Fabric's own removal leaves — no `_activeObject` or `_hoveredTarget` left pointing at an object that has left the root — so the reparent path corrupts nothing while this is open; `grouping-manager.group()` keeps the defect until this lands.

title: Fabric's own removal hook clears `_hoveredTarget` and `_hoveredTargets` but not `_hoveredActualTarget`, so a removed object is still reported as a hover event's `oldActualTarget`
detail: FOUND BY TASK 13.3's fix round 2 while reproducing `Canvas._onObjectRemoved`'s cleanup for the reparent path, and reported in that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer (`c17ce13f`). The hook clears `_hoveredTarget` and `_hoveredTargets` (`fabric/src/canvas/Canvas.ts:1220`, `:1236`) and leaves `_hoveredActualTarget` pointing at the object, so the next hover event's payload can name a removed object as `oldActualTarget`. **Not this path's defect, and parity is unaffected:** `detachFromRoot` reproduces what the hook does, so the reparent path and a real `canvas.remove` leave the same `_hoveredActualTarget` — the new parity case compares the two states and passes. **Why a row rather than a fix:** the field is Fabric's and the omission is Fabric's, so an editor-side write would be a fourth private field reproduced by hand with nothing to check it against — the shape this task spent two rounds removing. **What an owner needs to decide** is whether any consumer reads `oldActualTarget` in a way a stale object can reach: measured cause is above, the consumer is unestablished. The related `hovered` accounting lives in `editor-shell/bridge.ts`'s `detachFromRoot` and its docstring.

title: The Add pane's eight card unit tiles are still hand-authored SVG, and item 2's wording says every icon is Lucide while DESIGN.md section 6 licenses a unit tile to carry a diagram
detail: FOUND BY TASK 13.2b (item 2's unmet half) while bringing the pane's shape and text tiles into the one icon vocabulary, and reported in that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer (`ffa23c9c`). The remaining hand-authored glyphs are `panes/add/card-diagrams.tsx`'s eight unit tiles, which `icons.test.tsx`'s `EXEMPT_SOURCES` still exempts. **It is not a defect against the design language, and the escape is real:** `DESIGN.md`'s Icons section (`### Icons`, `:520`, marker `<!-- §6 -->` at `:522`) says a *card unit* in the Add pane is not arbitrary — the card library is a fixed set of eight — so a unit tile may carry a diagram of what it builds (`:544-547`), which is the one licence the file grants for a non-family glyph. **The open question is item 2's scope rather than the code's:** the user's own words were "every icon Lucide", and eight glyphs are diagrams by rule. So the decision is whether the item is discharged for those eight because the acceptance instrument licenses them, or whether the user's wording requires them to move too — which is the user's to make, and it is why this is a row rather than a line in a commit. **What an owner needs:** `icons.test.tsx`'s `EXEMPT_SOURCES` names them, so the exemption is visible and cannot be forgotten; the work, if ruled, is eight diagrams in the one family or an explicit exemption recorded in `DESIGN.md` rather than only in a test list.

title: An unknown chart family wears bar's mark while the row's role abstains, so the row reads Bar for a chart the document never called a bar
detail: FOUND BY TASK 13.2b'S TASK REVIEW (its finding 2), 2026-10-15, which measured the rendering rather than reading it. **The tree is careful and the mark undoes it.** `layer-tree.ts`'s `chartMark` (`:207-216`) reports a family this build cannot name as `family: undefined`, and its own doc says why — "the row would then claim a chart is a gauge when the document says otherwise, which is the one thing a mark must never do". The mark then does exactly that, one layer up: `panes/composition/kind-mark.tsx:40-43`'s `chartFamilyGlyph` returns `CHART_FALLBACK` for an absent family *and* for one it cannot name, and `CHART_FALLBACK` is `CHART_BAR_GLYPH` (`:27`). **Nothing else on the row corrects it.** The role abstains rather than disclaiming — `ui-copy.ts:54-57` renders an unknown family as the kind word "Chart" — so the row reads `Bar` beside a mark that is a bar chart, and the document never said bar. **This is not `vg-459` again.** That was two *shapes* wearing one glyph, which is cosmetic; this claims a family the document never named, which is the failure the projection's own comment forbids. **Reachability:** `chartMark` reads `object.get("family")` as `unknown` and matches it against `CHART_FAMILIES`, so any persisted document naming a family outside that set — one written by a later build, or hand-edited — reaches it. The collision is asserted rather than hidden at `kind-mark.dom.test.tsx:211-218`, which is the assertion a fix should flip. **Why a row and not a fix:** there is no family-neutral chart mark to fall back to — `KIND_GLYPHS.chart` is *itself* `CHART_BAR_GLYPH` (`icons.ts:231`), so the generic kind mark and the unknown-family mark are one glyph, and the fix is a decision about what an unnamed chart should wear (a neutral chart glyph, or no mark at all) spanning `icons.ts` and `kind-mark.tsx`. **An owner also has the sibling arm to compare against:** `kind-mark.tsx`'s `shapeGlyph` falls back to `KIND_GLYPHS.shape`, which is honest about being unable to name the kind, so the chart arm is the one place the convention is not followed.

title: Three of Phase 13's landed items have no browser case, so a regression living in the stylesheet is invisible to every check
detail: FOUND BY TASK 13.5'S IMPLEMENTER and carried in its commit trailer (`677ff7bf`), 2026-10-15, while writing the two cases the phase owed and checking what the other items already had. **The three:** item 2 (`vg-459`, the layer kind marks and the add pane's tiles) and item 9 (`vg-466`, the inspector header's kind glyph and the rule above its first section) are pinned by jsdom cases alone (`kind-mark.dom.test.tsx`, `icons.test.tsx`, and the inspector's own dom suite); item 6's positive half (`vg-463`, "the inspector leads with the eight") is pinned by a jsdom case of its own (`selection-inspector/index.dom.test.ts:895`, asserting the column's eight `aria-label`s against `uiCopy.arrangeLabels`) and by no browser case either — nor by a capture: `editor.spec.ts:1880` photographs the layer panel, not the lead. **Why jsdom is not the gap being claimed, and the gap is narrower than "untested":** those cases do read a rendered DOM, so the *structure* the fix landed is pinned. What they cannot read is a computed stylesheet cascade or a painted surface — jsdom applies no external CSS — so **a regression that lives in `editor-shell.css` reverts any of the three with every check green.** That is the same shape as `vg-195` and `vg-284` (both archived, both `verified`): a browser surface whose only assertion was the one that could not see the defect. **The order this was found in matters:** the phase's acceptance is rendered evidence, and 13.5's Step 4 pass gives each of the three *one* reading. One reading taken once is not a case that pins them — nothing runs the next time someone edits that stylesheet. **What an owner needs:** one browser case per item, in the spec that already owns its surface — `shell-appearance.spec.ts` for the marks' weight and family, `inspector-sections.spec.ts` or `design-language.spec.ts` for the header. Each is small; none needs new scaffolding. **Scope note, corrected 2026-10-15 after the review of `677ff7bf` falsified two clauses of it.** The trailer says `vg-459` and `vg-466` are "jsdom-only" and that `vg-463`'s half "has a capture at most" — the first clause is right, the second is false, and this row repeated it until the review read `index.dom.test.ts:895`. Earlier wording of this note also said the trailer called all three "jsdom-only", which it does not. **The finding is unchanged and covers all three:** what none of them has is a **browser** case, so a regression living in `editor-shell.css` still reverts any of them with every check green. Filed from that trailer; the implementer's report (`task-13.5-report.md`) carries the per-item version.

title: Item 1's 10px rounded thumb, its track and its hover colour are pinned only as stylesheet text, so the whole `::-webkit-scrollbar*` half can revert with every case green
detail: FOUND BY THE REVIEW of `677ff7bf` (Phase 13.5 Steps 1–3), 2026-10-15, on that task's own new case — so this is a gap in a case landed hours earlier, not a pre-existing one. **What the case reads, and what Chromium paints from.** The case asserts `scrollbar-width` and `scrollbar-color` through the cascade on `.editor-shell-panel` and `.editor-shell-inspector`. The four rules that actually paint the scroller in Chromium are the `::-webkit-scrollbar*` family at `editor-shell.css:1127-1141` — a 10px gutter, the track, the thumb's colour and `--radius-sm`, and a hover colour. `:1120-1123` states the relationship and the statement is correct: Chrome reads the pseudo-element family and ignores the standard pair **the moment one of them matches**. So the case reads the half Chromium does not paint from, and **deleting all four webkit rules leaves it green** while the shell's thumb reverts to the platform's thin one — colour kept by the standard pair, geometry, radius and hover gone. **The one pin that exists is a text read.** `editor-shell.control-rules.test.ts:385-401` reads the stylesheet's own text, which pins the declarations and not their effect. The new case's docstring declares this ceiling honestly (`it proves the scrollers are styled by the tokens, not that a thumb is painted from them`); the review's sharper point is *which* half a reader would take the case to cover. **Why a row rather than a fix in that task.** What would pin it is a rendered read of a painted thumb — geometry, a radius and a hover state — and the repo's standing rule is that screenshots are evidence rather than cross-platform goldens, so a pixel case is not obviously the answer. The alternatives each need a decision before a test edit: accept a pixel read of the scroller's edge; probe `getComputedStyle(el, '::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb')` (**a trap** — Chromium answers with the element's own style, so such a case reads green forever); or rule that the standard pair is the whole styling and delete the webkit family, which trades the 10px rounded hover thumb for the platform's thin one and so is a design change, not a simplification. **What it costs the phase:** 13.5's Step 4 pass takes one rendered reading of item 1 and `vg-458` closes on the consumption the case does prove. What must not be claimed in that close, or in any later summary of item 1, is that the thumb's geometry and hover are pinned by a case. **Near rows:** `vg-458` (item 1 itself), `vg-479` (the trio are `:root` literals that follow no palette), `vg-480` (two portalled scrollers the rule does not reach).

title: The layer row's fourth control arm reserves 126px for a row the product can no longer draw, and two rows state their arithmetic against it
detail: FOUND BY TASK 13.5'S SERIAL BROWSER PASS WHILE FIXING THE FIVE STALE EXPECTATIONS IT FOUND, AND REPORTED IN THAT COMMIT'S `Discovered, not fixed:` TRAILER (`17cefbcb`). NOT BY A FAILING TEST — that is part of the finding: a dead selector changes nothing, so nothing can redden. `editor-shell.css:2339` carries the fourth arm of the attended row's reserve, `.vigilia-layer-row:has(.vigilia-layer-state button:nth-child(4)) { padding-right: 126px }`, and the slot it measures can hold three buttons at most: `RowAffordances` draws a visibility control and, when the row is attended or selected or locked, a lock control (`row-affordances.tsx:62-88`), and `composition-pane.tsx:666` adds at most one enter/leave control beside them. The fourth button was the rename pen, and `vg-462` (item 4) removed it — the caret's job moved onto the row itself, a double-click or F2/Enter, which the pane's own comment states at `composition-pane.tsx:663-665`. So the arm has been unreachable since `e572c302`, and the prose above it (`editor-shell.css:2320`, 'the question for one control on a row that draws four') is stale with it. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the ceiling is two or three is not the same question as whether the arm can match — 126px needs four, three needs 96px, so the arm is dead either way; and nobody has measured whether the three-control arm still leaves the role covered, which is `vg-447`'s half and not this row's. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the deletion is two lines, but `vg-447` (open) and the withdrawn `vg-260` both state their arithmetic against a row drawing all four controls ('126px reserved', `group-time-card` hovered or `group-large` selected), and `vg-447` carries a ruling still owed on which column yields — so the arm, the stale prose and those rows' arithmetic want one ruling rather than a deletion made while passing through. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: reading the arm against the ceiling the product now has, deleting it and the phrase in the comment that names four, and revising `vg-447` and `vg-260`'s four-control figures to say they were measured on a shape the product no longer produces. NEAR ROWS: `vg-447`, `vg-260`, `vg-462`.

title: A palette gradient stop's offset is bounded at 0 and 1 and is typed-only, so one bounded number outside the inspector still has no slider
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 14.1, checking the `NOT COVERED` clause of `vg-469`'s census: that row's sweep covered the selection inspector and the chart manager, and recorded that the artboard, palette, theme and settings-modal panes were never checked for a bounded number in some other control shape. They carry numeric controls through `ControlNumber` rather than through the `control` union the census read, and re-reading them on 2026-10-15 found THREE bounded typed-only controls outside those two surfaces rather than one: the artboard size pair (both halves `min: 1 max: 16384` in `panes/document/artboard-fields.tsx` and `panes/document/new-document-chooser.tsx`), a chart series' `Precision` (`chart-manager/chart-fields.tsx`, inside the chart manager, converted with the rest of that file), and this row's subject. **THE ARTBOARD PAIR STAYS TYPED and this is the reason, recorded here rather than in a report:** 16384 is `MAX_ARTBOARD_DIMENSION` (`renderer-core/src/theme/document.ts`), the largest artboard a package may hold — a *validity ceiling* the document format enforces, not a range anyone drags, and a track with sixteen thousand steps is not a control. That is a different thing from this row's offset, where 0 and 1 are the two ends of the value's own range. **THIS ROW IS THE PALETTE OFFSET ALONE:** `panes/tokens/paint-list.tsx`'s gradient stop row carries `min: 0` and `max: 1` — the stop's position along the gradient, which is a fraction by definition — and renders as a text box with no track. So a bounding range exists and `vg-007`'s rule (a bounded number clamps onto its bound and carries a native slider) is not applied to it. NOT SWEPT WITH THE INSPECTOR because it is not the inspector: this is a theme token's own editor, its commit path is `commit({ ...entry, value: { ...value, stops } })` rather than the column's edit port, and the change is a control swap in a pane Task 14.1's brief did not name. The three panes' remaining numeric controls (`angle`, `size`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) are unbounded — two of them refuse a non-positive value at the commit — so this row is the whole of what the census's unchecked clause leaves open. **KEPT FILED RATHER THAN FIXED** (ruled 2026-10-15): it is a control swap in a pane the task's brief did not name, and the row's own commit path is not the inspector's edit port.

title: A slider whose projected value sits outside its own range draws its thumb at the bound while its well shows the stored value, so the two halves of one control disagree
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 14.1's fix round, in the same state its wheel finding describes, and NOT fixed by that finding's ruling. THE STATE: a panel carrying a border of 100 whose box is then typed down to a drawn edge of 40 has `max` 40 and a value of 100 — `selection-inspector/index.ts` writes `scaleX = dimension / object.width`, so a Size edit moves the bound and leaves the stored value where it was. `vg-478` fixed the radius's own version of this at the write; a border, a shadow blur and the chart's drawn-box measures can still hold a value above the ceiling their control now reads. WHAT THE RULING ALREADY SETTLED: the wheel is a no-op in that state (`control-slider.tsx`'s handler returns before it steps, so a gesture that should raise the value cannot lower it and write a history entry for an edit nobody made). WHAT IS LEFT: Base UI renders the thumb clamped to `max`, while the well — a `ControlNumber` fed the same `shown` value — reads 100. One control, two numbers, and no refusal on either half saying which is real. NEITHER HALF IS OBVIOUSLY RIGHT, which is why this is a row rather than a patch: clamping the projection would silently rewrite the author's stored 100 into 40 in the field's display (the value is out of range because another owner's measure moved, not because the author typed it), and letting the track draw out of range is not something Base UI offers. The candidates are to clamp at the write the way `vg-478` clamps the radius, to show the well's value and mark the track as out of range, or to refuse both halves with a reason until one of the two is chosen. Reachable in principle on the panel border, the shadow blur and every chart setting bounded by `bound: "drawnBox"` / "halfDrawnBox"; not reproduced in a browser by this task.

title: host-bleed's pixel reading paints an empty canvas when the spec runs with its own earlier cases, and passes alone, so a full-run reading cannot say whether the clip is blank
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 14.1's fix round, in the full browser pass its brief requires. MEASURED, three samples on the same tree (`develop` at `c242ad63`, bundle rebuilt with `npm run build` then `npm run build:fixture -w @vigilia/editor`, `--workers=1`): in the whole suite the case is red with `Expected: > 1000, Received: 0` — the host player's `#artboard canvas.lower-canvas` is visible and every pixel of it is transparent; in a three-file run (`shell-appearance`, `host-bleed`, `host-player`) it is red in the same way, at 219ms; run alone (`npx playwright test tests/e2e/host-bleed.spec.ts -g "shows the same clipped quarter"`) it PASSES in 2.2s. The two cases before it in the same file passed in every sample, and they assert the notice's own sentence ("1 of 2 objects past the left edge"), so the scene is loaded and the objects exist — what fails is the pixel read alone. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED, and the two readings differ in the one thing that matters: either the scene renders nothing in some orders, or the pixel read races the first render and the ordering of the file's cases decides which. NOT THIS TASK'S: `packages/player` has no import path into `@vigilia/editor` (its own boundary case, `packages/player/src/boundaries.test.ts`), and Task 14.1's diff touches only the editor's control set, the selection inspector and the chart manager. NOT FIXED because diagnosing it means running the file's cases in different orders, which is not what this round is for. SEVERITY: medium — the case is the only instrument that reads the player's own pixels for a deliberate bleed, so while this is open a blank display cannot be told from a race.

title: Both current control drawings still draw the slider's well at 36px while the product and DESIGN.md §5 say 40, and the drawings README's refresh rule owns the change
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 14.1's fix round R2, from its re-review's F1. THE STATE: `docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html:144` and `docs/design/mockups/current/controls-editorial.html:145` each carry `100` — the slider row's well, drawn at 36. `DESIGN.md` §5's slider row read 36 until this round and reads **40** now (`5f8def05`), because the well carries an editable field since `vg-469`'s item 10: §3's well padding (`--space-6`) and the 1px border leave the field 22px at 36, against §5's own *Keyboard and target size* rule of a 24×24 hit area, and `24 + 2×6 + 2×1 = 38` is the floor. WHY THE DRAWING WAS NEVER WRONG: it draws a readout — a ``, not a `` — so no target rule bound it, and the arithmetic above is exactly what changed. WHAT OWNS THE CHANGE: the drawings are drawn documents whose literals pair with captures, so raising the well to 40 pulls its capture and `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md`'s refresh rule behind it, and that cascade is the drawing owner's rather than a fix round's. The drawing is not stale in any other respect — its padding, border and radius all match §3 and `control-well.tsx`.

title: A chart series with no authored precision reads 0 in its control, so dragging back to the floor writes a whole-number precision the document never had
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 14.1's fix round R2, from its re-review's F3. THE STATE: `chart-manager/chart-fields.tsx` passes `binding.precision ?? PRECISION_FLOOR` to the series' `ControlSlider`, so a binding that carries no `precision` renders `0` on the track and in its well where the `ControlNumber` it replaced showed an empty box. `renderer-core/src/scene/plan.ts:315-327` reads an ABSENT precision as "at most one decimal" and an explicit one as that many digits, clamped 0–6 — so `0` is not the value the renderer draws with. THE SCENARIO: a line series with no authored precision draws `12.3`; the field reads `0`, and nothing in its state says the number is unauthored. An author who drags 0 → 2 → 0 to put it back writes `precision: 0` and silently switches the chart from "at most one decimal" to whole numbers — a document edit nobody meant, with a history entry for it. THE ROUTE THAT EXISTS, and why it is not enough: the well's empty draft commits `onClear` and returns the binding to absent (`control-number.tsx`'s `commit` calls it when the draft is empty and the caller supplies it), but the field then re-reads `0`, so the state the author is in is indistinguishable from the one they left. WHAT A SLIDER IS MISSING, which is why this is a row and not a patch: `ControlSlider`'s `value` is a required number and Base UI clamps it into `[min, max]`, so a track has no unauthored position — expressing one means the track drawing the renderer's fallback while the well reads empty, which is the two-halves-disagree shape `vg-494` already records, or a fourth control state. `chart-manager/panel.ts`'s `settingRows` has the same `?? bound.min` fallback for a descriptor with no family default, which round 0 accepted, so this is consistency rather than a new invention — the row is filed because the fallback has now been inherited silently twice and the hazard is not written where an author meets it.

title: The well has padded 6px horizontally while DESIGN.md §3's table assigns the 4px step to well padding, and no case asserts the well's width so nothing has ever reddened on it
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 14.1's fix round R3, whose review read §5's new paragraph and could not follow its citation. A THREE-WAY SPLIT, all of it pre-existing and none of it this task's making: **the code pads 6** (`components/ui/control-well.tsx`'s `wellClasses` returns `px-[var(--space-6)]`, and `--space-6` is 6px at `editor-shell/editor-shell.css:465`), **both current drawings draw 6** (`docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html:144` and `controls-editorial.html:145`, each `padding:4px 6px`), and **DESIGN.md §3's own table says 4** (`DESIGN.md:182`, `| 4 | Inside a control (well padding, icon button) |`; 6 is assigned to "between the rows of one section"). Code and drawings agree with each other and disagree with the normative table. WHY NOTHING REDDENS: no case asserts the well's width at all — `design-language.spec.ts` reads the well's right edge against the row and passes at either width, and `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` checks which px lengths a surface writes without comparing that list to DESIGN.md, so a padding the table does not sanction is invisible to every instrument here. WHY IT SURFACED: §5's amendment (`5f8def05`) had to cite the padding to justify 40px, and the citation pointed at §3, which fixes 4 — a reader following it computes `well − 10` and cannot reproduce the amendment at all. THE TWO REMEDIES, which are NOT equivalent: **(a) narrow the well's pad to §3's 4px.** At 36px that leaves a 26px field, so §5's 24×24 target was never violated by the 36px well — meaning no §5 amendment and no `vg-496` would have been needed at all, and this task's own outcome would be undone by the fix to its citation. Set against that: `wellClasses` is shared by EVERY well in the shell rather than the slider's alone, and §5's control vocabulary is closed, so padding one control's well to a different step makes the slider's well a different control from every other well — a drawn difference, not a code one. **(b) move §3's table** to say the well's horizontal pad is 6, as both drawings already draw it. HOW THE TRADE RUNS: (a) is the smaller edit and the only one that would erase work; (b) keeps one padding rule for every well and pulls the normative table onto what the code and two drawings already show, which AGENTS.md's "one owner per concept" favours when three sources agree and the fourth is a table cell. **THE DECISION IS OWED AND IS NOT TAKEN HERE** — it moves a §3 step's meaning for every well, which is the design-language owner's call rather than a fix round's. Read with `vg-496` (the two drawings still draw a 36px well, and the same table cell governs whether they should) and `vg-469` (item 10 is what made the well's width matter: a readout had no target rule, an input does). **Remedy (a) is not a CSS revert either**: `control-slider.tsx`'s `wellClassName` is the only writer of 40 in the scanned tree — every other 40px hit is inside a comment, and the checker strips those — and `unconsumedPx` reds an allowlist entry no file writes, so (a) is two edits (the width, and the `40` in `designLanguagePx`) while (b) is one.

title: Item 17 removed the inspector's only route to the type-preset panel, and nothing else offers one
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 while doing Task 14.2 (the user's items 13 and 17), and it is a consequence of item 17 rather than of item 13. The read-only section that went was also the only place the inspector rendered data-vigilia-reveal-type-presets — an “Edit type presets” button whose click called onRevealPane(“tokens”, presetRevealTarget(selectionPresetId)) and opened the Tokens pane scrolled to the preset the selection is set in.
