All of it is gone with the button, because none of it has a second caller. NOT A MECHANICAL REMOVAL, which is why this is a row and not a fix inside the task: the missing capability is “from a selected object, reach the type preset it is set in”, and where it belongs — a row in the Content section, the type-preset panel's own search, or nowhere because the Tokens pane is one click away — is a design decision. editor-shell.css's two appearance rules for the button went with it. vg-474 owns the removal of the sections and does not decide this.

title: Two verified rows ride on a surface item 17 removed, so vg-160's and vg-102's checks can no longer run
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 while doing Task 14.2, by running the checks its own rows name rather than trusting them. vg-160 (verified, archived) checks that “the Document pane's References sub-panel names itself data-vigilia-panel='references', not 'style'”, read off panes/document/references.tsx and pinned by the editor.spec.ts case “lists the document's references, and the selection's own in its Spends column”. Both are gone: the file with item 17 and the case with item 17 and vg-160's own close (R4 — the case had no surviving half). What vg-160 asked for is moot, because there is no panel left to rename. vg-102 (verified, archived) checks that a rebuilt editor shows “ZERO raw references” with “the resolution lines read Type preset: Card title and Paint: Text”. Those lines were resolutionField in selection-inspector/appearance.ts, deleted with the read-only section; nothing renders a label/value resolution row now (measured 2026-10-15: resolutionField, resolutionValue and data-vigilia-resolution have no producer or reader anywhere in src/web outside the removal note in index.dom.test.ts). vg-102's subject is therefore gone with its surface. THE REMEDY IS ONE DECISION FOR BOTH — withdraw each as no-longer-reachable, or re-point each at the surface that carries its subject now — and it is not taken here because a verified row's close is a register ruling, not a task. vg-232 (verified) was the third row in this shape and it survives: its check was re-pointed in the same commit at the run editor's preset label, so it still has a witness.

title: The register has no state for a finding whose subject a later change deleted, so three verified and open rows hold states that no longer describe them
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 closing Task 14.2, by running the checks its own rows name rather than trusting them (`vg-500` is the row that noticed the first two). **Task 14.2 deleted the two read-only surfaces the user's item 17 named, and three rows were riding on them:** `vg-160` and `vg-102` are archived `verified` with checks that read files and cases the removal deleted, and `vg-423` is `open` about `panes/document/references.tsx:47`'s `id="style"` — a marker on a section that no longer exists. Their provenance is appended to each row's `detail`; their state is untouched. **WITH DRAWING THEM IS NOT TAKEN HERE, AND NOT BECAUSE IT IS DIFFICULT:** AGENTS.md reserves `withdrawn` for a finding we decided *not to fix*, reasoned with the user and recorded in `detail`, and an agent's hand writes it only after that. A subject that a later change removed is neither fixed nor declined, so none of the register's states fits — `verified` claims a fix that no longer has anything to verify, and `open` claims work that has no subject. **UNTIL THE VOCABULARY HAS A STATE FOR IT, THE HONEST POSITION IS THAT ALL THREE ARE MIS-STATED**, which is why this row exists rather than three silent edits. **The options, with what each costs:** (a) add a `moot` state and close all three with the removing commit named — cheapest and truest, but it grows the register's schema, which `scripts/backlog-check.mjs` validates and which `backlog-archive.jsonl` splits on; (b) close them `withdrawn` with the removal as the reason — no schema change, but it records a decision nobody made; (c) leave them as they are with the provenance in `detail` — no false claim about *this* change, but the archived pair still greps as `verified` for a reader who does not read to the end. **THE TRIGGER IS `vg-474`'s own close**: item 17's register row, once it goes to the archive, is the natural place to rule this, because the three rows' subjects and that row's fix are the same deletion.

RULED 2026-10-15: **CLOSE THE THREE AS `withdrawn`, and add no `moot` state.** The register's vocabulary stays two-valued on the closed side, and the reason travels on each row instead — which is what keeps the close readable, since `withdrawn` on its own would read as a decision not to do work that was never done. The three are `vg-160` and `vg-102` (both archived `verified`, whose subject Task 14.2 deleted) and `vg-423` (open). Where a row was `verified`, its `check` and `artefacts` are left standing: the work did land, and it is the subject that is gone.

title: backlog-check validates every row and never the set, so a register row that vanished passes the gate that owns it
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 while closing Task 14.2, by breaking it: an append script of the controller's own used `lastIndexOf` to find the final line's start and cut the register's last row (`vg-500`) instead of appending after it. **`node scripts/backlog-check.mjs` reported `500 items across both registers, all valid` BEFORE the edit and `500 items across both registers, all valid` AFTER it** — the deletion and the addition cancelled in the only number the gate prints, and every remaining row still parsed, so the run was green with a filed finding gone. The same blindness is total for a plain deletion: removing `vg-500` alone reports `499 items ... all valid` and exits 0. **THE GATE CHECKS MEMBERSHIP, NOT CONTINUITY** — it validates each row's shape, its `§` escapes, its state and (for `verified`) its `check` and `artefacts`, and it has no notion of the set as it was. **NOT FIXED HERE, because the fix needs a decision rather than a patch:** an id-gap rule is the obvious candidate and would NOT have caught this one (the deleted id was replaced by the next id, so the sequence stayed unbroken), which leaves comparing against a previous revision — reading the register out of `git`, so the gate depends on history — or recording a count and a high-water mark inside the file itself, which makes the register carry state about itself. **A reader who trusts the gate's one number should know what it does not say.** Related: `vg-455` is the plan's named unowned gate hole, and this is a second one in the same script.

title: The empty-canvas click helpers probe at fractional coordinates while the browser rounds the click, so a mis-hit can satisfy a position assertion against the wrong menu
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 14.3's review (its finding 4, filed at the controller's ruling), while checking the one helper that task had to change. **The object-menu helper was hardened for this exact hazard and the empty-canvas pair was not:** `editor-context-menu.spec.ts:62-70` (`emptyCanvasPoint`) and `:143-152` (`emptyCanvasPointHigh`) both probe with `rect.left + rect.width * fx` over a 0.02 step and return that point unchanged, while `editorCanvas.findTarget` takes the pointer coordinates as integers — a browser rounds `clientX` to a `long` — so the point they *test* with and the point the click *lands* on differ by up to half a pixel. **WHY IT IS NOT MERELY UNTIDY: the object menu fails loudly on a mis-hit and the creation menu does not.** A click that rounds onto an object opens the object menu instead, and a case asserting `toContain("Copy")` reds; but the empty-canvas case that reads the *popup's position* ("the menu lands where the pointer was") asserts geometry rather than contents, and the object menu opens at the same place — so the wrong menu satisfies it and the case passes having tested nothing. **NOT FIXED HERE, and it is not this task's:** the two helpers predate Task 14.3, which touched neither of them, and the fix is a decision about the helper (return a rounded point and re-probe at that integer, or assert contents as well as position) rather than a mechanical change. **The reviewer's own re-reading is the reason it was found rather than assumed** — the task's report claimed the pair was "not exposed to this", which is a mitigation and not a proof.

title: The shell drawing's footer and all three of its captures read Fabric editor ready, which the product's footer no longer says
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 14.4's fix round R1, at the controller's ruling, after the task corrected the drawing and the review refused it. WHAT DISAGREES: docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html draws the footer as Fabric editor ready at line 372, and the three captures beside it -- shell-capture-add.png, shell-capture-graphite.png and shell-capture-glyphs.png -- each read the same old string, while the product's own footer has read Editor ready since Task 14.4 (item 16, the user's ruling on vg-473). So the drawing and its own evidence agree with each other and both disagree with the product, with no marker saying which half is current. WHY THE DRAWING EDIT WAS REFUSED RATHER THAN KEPT: a mockup's literals are paired with the captures taken from it, so a change to one pulls the other's refresh behind it, and that cascade belongs to the drawing's owner rather than to a copy task. Task 14.1's ruling met this identical shape in the same phase and refused the same edit in the same words, which is what makes this a ruling rather than a preference. THE REFRESH OBLIGATION IS THE DRAWING OWNER'S: the drawing line and all three captures move together or none of them moves, and the captures must not be refreshed by anyone who does not own the drawing. Task 14.4's fix round reverted its own one-line edit to shell.html:372 rather than leave the pair split.

title: A parity licence's date attaches to a quotation's first line, so a wrapped rule reworded by the citing commit escapes the same-commit refusal
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 10.1's scoped re-review (Scope A, finding A1), while confirming that the rejection's second ruled item had landed. `ruleCommit` (`src/web/tests/e2e/mockup-values.test.ts:892`) locates the quotation in the file the licence names — wrap-aware, through `rawOffsetOf` — and then blames **only the one line the quotation starts on**, so a quotation the source wraps across several lines is dated by its first line alone. **MEASURED IN A SCRATCH REPOSITORY rather than reasoned:** commit A writes a three-line sentence and commit B rewrites only its third line; `git blame --porcelain -L 2,2` answers A (`004d885a…`) while `-L 3,3` answers B (`dd6e5040…`). The consequence is narrow and real: a licence citing a rule the citing commit rewords *below its first line* is not refused as "written in the same commit", which is exactly the shape the ruled item was fixed for at the single-line level. **NOT A REGRESSION** — the marker arm it replaced carried the same class of blind spot one level up, which the reviewer states. **NOT FIXED HERE, and it needs a decision rather than a patch:** dating a multi-line quotation means choosing what its date *is* — the newest of its lines, all of them compared, or a range test against `licensedAt` — and each choice changes which licences are refused. What makes it worth fixing rather than documenting is the module's own claim at `mockup-values.ts:766-768`, that a rule reworded in the citing commit is caught: true of §5's single-line row, not true of a wrapped one.

title: The labelled button's fill and radius are owned twice and disagree, so section 5's new entry describes a shape one of its two owners does not render
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 10.2's implementer while landing `vg-316`'s ruling, and filed as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailers in `dedf2d77`. `vg-441` and `vg-316` were closed by naming the labelled button in `DESIGN.md` section 5, and naming it is what exposed the disagreement: the control has two owners and they do not render the same shape. MEASURED, resting fill: `ACTION_BUTTON` renders `bg-panel-2` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/new-document-chooser.tsx:43` and `src/web/packages/editor/src/persistence-manager/replace-document-prompt.tsx:15`) where `.editor-shell-dialog > button` renders `var(--vigilia-control-bg)` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1666`) — and section 4 now names the latter as the control fill, so the two owners disagree about which role the button's surface is. MEASURED, radius: the dialog rule renders `border-radius: 6px` (section 3's `--radius-md`, "Controls, menu rows, small tiles") where `ACTION_BUTTON` renders `rounded-sm`, which is `--radius-sm` 4px, section 3's "Swatches, inline chips, the slider thumb's container". Two properties, one cause: `ACTION_BUTTON` hand-copies the dialog button's shape rather than taking it from one owner, so the two drift independently. NOT FIXED HERE because it needs a decision rather than a patch — which of the two is the labelled button's shape — and because the ruling that named the control was explicit that the product does not change. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: one owner for the labelled button's resting shape, and a parity or DOM case pinning the fill and the radius at the value section 3 and section 4 give them.

title: The labelled button's hover raises its edge to the accent in both owners where section 5 rule 6 requires the muted role, and two owners agreeing is what makes it a rule question
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 10.2's implementer while landing `vg-316`'s ruling, and filed as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `dedf2d77`. MEASURED: `.editor-shell-dialog > button:hover` raises both `border-color` and `color` to `var(--shell-accent)` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1678`) and `ACTION_BUTTON`'s `hover:border-accent hover:text-accent` does the same (`src/web/packages/editor/src/new-document-chooser.tsx:43`). `DESIGN.md` section 5 rule 6 states the opposite for a control with a resting edge: "Hover raises `--edge` to `--muted`. On a control that carries a resting `--edge` — the well, the toggle — the border brightens." A labelled button carries a resting `--edge`. **This is a different question from the fill-and-radius row beside it**, and it is why the two are filed separately: there the two owners disagree with each other and the fix is to pick one, while here the two owners agree with each other and disagree with the rule, so either the rule is wrong or two deliberate implementations are. Section 4's rationing is the stake — the accent is "at most one accent-filled element in a region at a time" — and a hovered button is a second accent in a region that already has one. NOT FIXED HERE because which side yields is a design decision, and because the ruling that named the control was explicit that the product does not change. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a ruling on whether a labelled button's hover is the accent or the muted role, and the losing side changed with it.

title: The Appearance pane's region label is drawn 12px sentence case where section 2 reserves the eyebrow shape for a region label
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 10.2's independent task review, as the residue of that task's first part, and filed as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `8c4c79b9`. MEASURED: `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html:42` draws the pane's heading as `font:600 12px/1 system-ui;margin-bottom:10px` — sentence case, no letter-spacing, 12px — while `docs/design/mockups/current/settings-keyboard.html:54` draws the other tabs' group headings as `font:600 10px/1.2 system-ui;letter-spacing:.11em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--muted)`. Both are the same element in the product: `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/settings.tsx:154` renders `<h3 id={PALETTE_GROUP_ID}>`, which `.editor-shell-dialog h3` styles once, so the two drawings disagree about one rule. Section 2 decides which side is stale: "Uppercase is reserved for section eyebrows … An eyebrow is `--text-2xs`, `600`, `letter-spacing: .11em`, muted, and it always labels a region, never a control. Nothing else is uppercase." "Shell palette" labels a region, and 12px is `--text-sm` ("Control text, menu items, list rows"), which is not a heading role either. **NOT A PRODUCT DEFECT** — the product takes the eyebrow shape and the drawings' own README states the precedence: "Where the current set and DESIGN.md disagree, DESIGN.md wins and the file is stale." So this is a drawing correction, which is the drawing owner's act rather than a product task's. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: `settings.html:42` redrawn at the eyebrow shape, or a ruling that a pane's own heading is a role section 2 does not name — in which case section 2 is what changes.

title: The repaint loop and publishing both stop on pagehide and nothing restarts them, so an editor returned from the back/forward cache keeps neither
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.2b's implementer while fixing `vg-040`'s F1 — the draft's timer stopped on `pagehide` and was never re-armed after a back/forward cache round trip — and filed as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `87d5b30d`. Two owners, one shape, verified at both sites. MEASURED, the repaint loop: `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-main.ts:426-428` registers `window.addEventListener("pagehide", () => chartRefresh.dispose(), { once: true })`, and `startChartRefresh` (`src/web/packages/scene-fabric/src/chart-refresh.ts:56-64`) returns only `setRate` and `dispose` — `dispose` sets `disposed = true` and cancels the pending frame, `tick` returns early on it (`:33`), and there is no re-arm, so the loop cannot start again. The `{ once: true }` makes the second firing moot: after one round trip the listener is gone and the loop is dead. MEASURED, publishing: `editor-main.ts:432-434` stops the publisher on `pagehide` and nothing restarts it on `pageshow`. What the author sees: charts, bound text and the clock stop updating while the page is plainly still open, and the host keeps showing whatever the phone was last sent. `vg-040`'s F1 was the same shape and was fixed by binding both events in `draft-store.ts:169-180` (`bindDraftAutosave`), which is the mechanism these two need — but neither is reachable by the draft's fix, because each owns its own resource. NOT FIXED HERE because both owners sit outside `vg-040` and that row's ruling was scoped to the draft. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: one page-lifetime binding that both stops and re-arms, `startChartRefresh` gaining the re-arm it lacks, and a case proving each resumes after a `pagehide`/`pageshow` pair.

title: A refused draft restore is announced and then immediately overwritten, so the author is never told why their work did not come back
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.2b's implementer while fixing `vg-040`'s R2, and filed as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `87d5b30d`. MEASURED: the catch at `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-main.ts:465-470` sets `status.textContent = "Could not restore the draft: …"` and then falls through to `bootTheme` at `:476`, whose opened branch mounts and overwrites the same element with `openedStatusText(...)` at `:488-489` — the implementer's own Chromium reading shows `status: "Editor ready"` after a refused Restore. So the author answers Restore, their draft does not come back, and the editor says nothing about it. The work itself is safe — that is what `87d5b30d` fixed, the draft surviving the fallback — so this is a reporting defect and not a data-loss one. NOT FIXED HERE because where the refusal should be said is a decision nothing has made yet: the boot branch owns the status line and the refusal has to survive it, which is an ordering question in `editor-main.ts`'s boot flow rather than a missing line. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a ruling on where a refused restore reports, and the refusal surviving the boot that follows it.

title: The draft slot holds one document, so a refused restore's draft survives only until the author edits the document that replaced it
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by the scoped re-review of Task 12.2b's R2, and carried as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in R3. MEASURED by reading the two branches: after a refused restore, `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-main.ts:465` catches, `bootTheme` at `:476` mounts a clean fallback document B, and the unrenderable draft D is still in the single slot with the autosave's `dirty` false — so R2's transition rule leaves D alone. But the **write** branch, `draft-store.ts:146`, is not gated on the transition: the author's first edit of B takes the next tick and overwrites D, and an edit followed by an undo before that tick clears it at `:147`. Either way D is gone within 30 s of the author touching B, with no save and no discard. The behaviour is deliberate and is not itself the defect — one slot is `vg-040`'s own decision 1, and the alternative, leaving D in place, would leave the document the author is actually editing undrafted, which is strictly worse. What was wrong was the claim: `editor-main.ts:466-468` says "the draft stays where a build that can read it will find it" and R2's docblock at `draft-store.ts:126-131` says clearing "would delete the only copy of the author's work", and both hold only until that first edit. R3 corrects the two comments; the ceiling is filed here rather than left in a comment, because a comment that overstates is how the next reader is misled. NOT FIXED because changing it is a decision nothing has made: a second slot, a pinned draft, or refusing to draft the fallback document until the author saves it are each a different product. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a ruling on what the single slot owes a draft the build cannot render, and the store changed to match it.

title: The tooltip's delay case asserts its label through an always-true ternary, so the expression reads as a condition that is not one
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.3a's independent task review, as a context line in that task's diff, so it predates the change. MEASURED: `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/controls/tooltip.dom.test.ts:78-80` reads `expect(open()?.textContent).toBe("A control".length > 0 ? "Glass blur" : "")`. The condition `"A control".length > 0` is a property of a string literal, so it is true on every run and the expression always evaluates to `"Glass blur"` — the ternary cannot select the empty string, and the literal `"A control"` it tests has nothing to do with the assertion beside it. The case asserts the right thing by accident of the branch that always wins. NOT FIXED HERE because it is cosmetic and predates the task: the assertion's outcome is correct either way, and it is filed rather than folded into `vg-450` because a test's readability is not that row's subject. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the ternary replaced by the literal it always evaluates to, or by the variable the case actually means to read.

title: An open register row can carry a check, and the checker validates checks only on verified rows, so a stale check survives invisibly
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by the controller while preparing Task 12.3b's close, as a near-miss: `vg-037` was `open` and already carried a `check` — the 2026-10-14 characterisation's ("Measured across every shape in the running editor … A fresh Circle and a fresh Rectangle both take blurRadius 16 on the same click") — which checks a capability NEARBY the row's claim and says nothing about a Circle's frost reading stronger than a Rect's. The close script's guard `if (/"check"\s*:/.test(line)) throw` would have rejected the close as written. MEASURED, not inferred: of 199 live rows, all `open`, 2 carry a `check` (`vg-037`, `vg-348`) and 0 carry `artefacts`; of 299 archived `verified` rows, 0 fail the word-overlap test. BOTH live instances PASS that test comfortably — `vg-037` shares 5 words with its own title (line, glass, control, circle, rect) and `vg-348` shares 8 — so the mechanical test cannot tell a stale check from a current one. THE CAUSE IS NAMED: `scripts/backlog-check.mjs:121` gates the `check` and `artefacts` rules on `item.state === "verified"`, so a check on an open row is unvalidated by construction; nothing rejects it and nothing checks it. NOT FIXED HERE because the correct behaviour is NOT already specified — the contract says what a `verified` row must carry and is silent on whether an `open` row may carry a check — so this needs a design decision: reject a check on an open row and strip it on reopen, or tolerate it as inert and make every close REPLACE the value rather than append it. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: one of those two behaviours chosen, the checker enforcing it, and a case proving an open row with a check is rejected (or that a reopen clears it). The consequence if left: a reopened row closed again without its check replaced records a nearby capability as its evidence, which is the failure AGENTS.md records as having already cost two false 'landed' reports.

title: The glass blur radius follows scaleX and ignores scaleY, so a panel stretched horizontally blurs more than one stretched vertically at the same authored value
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.3b's implementer, carried as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `cc1ea2d0`, and its cause verified by the controller against the source before it was allowed to become a row. MEASURED: `src/web/packages/scene-fabric/src/glass.ts:376` reads `const blurRadius = treatment.blurRadius * Math.hypot(own[0], own[1]);`, where `own = deviceMatrix(object, canvas)` and `deviceMatrix` (`:543`) returns Fabric's `[a, b, c, d, e, f]`. So `own[0]`/`own[1]` are the matrix's `a` and `b`, and at angle 0 `a = scaleX * viewportScale * retina` while `b = 0` — `hypot` therefore yields `|scaleX * viewportScale * retina|`, which is rotation-independent and in which `scaleY` does not appear at all. The inspector's own Size fields are what write `scaleX`/`scaleY` (`index.ts`'s `width`/`height` arms scale a shape rather than resizing it), so the asymmetry is reachable from the product's UI. NOT FIXED HERE because whether a non-uniformly scaled panel SHOULD blur isotropically is a design decision, not a defect with a specified correct behaviour: a single scalar radius must be chosen for a non-uniform scale, and `hypot(a, b)` (the transformed unit-x length) is one convention among several. A COMMIT BODY CANNOT BE AMENDED, so the pointer is corrected here: the trailer and the report both said bare "`glass.ts`" while THREE tracked files bear that name (`editor/src/selection-inspector/glass.ts`, `renderer-core/src/theme/glass.ts`, `scene-fabric/src/glass.ts`), and this row's subject is the last of the three. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the intended behaviour for a non-uniform scale chosen and either the radius made isotropic (a `hypot` over both axes' transformed lengths) or the current convention stated as deliberate in a comment and a test.

title: The frost-extent instrument is method-dependent at the box rim, so two harnesses read the same frost 3.6 percent apart
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.3b's implementer during fix round R2's re-take, and it is a defect in the evidence instrument rather than in the product. MEASURED: the same frosted Rectangle in the same side-by-side scene reads 13,228 px under the whole-scene cross-page pair (one capture with the rect frosted and the circle bare, against one with the circle frosted and the rect bare) and 12,766 px under the per-shape pair (each shape differenced against an untreated capture of itself) — a 3.6 percent difference in a quantity both harnesses agree on in the interior, so the committed ratio for that scene is 1.3831 under one method and 1.4332 under the other. The circle reads 18,296 px under both. WHERE THEY DIFFER, located rather than described: exactly the rect box's outer rim, 462 px, at rows 236-239 and 319-320 (about 31 px per row) and columns 52-54 and 201-203 (about 30 px per column), with onlyCrossPage 462 and onlyPerShapePair 0. WHAT WAS RULED OUT: a between-page shift of the scene, because the far baseline over the photograph at (215,300)-(305,380) reads 0 under both pairs and all four corners of the rect box read 0 under both. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED, in those words, on the row and in the committed probe — the two methods differ only in which untreated capture is the baseline, so the leading hypothesis is a difference in the threshold's noise floor at a soft rim, and it has not been tested. NOT FIXED HERE because the cause is not established and establishing it is an investigation rather than an edit. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the 462 rim pixels explained (a threshold effect, a baseline-capture difference, or something else), the instrument made method-independent or the method named as part of the reading, and the probe carrying one number per scene rather than two. The consequence if left: a future task measuring a frost extent by a different method will read a few percent away and chase a phantom regression.

title: load-failure.ts's showLoadFailure comment cites main.ts line numbers that have moved and still calls a late failure's status an open question the ruling settled

title: No keyboard gesture makes a multi-selection, so a keyboard author cannot reach the arrange action
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.4a’s implementer while landing `vg-056`, carried as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `26b9be94` and left unfiled for the controller. THE GAP: `vg-056` made the composition pane’s layer list reach `canArrange`’s multi-selection gate by pointer — shift extends a range, ctrl toggles one — but nothing in the shell produces a multi-selection from the keyboard, so arrange stays unreachable for a keyboard-only author. MEASURED, not inferred: `moveFocus` in `panes/composition/composition-pane.tsx` handles ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End by calling `focus(index)` and returning, and selects nothing, so the tree’s arrow keys move focus only. The row’s second half as the implementer stated it — that Fabric’s multi-selection is “pointer-only” — is NOT supportable as written and is recorded here in the narrower form that is: Fabric’s built-in *interaction* for multi-selection is pointer-driven, while an `ActiveSelection` is constructible programmatically, which is exactly what `vg-056`’s `selectLayers` does. The 2026-10-15 Space ruling does not close this: Space is a plain select, so it moves the anchor and still cannot *make* a multi-selection. WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN TASK: a keyboard route in the list alone would be a new product decision about the canvas’s own parity — whether the canvas must also offer a keyboard multi-select, and with which gesture — rather than the application of `vg-056`’s ruling. THE FIX NEEDS A DESIGN DECISION, which is why it is a row and not a task: no gesture is specified, and picking one (shift+arrow extending from the anchor? space to toggle?) settles behaviour for the canvas as well as the list.

title: Two editor.spec.ts cases fail consistently at a second navigation, blocked by the unsaved-draft prompt rather than by a missing canvas
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.4a's independent task reviewer, as an extra check the implementer never ran: it ran `editor.spec.ts` because a plain layer-row click is the path `vg-056` touched. It did not file a row and flagged it for the controller instead, which is the right division — it was reviewing, not fixing. THE MEASUREMENT: `editor.spec.ts` under `desktop-chromium` reads **6 failed / 61 passed**. Four of the six were load flakes and passed on re-run; **two fail consistently**, at the second `page.goto(EDITOR)` inside their own case, and what blocks them is the unsaved-draft dialog (`packages/editor/src/draft-recovery-prompt.tsx`, whose copy is `uiCopy.draftRecovery`) rather than a canvas that did not mount. The spec navigates 69 times, so a case that dirties the document and then navigates again is the shape to look for. THE CONTROL, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS FILED AS PRE-EXISTING RATHER THAN AS 12.4a's: the reviewer reverted `editor-shell/bridge.ts` and `panes/composition/composition-pane.tsx` to the parent commit `7728dfbd`, rebuilt, and re-ran — **the same two failed identically**. It then restored both, with `cmp` exit 0 on each, and left the tree byte-identical to HEAD. So the pair is not caused by the multi-selection work and predates it. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED BEYOND THAT: the reviewer named the prompt as what blocks the navigation, which the control supports, but it did not establish whether the correct reading is that those two cases should dismiss the prompt, that the prompt should not appear on a fresh navigation, or that the cases dirty the document in a way they should not. That third reading would make this a product defect rather than a test defect, and telling them apart needs the cases read against `draft-store.ts`'s commit rules. WHY A ROW AND NOT A FIX: the cause is not established to `file:line` for the correct-behaviour half, more than one owner could fix it (the spec's own navigation helper, the prompt's trigger condition, or the draft store), and which of the three readings holds is a decision rather than a correction. TWO NEAR ROWS, NEITHER OF WHICH IS THIS ONE: `vg-511` and `vg-512` are both open and both about the draft-restore path's own behaviour — a refused restore being announced and then overwritten, and the draft slot holding one document — so they touch the same component and are not duplicates of a pair of failing cases. NOT VERIFIED BY THE CONTROLLER: the failing line numbers and the re-run split are the reviewer's, taken from its own run and its own control; the controller confirmed only that `draft-recovery-prompt.tsx` exists at that path, that `uiCopy.draftRecovery` supplies its copy, and that `editor.spec.ts` navigates 69 times.

HALF OF THIS PAIR IS NOW FIXED, 2026-10-15, BY TASK 12.4D'S FIX ROUND R1 (commit `7d3b3afa`), AND THE FIX TOOK ONE OF THE THREE READINGS THIS ROW SAID NEEDED A DECISION. Repairing the no-snap aim in `editor.spec.ts`'s "snaps a resized object to a neighbour and shows a guide" made that case reach its second `page.goto(EDITOR)` for the first time, and it then failed exactly as this row describes: the canvas assertion timed out and the page snapshot showed the unsaved-draft dialog. **The reading taken is the first of the three** — those cases should dismiss the prompt — implemented as `answerDialogIfShown(page, "Discard")` after that navigation, which is the same answer `composition-panel.spec.ts`, `rebuild-driver.ts` and `editor-display.spec.ts` already give at their own reloads. The round's own justification for taking it rather than asking: the answer is already specified elsewhere in the suite, so it is not a new decision, and without it the fix it was dispatched for could not be shown green at all. **WHAT THAT LEAVES OPEN, WHICH IS WHY THIS ROW IS NOT CLOSED:** (1) the other case of the two was not named and not touched — the round fixed the one case the finding led it to and said so; (2) whether reading one is the right answer **everywhere** is still the sweep the row describes, and it now has a precedent to follow rather than a question about which of three readings to take; (3) the round could not date the breakage, and neither could this row, because the pre-widening tree aborts before the reload is ever reached — so "pre-existing" still rests on the earlier reviewer's `7728dfbd` control rather than on anything measured since. **NOT VERIFIED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT MEASURED HERE:** how many of the pair still fail. `editor.spec.ts` as a whole has not been re-run since `7d3b3afa` — Task 12.4f holds the browser and the shared `dist`, so the controller did not run it — and the round's own runs were of the single repaired case and of `snapping.spec.ts`. Whoever takes this row should run `editor.spec.ts` under `desktop-chromium` first and start from what it reads now.

title: The local gate omits three CI steps, so a task can close green on `npm run gate` while CI is red
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by the controller while closing Task 12.4b (`vg-230`), from that task's own review: the review returned spec compliance FAIL on two red checks the implementer never ran, and **one of them is a CI step the local gate does not execute**. MEASURED, not inferred. `src/web/package.json`'s `gate` script is `biome check .. && npm run gates:self-test && npm run design:check && npm run test`. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs, in order, `npm run gate` (`:68`), `npm run status:check` (`:71`), `npm run hooks:check` (`:77`) and `npm run typecheck` (`:86`). **So three CI steps are outside the gate: `typecheck`, `status:check` and `hooks:check`.** Reproduced at `51ae5fec`: `npm run typecheck` exits **1** with `Found 5 errors in 2 files` — a required `EditorShellSnapshot.objectCount` missing from five stub literals — while `npm run gate` at the same commit exits **0**. THE GATE'S OWN COMMENT ESTABLISHES THE PRINCIPLE AND THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF IT: it records that the unit suite joined the chain because 'a task closed with `vitest run` red (`vg-323`)', and that `design:check` joined 'for that same reason: it ran only as its own CI step, so a local `npm run gate` read green over a red live-tree verdict (`vg-435`)'. Both were fixed by adding the missing step to the chain. **`typecheck` is the same shape, unfixed, and it has now cost a fix round.** WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE COMMIT: the drain's own close rule is that every phase close names its gate command and that command's exit code, on the ground that 'gates run' is not checkable. That rule is only sound if the gate is the thing CI runs, and it is not — so every close in this plan cites a number that a red CI would not agree with. THE FIX IS ONE LINE IF THE DECISION IS TO INCLUDE IT (`npm run typecheck` in the chain), AND THE DECISION IS THE COST RATHER THAN THE CORRECTNESS: `typecheck` runs `--workspaces` and is the slowest of the three, while the gate's comment says the chain is ordered 'fastest first, so the 1.5s design check fails before the unit suite starts'. `status:check` and `hooks:check` are cheap and `hooks:check` overlaps `gates:self-test`'s `sdd-checkpoint.mjs --self-check`, so they may be deliberate omissions where `typecheck` is not — **the gate comment explains why test and design:check were added and says nothing about typecheck, which is what makes it look like an omission rather than a decision.** WHY A ROW AND NOT AN ON-THE-FLY FIX: the fix is trivial but the *contract* is not — it changes what 'the gate' means for every task in the plan, and whether a slow type-check belongs in a chain ordered for fast failure is a judgement the gate's owner should make deliberately rather than one a controller makes while closing someone else's task. NEAR ROWS: none found — `vg-323` and `vg-435` are both archived `verified` and are the two precedents this row is the third of, not duplicates of it.

title: The shell drawing's status row and `.editor-shell-status` are swapped on their gap and padding
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by the scoped re-review of Task 12.4b (`vg-230`)'s fix round R1, and re-measured by the controller before filing rather than taken on report. MEASURED at `1317e07f`: `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html` draws the status row as `gap:14px; padding:0 12px`, while the product's `.editor-shell-status` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css` states `padding: 0 var(--space-14)` and `gap: var(--space-12)` — and `--space-12` is 12px and `--space-14` is 14px (the tokens' own declarations). **So the two surfaces disagree about which of the two values is the gap and which is the padding: the drawing says 14 then 12, the product says 12 then 14.** WHY NO INSTRUMENT CATCHES IT: both values are §3 steps and both are declared as the right tokens, so the text scan, the ratchet and the browser's on-scale assertion are all satisfied — the disagreement is about which property owns which value, which no check reads. WHY IT ARRIVED HERE: it came with `51ae5fec`, the commit that corrected this same row's drawing for §7.6's counts, so the correction and the defect are in one commit and the defect is in the half that was not being looked at. WHY A ROW AND NOT AN ON-THE-FLY FIX: the on-the-fly test fails on its second clause rather than its first — the cause is named at `file:line` and the fix is small, but **which side is right is not already specified**. `docs/design/mockups/README.md` says the current set is the target and "when the product differs, the product is the defect", which points at the stylesheet; but it also says a difference is disposed of by being fixed or "licensed by a rule that predates it", and the parity capture that would have to dispose of this one has not run. Reading the drawing's own 26px row as the authority would put `gap` at 14 and `padding` at 12, inverting two declarations in a file whose other rows Task 12.4e owns outright. **So the fix belongs to whoever owns that parity capture, or to 12.4e's pass over the stylesheet, and not to a controller closing someone else's task.** NEAR ROWS: none found in the live register — `vg-325` is this row's neighbour on the status strip's appearance but is about ink and elevation rather than these two declarations, and no `PARITY` row matches the row's selector.

title: The exclusion of the reserved `none` from a palette token list is spelled six times, and `palette-tokens.ts` already owns the list
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 while recovering Task 12.4c (`vg-269`), which added a sixth reader of the rule and a fifth spelling of it. THE OBSERVATION: the membership rule "a palette's tokens, minus the reserved `none`" is written out at five sites, each with its own predicate. (1) `paletteTokenIds` in the new `src/web/packages/editor/src/palette-manager/token-list.ts`, added by this task, which is `Object.keys(palette).filter((id) => id !== "none")`. (2) `paletteRoleMatch` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/card-token-mapping.ts`, `Object.keys(globals?.palette ?? {}).filter((id) => id !== "none")`. (3) `surfacePalette` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/new-object-defaults.ts`, `Object.entries(...).filter(([id]) => id !== "none")`. (4) `firstPalette`, the same file, the same filter again. (5) the `keep` predicate at `src/web/packages/editor/src/selection-inspector/runs.tsx`, which passes `(id) => id !== "none"` into the shared helper, and (6) `paintOptions` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/selection-inspector/panel.ts`, which passes `(id, entry) => id !== "none" && …` into the same `paletteTokenOptions` — **this site was missed by the row as first filed and the count corrected from five to six by Task 12.4c's independent review**, which found it by grepping the predicate rather than the helper. THE EXISTING OWNER THE NEW MODULE DID NOT REACH: `paletteTokenOptions` in `src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/theme/palette-tokens.ts` is already "**one function**, because the artboard's paint controls, the chart paint rows and the inspector's material fields each offered the same document tokens and each was its own place a label could print as an id (`vg-104`, RULED 2026-10-12)". So this repo has already ruled that the document's token list gets one owner, and that file's doc states the membership difference is deliberately the caller's `keep` — "the artboard offers every token, the inspector hides `none`". Every site above is therefore consistent with the ruling and none of them is the defect; what is new is that Task 12.4c added a second enumeration with a second home rather than a caller of the first. TWO SHAPES DIFFER AND THAT IS THE DECISION: `paletteTokenOptions` returns `palette.<id>` references with the author's name for each (`PaletteTokenOption`), while the new `paletteTokenIds` returns bare ids — the two readers of the new one are the bridge's snapshot (a count) and `PaintList` (rows keyed by bare id), so neither wants the names or the `palette.` prefix. A single owner would have to export both shapes, or the ids form would have to be the base the options form is built on. WHY A ROW AND NOT AN ON-THE-FLY FIX, on the second clause of the test rather than the first: the cause is named to symbol, but **where the exclusion lives is a design decision that is not already specified** — whether `renderer-core`'s theme module should own "`none` is reserved" as a named export (that package's `fabric-envelope-validate.ts` already treats `palette["none"]` as special, and `src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/theme/` is on `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs`'s mechanism-boundary watchlist, so a write there needs a note at `docs/decisions/` first), or whether `vg-104`'s ruling stands and the membership stays caller-supplied with the new module rewritten as a caller. **It also spans two packages**, and the fix touches `card-token-mapping.ts` and `new-object-defaults.ts`, neither of which Task 12.4c owns. NEAR ROWS: none found in either register — the live file holds no row matching `paletteTokenIds`, `surfacePalette`, `paletteRoleMatch` or "reserved none", and `vg-104` is archived `verified`, being the ruling this row tests the new module against rather than a duplicate of it. NOT VERIFIED: whether the five predicates are semantically identical in every case — `paletteTokenUsage` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/palette-manager/index.ts` deliberately iterates **all** ids including `none`, and `paint-list.tsx`'s delete chooser filters on `id !== selected` rather than on `none`, so a unification has to say which of those two are the same rule and which are different ones. That is part of the decision, not an obstacle to it.

title: Three panes the rail renders are drawn nowhere in the checked set, so Plan 4's panes have no acceptance instrument
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by the controller while closing Task 12.4c (`vg-269`), which the row's ruling had told to extend the drawing for "the three panes it does not show". The task drew the Add pane's new count and **deferred the three pane drawings to their own task rather than drawing them thinly**, and this row is that deferral made visible — an unregistered deferred half is work the drain's own arithmetic cannot see. THE MEASUREMENT, taken on the tree rather than read from a report: `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html` draws the rail with its four slots and **only the Add pane's column** — the words "Composition", "Tokens" and "Document" each occur **zero** times in the file — so there is no drawing of those three panes to add anything to. `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md` already records the gap in its own words: "**Plan 4's panes are drawn only where `shell.html` shows the Add one** — Composition, Tokens and Document appear in no drawing, so `pane-composition`, `pane-tokens` and `pane-document` sit in this directory beside no drawing." So three captured surfaces are outside the acceptance instrument, whose item requires that a surface be drawn for the drawing to measure it. WHY IT IS A TASK AND NOT A THREE-FILE EDIT, which is what makes it worth a row rather than a note: `docs/design/mockups/README.md` states the current set as "those **six** files" with a table of exactly six, and `tests/e2e/design-language.spec.ts` reads "every literal **every drawing in `docs/design/mockups/current/`** declares" — so adding three drawings obliges an edit to that README's own count and its table, and puts three new literal sets under the instrument's rules, where a drawing that is thin or that devises its own treatment is a red gate rather than a missing one. The README's own refresh rule is "**the current files are refreshed when the set of surfaces changes** — a pane, a tab, a section or a rail slot that appears or disappears is drawn, in the original's treatment, never in a treatment of the product's devising", which is the rule that would govern the work. WHY NOT FIXED WHILE 12.4c WAS OPEN: the brief for that task permitted the split explicitly ("a split is better than three thin drawings and a rushed product change"), the panes are an existing gap rather than one this task created — nothing appeared or disappeared in it — and drawing three surfaces in the original's treatment is design work, not a count fix. WHY NOT A DECISION EITHER, on the controller's own reckoning: STATUS.md carries the same gap as "a three-way choice (draw them, narrow the item, carry the residue) rather than a gap" for the sixteenth acceptance item, so the choice is between drawing them, narrowing the item that requires a drawing per surface, and carrying the residue — and **which of the three is a ruling rather than a task**. That is why this row does not name a fix. NEAR ROWS: `vg-324` is the nearest — it is the same shape one surface over ("No drawing in the checked set draws the `?` shortcut sheet"), and if that row is worked first the answer it settles for the shortcut sheet is the answer this one needs; `vg-402` owns re-shooting the captures beside the drawings, which is the image half and not the drawing half; `vg-390` owns whether a capture the register attaches to a later parity plan counts for the plan whose surfaces it shows. None of the three is this row. NOT VERIFIED: whether Plan 4's own parity report names these panes as differences it could not dispose of — that report is not in the tree, so whether the three panes are "undrawn and therefore unmeasured" or "measured and disposed some other way" was not established, and the row states only what the drawings and the screenshots README say.

title: A gesture inside a group snaps to nothing, because both snapping paths refuse a group child for its plane
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.4d (`vg-123`) as an unfixed by-product of its own work, and carried in that commit as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer; materialised here by the controller. THE FINDING: a drag or a resize of an object **inside a group** reaches no snap candidate at all, on either path, and the cause is the plane each path assumes rather than the candidate set. **Measured by Task 12.4d, which was trying to make a part-inside-a-card resize the assertion its ruling named and could not.** (1) THE SCALE PATH refuses before any candidate is read: `isSupportedScaleTarget` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/snap-manager/scaling/scale-snapping-controller.ts` returns false when `target.group !== undefined || target.parent !== undefined`, so `beginGesture` never starts a session. Proved **load-bearing rather than over-broad** by relaxing the guard on the unmodified tree: the gesture then ran and wrote canvas-plane geometry into the child's group plane, landing the part at `1646.72` instead of ~`958`. (2) THE MOVEMENT PATH refuses every step: `assertRawIntentMatchesBaseline` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/snap-manager/movement-snapping-resolver.ts` requires `intent.bounds` to be `baseline.bounds` translated by `intent.position - baseline.position`, and a group child's `position` is group-plane while its `bounds` are canvas-plane — so it throws `Movement raw intent must be a translation of the gesture baseline` at every step, the throw is swallowed by the guard in `createSnapManager`, and the drag lands raw. **The candidate set is nevertheless correct, which is what isolates this from `vg-123`:** a probe of the built bundle read the sources at gesture start during a part drag as `["right-card@700","right-card-part@960","mover@300","loose-source@900"]` plus the artboard, so the part beside the dragged one **is** offered and the drag still does not snap. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR A RULING ALREADY MADE: `vg-123`'s ruling asked that its instrument — a resize of a part inside a card — become the assertion the work is fixed against, and that clause **cannot be met while this stands**; that task delivered the widening, left the instrument a recording, and proved the row's own title through a dragged card instead. So this row is the residue of a ruled clause, not only a new bug. WHY A ROW AND NOT AN ON-THE-FLY FIX, on the test's third clause rather than its first: the cause is named to symbol, but **the fix needs a design decision this task could not take** — which ancestor transforms are safe to write a movement or scale plan through — and the scale half is not small: `sendPointToPlane` is **not exported from `fabric/es`**, so converting a plan's anchor into the group plane means hand-rolled matrix work rather than the one-line conversion it looks like. It also spans two controllers and the resolver, none of which `vg-123` owned. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a decision on the plane question, then a plan written through the ancestor transform, with the part-inside-a-card resize finally snapping **and drawing its guide** — at which point `snapping.spec.ts`'s nested instrument can become the assertion its own comment says it is waiting to be. NEAR ROWS: none found — the live register holds no row naming `isSupportedScaleTarget`, `assertRawIntentMatchesBaseline` or the snapping plane question, and `vg-123` is the row whose ruling this blocks rather than a duplicate of it. NOT VERIFIED: the arithmetic of the two probe readings above (`1646.72`, and the candidate list) is the implementer's own; the controller verified only that both refusing symbols exist and read as described.

CORRECTED 2026-10-15 BY TASK 12.4d'S FIX ROUND (commit `7d3b3afa`, the review's F4 and F3). TWO CORRECTIONS, AND THE FIRST IS A WORD THIS ROW OVERSTATED. **(1) The scale guard is load-bearing, and this row claimed more than its evidence showed.** The relaxed-guard reading (`1646.72` instead of ~`958`) shows the current projection is computed in the canvas plane; it does **not** show the guard is not over-broad, because the guard also refuses a group child under an **identity** transform — which is exactly the case the ruling's instrument needs. So "load-bearing rather than over-broad" is wrong as written and reads as *load-bearing* alone. **(2) The movement path's throw is real, and its cause is not the plane story this row gave.** Measured on screen by dragging `left-card-part` in the nested fixture with the console attached: the drag throws `Movement raw intent must be a translation of the gesture baseline` **11 times across 12 pointer steps**, the throw is swallowed, and the part lands raw (`893.33` against an aim of `955.01`) drawing no guide — so the refusal is confirmed rather than inferred. **The real cause is that Fabric re-fits the group around the child being dragged:** read from the live canvas, the child's own `left` moves `-90.5` while its world box moves `+533.33`, and the card's own box collapses from 400×200 onto the part (`{893.33, 440, 61, 81}` mid-drag). `assertRawIntentMatchesBaseline` requires the world box to be the baseline translated by the change in the object's own `left`/`top`, and those can never agree while the group is re-fitting. **An identity group is not enough** — the group in that fixture is `scaleX` 1, `angle` 0 — which is the half of the earlier arithmetic that was wrong. So the consequence for `vg-123` is unchanged (a gesture inside a group still reaches no candidate), but anyone taking this row should price the group re-fit rather than a plane conversion, and should expect the fix to be about **when** the group re-fits rather than about converting an anchor between planes. NEAR ROWS: `vg-526` is the dedupe's own gap, found in the same round and about a different mechanism.

title: The compact layout's layer panel is 280px where the wide layout's is 246px, so the bound column gets more room in a narrow window than in a wide one
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.4e (`vg-274`) while converting `editor-shell.css`, and carried in that commit as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer; materialised here by the controller. THE FACT, verified on the tree rather than read from the trailer: the wide layout's grid gives the layer panel DESIGN.md §7.3's 246px (`grid-template-columns: 46px 246px minmax(0, 1fr) 276px`), while the compact media query gives the same panel `var(--compact-layer-panel-width)`, declared `280px` — so below the breakpoint the panel is 34px WIDER than it is above it, and the bound column inside the row therefore has more room in a narrow window than in a wide one. THE TRAILER'S OWN QUOTED EVIDENCE IS SUPERSEDED AND MUST NOT BE SEARCHED FOR: it says "the sentence beside it justifies 280 against 'the wide layout's 360px', which no longer exists" — that was the pre-commit text, and **this commit corrected it**, `/* 280px rather than the wide layout's 360px` becoming `/* 280px rather than the wide layout's 246px`. No 360px sentence remains beside the 280px, so a session looking for one finds nothing; the 360px references that do survive in the file are about the pane's own superseded width elsewhere (§7.3 re-cut it to 246px) and are current there. WHAT IS ACTUALLY STALE IS THE REASON, WHICH THE COMMIT LEFT STANDING: the comment's justification is "because the stage is sharing a narrow window with it. The bound column is what gives way first." That reason was written when the wide pane was 360px, and the trade it describes — a narrower stage bought for a wider bound column — now reads as the bound column having given way LESS in the narrow layout than in the wide one, which is the opposite of what the sentence says the compact layout is for. WHY A ROW AND NOT AN ON-THE-FLY FIX: which width the compact pane should take is a design decision, not a defect with a named correct behaviour — DESIGN.md §7.3 states "width 246px by default" with no compact exception, and the panel-inside-the-panel arithmetic the comment refers to (the sub-columns re-cut for 246px) has no recorded compact variant either. The change is one value plus one sentence; the answer is not in any doc. WHY IT IS NOT `vg-274`'S RESIDUE: `vg-274` ruled the file joins the ratchet and its values convert, which is done; this row is about whether the compact layout's value should be the wide layout's, which the conversion deliberately did not decide (the trailer's own words: the value is converted literally as a token and reported rather than changed). NEAR ROWS: `vg-316` and `vg-325` own values in this same file but neither owns a width; `vg-440` is the drawings' own stale furniture. NOT VERIFIED: the visual consequence below the breakpoint — whether a 280px panel in a narrow window actually costs the stage more than it buys the bound column — which needs a browser read at a compact viewport rather than a reading of the grid.

title: host-player's reconnect case finds no connection strip to assert, in the ordered suite and alone on the real host
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by the controller's serial browser pass at Phase 14's close (`npx playwright test --workers=1` over a bundle built in the runbook's order: 301 passed / 4 failed / 226 skipped, exit 1). **Three of the four reds are rows the register already owns** — `vg-431` (`glass-lifecycle.spec.ts:25`, named verbatim), `vg-258` (the display cluster's phone assertions) and `vg-212` (publish-loop's ordered-suite red) — and **this one is named by no row, which is what makes it the pass's finding rather than an expected red.** `[desktop-host] tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts:1280`, "a display fed by the real host › reconnects after the stream fails, and the reading resumes", fails at `:1307` on `await expect(page.locator("#vigilia-connection")).toHaveText(/reconnect|connect/i)` with **"Error: element(s) not found" inside a 5000 ms timeout** — the strip never appears, so the case never reaches its text assertion. **Reproduced in isolation** (`--project=desktop-host -g "reconnects after the stream fails" --workers=1`: 1 failed, exit 1), so this is not the ordered suite's load. **Not this wave's change:** neither `tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts` nor `packages/player/src/chrome.ts`, which owns the strip at `:180`, was touched by Phase 13 or Phase 14 — the newest commit on either is from an earlier wave. **CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED, and two candidates are open rather than one:** the strip is conditional (the same `chrome.ts` calls `removeStrip` for it, and a dozen cases in this same spec assert `toHaveCount(0)`), so either a failed stream no longer drives the player into the state that draws it, or the real host never fails the stream on this machine. **The environment is a live candidate, not a dismissed one** — `vg-143` records this same spec file's units case timing out on the real host in isolation too. NOT FIXED HERE: the cause is not established and the fix needs the host's own behaviour read rather than a locator moved, so it is filed rather than guessed at.

title: repeatsEnclosingBounds' epsilon can only match a child that adds no stroke, so a stroke-carrying part still offers a duplicate of its group's centre line
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.4d's fix round R1 (`vg-123`) as an unfixed by-product of its own work, and carried in commit `7d3b3afa` as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer; materialised here by the controller. THE GAP: the dedupe that `vg-123`'s widening added — `repeatsEnclosingBounds` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/snap-manager/index.ts` — compares a part's box with the nearest enclosing box already offered on all four edges at `SNAP_SOURCE_BOUNDS_EPSILON = 1e-9`. **Measured by R1 with `util.enlivenObjects` on the very JSON the specs author, and the result is that the dedupe fires on almost no real shape:** on `snapping.spec.ts`'s own `source("group", …)` the group box is 80×80 at (100,200) and the child's is 81×81 — the child's `getBoundingRect()` includes its own stroke — so the boxes differ by a stroke, the epsilon cannot absorb it, and the part **is** offered. The same holds for the nested fixture's card (group 400×200, part 61×81) and the starter's card (`cardGroup`, 360×200 against a panel 362×202). It fires only where a child adds no stroke and the group is fitted to it or declares its box: `new Group([rect])` yields the child's own 81×81, which is the path the unit case `offers a part repeating its group's own box once, as the group` exercises — so the dedupe is not dead, it is narrower than the hazard it was written for. WHY THAT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDINESS: `vg-123`'s report gave the dedupe the job of preventing "two candidates at one coordinate with different identities", the shape a count cannot see. **On a stroke-carrying part that hazard is still open** — the part duplicates its group's centre line and offers that group's edges shifted by a stroke — so the widening ships with a dedupe that does not dedupe the cases the fixtures actually contain. WHY A ROW AND NOT AN ON-THE-FLY FIX: widening the epsilon to absorb a stroke is a behaviour change and a design decision (how much of a stroke counts as the same box, and whether a shifted edge is the same edge), which R1 named rather than took; the code is unchanged and the scope is written into `snap-manager/index.ts` beside the function. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a decision on whether the dedupe compares declared boxes, stroke-inclusive boxes, or centres, then the comparison changed to match and a unit case on a stroke-carrying part that asserts the group's line is offered **once**. NEAR ROWS: `vg-123` (the widening this dedupe belongs to, whose own title is about a card snapping into a neighbouring card and which is unaffected), and `vg-524` (the two snapping refusals, whose movement half R1 re-measured in the same round — a different mechanism, filed separately). NOT VERIFIED: the report's own claim that the dedupe's *narrow* job is safe — that a fitted single-part group's part may be dropped without losing a line the group does not already offer — is R1's probe, not the controller's; the controller verified only that the epsilon and the function exist and read as described.

CORRECTED 2026-10-15, FROM ITS OWN INDEPENDENT REVIEW. **The duplicate is not one shape but three, and the row's sentence describes only the first.** The review measured each authored shape rather than the spec's own JSON alone: on `source("group", …)` — the shape this row quoted — the child sits at local 0, so a stroke-carrying child duplicates the group's **centre line** exactly. On the starter's cards (`cardGroup`) the child fills the card, so the exact duplicate is the **shared left/top edge** and the centres sit half a stroke apart. On the nested fixture's card (`openNestedFixture`) the group and the part share **no coordinate at all**. So the hazard is real and shape-dependent, and a fix must be written against the shapes rather than against the one this row named. **Two wording defects the review also found are corrected here:** the commit is `7d3b3afa` (this row and `vg-524` both said `7d3bafa`, which resolves to nothing — a sha that does not resolve is the one defect a reader cannot work around), and `snap-manager/index.ts`'s new note says the dedupe "fires only on a child that adds no stroke", which the case it cites contradicts: `new Group([sole])` has `strokeWidth` 1 and both boxes measure 81×81, so it fires. What is true is that it fires when the **enclosing box equals the child's**, which a fitted group satisfies whether or not the child carries a stroke.

title: A package saved while a group is entered stores a dimmed thumbnail
detail:
FOUND BY the Task 12.4f implementer (agent), 2026-10-15, carried as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `1436df49`.

WHAT: `captureCanvas` renders the live canvas, and `vg-023` makes the live canvas a dimmed one while a group is entered — so a theme package saved from inside a group stores a thumbnail with everything outside the entered group at `0.45`. WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX AND WAS NOT TAKEN: whether a capture should lift a view state at all is a decision the register does not have yet, and the two defensible answers differ for reasons rather than taste — a thumbnail that lifts the dim shows the document as it would be shared, while one that keeps it shows what the author actually saw. It is the same class as the row above it: a view state reaching an artifact that outlives the session. NOT YET MEASURED: whether the thumbnail is regenerated on exit rather than only on save, which decides whether this is visible at all in the common path; the implementer established that the capture reads the live canvas, not that a stored thumbnail ever differs from a post-exit one. SETTLED BY: a ruling on whether capture is a read of the document or a read of the screen.

RULED 2026-10-15: **A CAPTURE READS THE DOCUMENT, NOT THE SCREEN.** A capture lifts a view state, so a thumbnail shows the document as it would be shared and the dim never reaches a saved artifact. This settles the question the row defers, and it is the same principle the row above it rests on: a view state must not reach something that outlives the session.

title: A DESIGN.md marker outside CITE_NUMBERS escapes every citation rule, so §7.9 is unchecked in both directions
detail:
FOUND BY the Task 12.4f implementer (agent), 2026-10-15, reported to the controller rather than fixed.

FOUND WHILE adding `DESIGN.md`'s `§7.9` for `vg-023`, and reported to the controller rather than fixed because the fix is a decision and the path is watched. WHAT: `scripts/design-md.mjs`'s `CITE_NUMBERS` stops at `"7.8"` and calls itself "the single source of truth for what a citation may resolve against". A marker outside that list is invisible to all three citation rules at once, which the code shows rather than the prose: the loop that requires every canonical number to carry a marker iterates `CITE_NUMBERS`, so `§7.9` is not required to have one; the loop that requires every marker to be claimed by a citation skips any number where `!known.has(number)`, and `§7.9` is exactly that, so it is never required to be cited either; and `UNCITED_OK` cannot record it, because that list exists to name markers the rules *would* have caught. Only the placement check still sees it, because that one walks the markers rather than the range — which is why `design:check` was red until the mapping row landed, and why the marker now passes while being uncheckable in both directions. FAILURE SHAPE: a future `§7.9` that nothing cites, or a `§7.9` marker deleted from DESIGN.md, both read green. The gap is the inverse of `vg-352`, which is about a marker being *over*-claimed by another document's numbering; this is a marker nothing can claim. NOT A MECHANICAL FIX, which is why it is a row: extending the range obliges a `§7.9` citation somewhere in `docs/`, `src/` or `scripts/` (a comment in `grouping-manager` is the natural home, beside the constant that implements the section), and `scripts/` is on `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs`'s watchlist — the self-test refuses a note-less edit to `scripts/anything.mjs` — so the edit carries a decision note under `docs/decisions/`. It also raises the question the migration spec owns: whether the range is edited per new §7.N or whether the subdivision should be declared as open-ended, since §7 is the only section this project keeps extending.

RULED 2026-10-15: **THE CANONICAL RANGE IS EXTENDED PER SUBDIVISION, and stays a stated list.** `"7.9"` joins `CITE_NUMBERS` and a `§7.9` citation is written in source, so the marker is required to exist *and* required to be claimed. The range does **not** become a `§7.N` predicate: the spec's declared `§7.1–§7.8` is a claim someone made, and a predicate would make it derived rather than stated. The cost is taken knowingly — each new `§7.N` obliges a `CITE_NUMBERS` edit, a citation, and a decision note under `docs/decisions/`, because `scripts/` is on `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs`'s watchlist.

title: backlog-check never tests whether a path inside a check still exists, so a verified row can cite a deleted file and stay green
detail:
FOUND WHILE applying §8.11's path corrections (agent, 2026-10-16).

WHAT: `scripts/backlog-check.mjs` enforces two things about a `verified` row's `check` — that it names a word from the row's own title, and that the row's `artefacts` resolve to commits that are ancestors of HEAD — and it does not test the third: whether a path the `check` names still exists. `vg-155`'s `check` named `file-section.ts` and `file-section.dom.test.ts` while the files are `panes/add/file-section.tsx` and `panes/add/file-section.dom.test.tsx`, and the 528-item checker stayed green the whole time. WHY IT MATTERS: the `check` is the row's proof of close, and the rule that a check must name a word from its title is deliberately lexical, so a check whose subject moved satisfies it by naming the same *word* at a path that no longer exists. The sha half cannot cover it — `artefacts` proves the commit is real and on the mainline, which is a different question from whether the file the check names is still there.

NOT A MECHANICAL FIX, which is why this is a row rather than an edit: a naive rule ('every path-shaped token in `check` must resolve') would red on legitimate checks, because some of them cite ledger files under `.superpowers/sdd/`, which is gitignored and so absent from `git ls-files` — `vg-328`'s check cites `adjudication.md` and `task-2-report.md` that exist on disk and in no tracked tree. So the decision is what counts as a check's path, and whether an untracked path is permitted, tolerated with a warning, or refused. A second decision follows: whether a `check` may cite a bare basename, which `vg-109` does (`index.dom.test.ts:1501`, unambiguous only because the row's `owner` names the directory).

DISCOVERED, NOT FIXED, in the §8.11 commit: filed rather than fixed because the fix needs that design decision, not because it is hard.

title: The settings-pane spec's section 5 counts the dialog host's consumers as six besides Settings, omits shortcut-reference.tsx and counts a test file and a CSS block among the surfaces
detail:
FOUND WHILE committing the parked-row representation (agent, 2026-10-16) — not the task being done.

WHAT: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-settings-pane-design.md` section 5 argues the modal host stays because `.editor-shell-dialog` is "consumed by six surfaces besides Settings", and enumerates them as `draft-recovery-prompt.tsx`, `new-document-chooser.tsx`, `persistence-manager/replace-document-prompt.tsx`, `theme-library-dialog.tsx`, "plus the host's own rules and `editor-shell.control-rules.test.ts`". Measured at source, `components/ui/dialog.tsx` is imported by exactly six modules — those four, plus `settings.tsx` and `shortcut-reference.tsx` — so the count **besides** Settings is five. The enumeration both **omits `shortcut-reference.tsx`**, a real consumer and the `?` sheet, and **counts two non-surfaces**: a CSS block in `editor-shell.css` and a Vitest file. One sentence later the same section says "the host and the five other consumers are untouched", so the spec disagrees with itself.

WHY IT MATTERS, and it is not a nit: section 5's whole job is to bound the change, and its list is what an implementer reads to decide whose settings-only CSS is dead in `vg-274`'s gated file and which dialogs need a look. An enumeration that drops a consumer and pads with a test file is the instrument being wrong about its own subject.

WHAT THE FIX IS: restate section 5 on one counting basis — the six modules that import `components/ui/dialog.tsx`, five of them besides Settings, naming `shortcut-reference.tsx` — and stop counting the host's own CSS rules and a test file as surfaces. Not fixed here because it is outside the parked-representation task and no test reads a spec's prose, so there is no regression test to leave behind; the spec is also awaiting the user's review, which is the natural moment to correct it.

title: packages/player/src/main.dom.test.ts's post-mount rejection case blows vitest's 20 second timeout inside the full suite while passing in 4.27 seconds alone
detail:
FOUND WHILE running the full gate on 2026-10-16, at `8eaecf0b` (agent, 2026-10-16) — not the task being done, which touched only `scripts/backlog-check.mjs`, two decision notes, `STATUS.md` and the two registers.

WHAT: `npm run gate` exit 1, the whole of the failure being one case — `packages/player/src/main.dom.test.ts > a rejection that arrives after the scene mounted > replaces the display that was already drawn` — reported as `Error: Test timed out in 20000ms`. The run's own numbers: `Test Files 1 failed | 257 passed (258)`, `Tests 1 failed | 3440 passed (3441)`, duration 111.61s, with vitest noting **258 workers spawned at ~3.75s startup each**.

TWO SAMPLES, SO THIS IS NOT A SINGLE READING: the same file run alone passes in **4.27s** (`npx vitest run packages/player/src/main.dom.test.ts`, exit 0), and a second full `npm run test` at the same commit passes **258/258 files and 3441/3441 tests**, exit 0, in **84.03s**. So the case is intermittent under load rather than broken, and the difference between the two full runs is 27 seconds of wall clock — the box was carrying other work in the first.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN CALLED FLAKE: the case is not old. It is the close of `vg-190` (artefacts `e08677f3`, `eb59248b`), landed in Phase 12.4, and it drives the real `main.ts` through a post-mount rejection with no module mocked — only `window.fetch` and `EventSource`. A jsdom case that costs 4.27s on an idle box is already close to a 20s ceiling, so the margin is what is thin, not the assertion. Three ways out and no way to choose between them without a decision: raise this file's `testTimeout`, make the case cheaper, or accept that the gate is load-sensitive and say so where a later session reads it. That is the design decision this row is.

RELATED, and deliberately not merged into this row: `vg-175` is the same shape in `themes/store.test.ts` (20359ms inside the full suite), `vg-285` is the same shape for the browser suite at its default worker count, and `vg-147` is the same shape against Playwright's 30s default. Four rows of one shape may want one ruling rather than four.
